Therefore, the captivating quality of <s>upamā</s> is obtained precisely by its being an <s>alaṅkāra</s>. Hence 'captivating' is a reiteration, being an already established meaning. And the relation of <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> does not arise when the similarity is exceedingly close, as in 'this cow is [like] a cow.' Therefore it is said: 'of two words whose grounds of application are mutually distinct.' Here, 'time and the like' refer to the grounds of application (<s>pravṛttinimitta</s>) of words. For some words operating in their own meaning, time is the ground of application, as for <s>vasanta</s> (spring) and the like. For some, direction — as for <s>prācya</s> (eastern) and the like. For some, class (<s>jāti</s>) — as for <s>go</s> (cow) and the like. For <s>śukla</s> (white) and the like, [the ground is] quality (<s>guṇa</s>). For <s>gacchati</s> (goes) and the like, action (<s>kriyā</s>). For <s>rājapuruṣa</s> (king's man) and the like, a relation such as owner-and-owned. Other cases too should be inferred similarly. 'Mutually distinct grounds of application such as time and the like' — of two words whose grounds of application are mutually distinct, such words being the designators of the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> respectively — this is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound) containing another <s>bahuvrīhi</s>. But in the statement 'this cow is a cow,' there is no difference in the ground of application, since <s>gotva</s> (cow-ness) alone is the single ground of application. Therefore, such a relation of <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> does not arise. The word <s>tu</s> in '<s>upamā tu tat</s>' serves to distinguish [<s>upamā</s>] from other <s>alaṅkāras</s>. The meaning is: <s>upamā</s> is precisely of this kind.

children.text:
eṣā copamā dvidhā, pūrṇā luptā ca /
pūrṇā yatra catuṣṭayamupādīyate upamānamupameyaṃ tayośca sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ saundaryādirūpamānopameyabhāvasya dyotaka ivādiḥ /
sāca pūrṇā trividhā, vākyasamāsataddhitāvaseyatvāt /
tatra vākyāvaseyāyāḥ śrautatvārthatvabhedena dvaividhyam /
avyayāvaseyā śrautī /
avyayaṃ hi luptavibhaktikatvena upamānopameyayorekataratrāpyaviśrāntatvādubhayorapyupamānopameyayorupamitikriyāviṣayatayā yathāyogaṃ karmakaraṇabhāvātmakaṃ saṃbandhamavadyotayati /
atastatra śrautī upamā /
taduktam-----
'yathevaśabdayogena śrutyānvayamarhati'
children.translated_text: And this <s>upamā</s> is of two kinds: <s>pūrṇā</s> (full) and <s>luptā</s> (elliptical). <s>Pūrṇā</s> is where the four [elements] are present: the <s>upamāna</s> (standard), the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison), the common property (<s>sādhāraṇa dharma</s>) such as beauty and the like, and the indicator of the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation such as <s>iva</s> (like). And this full [simile] is of three kinds, being apprehended through sentence, compound, or secondary suffix (<s>taddhita</s>). Therein, the one apprehended through a sentence is twofold, by the distinction of being denotative (<s>śrauta</s>) and implied (<s>ārtha</s>). That which is apprehended through an indeclinable is <s>śrautī</s> (denotative). For an indeclinable, since it has dropped case-endings and thus does not rest in either the <s>upamāna</s> or <s>upameya</s> alone, illuminates the relation — in the form of object, instrument, or agent, as appropriate — with both the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> as the domain of the action of comparing, by following both. Therefore, the <s>upamā</s> there is <s>śrautī</s>. This was stated: 'Through the use of words like <s>yathā</s> and <s>iva</s>, it is entitled to denotative connection.'

children.text:
iti /
yathevaśabdau cātropalakṣaṇam /
avyayāntarādapi vāśabdādeḥ tena rūpeṇa upamānopameyabhāvasyāvagateḥ /
children.translated_text: And here the words <s>yathā</s> and <s>iva</s> are illustrative [of the class]. The <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation can be understood even from other indeclinables such as <s>vā</s> and the like, in that same manner.
For example:

children.text: tāṃ jānīyāḥ parimitakathāṃ jīvitaṃ me dvitīyaṃ
children.translated_text: You should know her, of measured speech, as my second life,
alone like a female <s>cakravāka</s> bird when I, her companion, am far away,
intensely longing as the heavy days pass, the young woman —
I think [she has become] like a lotus-pond crushed by winter, or of another form altogether.
An example of that [simile] with the word <s>yathā</s>:
For the rekindling of the fever of love and then for the increase of torment,
the moonlight became for those separated [lovers] like sandalwood paste. [UKss 1.*18]

children.text:
atra cāndrī candrikā upameyā /
candanamupamānam /
kāmajvarotthitihetutvaṃ saṃtāpavṛddhinibandhanatvaṃ cānavasthitaṃ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ /
yathāśabdaścāvyayatvena luptavibhaktikatvādupamānopameyayorekatarasminnarthe viśrāntaḥ śrautena rūpeṇobhayādhāramupamānopameyabhāvamavadyotayati /
teneyaṃ saṃpūrṇā śrautī ca /
evamivaśabdayoge 'pyudāharaṇaṃ yojyam /
children.translated_text: Here the moonlight is the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison). Sandalwood paste is the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison). Being the cause of rekindling the fever of love and being the occasion for the increase of torment — which are not permanently fixed — are the common property. And the word <s>yathā</s>, being an indeclinable and thus having dropped case-endings, does not rest in the meaning of either the <s>upamāna</s> or the <s>upameya</s> alone, but illuminates the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation based on both, through its denotative form. Therefore this [simile] is both full (<s>saṃpūrṇā</s>) and denotative (<s>śrautī</s>). An example with the word <s>iva</s> should be constructed in the same way.
With eyes like blue lotuses, with faces like lotuses, the beauties of the lake

children.text: taruṇya iva bhānti sma cakravākaiḥ stanairiva // UKss_1.*19 //
children.translated_text: shone with <s>cakravākas</s> like breasts. [UKss 1.*19]
Thus this full (<s>saṃpūrṇā</s>) simile expressed through a sentence, indicated by an indeclinable, is <s>śrautī</s> (denotative).

children.text:
yā tūpamā sadṛśādibhiḥ padaiḥ śliṣṭā tasyāṃ na śrautena rūpeṇa ubhayānuyāyitayā upamānopameyabhāvo 'vagamyate /
api tvarthāt /
sadṛśādīnāṃ padānāmupamānopameyayorekatraiva viśrānteḥ /
anyatra ca tadgatasādṛśyaparyālocanayā tatsaṃbandhitvāvagateḥ /
tenāsau ārthī /
taduktaṃ 'sadṛśādipadāśleṣādanyathā'iti /
anyatheti /
aśrautena rūpeṇetyarthaḥ /
tasyā udāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: But the <s>upamā</s> which is attached to words like <s>sadṛśa</s> (similar) and the like — in that case, the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation is not understood through the denotative form by way of following both [upamāna and upameya]. Rather, it is [understood] through the meaning. Because words like <s>sadṛśa</s> and the like rest in only one of the two — either the <s>upamāna</s> or the <s>upameya</s>. And the other [member] is understood to be connected with it through the consideration of the similarity belonging to [the first]. Therefore, that [simile] is <s>ārthī</s> (implied). This was stated: 'Otherwise, through the attachment of words like <s>sadṛśa</s> and the like.' 'Otherwise' means: through the non-denotative form. An example of that:
White from blooming at night, with bees resting on the filaments,
the grove of night-lotuses was like the orb of the full moon. [UKss 1.*20]

children.text:
atra kumudakānanaṃ vikasitaṃ kiñjalkālīnaṣaṭpadatvaviśiṣṭamupameyam, pūrṇendubimbamupamānam, dhavalatvaṃ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ /
pratimāśabda upamānopameyabhāvāvagatihetuḥ /
sa ca upamāne viśrāntaḥ /
tathāhi /
pūrṇondubimbaṃ pratimā pratibimbaṃ sadṛśamasyeti bahūvrīhiratra kriyate /
tena pratimāśabda upamāne viśrāntaḥ /
tena copamāne viśrāntenāpi arthādupameyasya sādṛśyamavagamyate /
sādṛśyasyobhayādhiṣṭhānatvāt /
yadāpi ca pūrṇendubimbena pratimamiti tṛtīyātatpuruṣastadāpyupameye khakaṇṭhenābhihitaṃ sādṛśyam /
upamāne ca tasyārthātpratipattiḥ /
ato bahuvrīhau upamānagatasādṛśyaparyālocanayā upameyatvamavagamyate /
tatpuruṣe tu upameyavartisādṛśyavicāreṇa umamānasyopamānatvāvagatirityārtho 'tropamānopameyabhāvaḥ /
atra ca upameyavartikiñjalkālīnaṣaṭpadatvābhidhānasāmarthyādaparamapi sādharmyamanabhihitamasitodaratvalakṣaṇamākṣiptam /
yathā pūrṇendubimbaṃ śaśalāñchanatvādasitodaramevaṃ kumudakānanamapi kiñjalkālīnaṣaṭpadatvāditi /
ato 'sitodaratvalakṣaṇaṃ dharmamapekṣya luptaikadeśatvālluptāpīyamupamā /
'netrairivotpalaiḥ'ityādau tu yadyapi netrotpalādīnāṃ samānadharmā dīrghatvanīlatvādayaḥ svaśabdena nopāttāstathāpi bhāntityabhidhīyamānārthe teṣāmanupraveśātsaṃpūrṇatvamevopamāyāḥ, catuṣṭayopalambhāt /
netrādīni hyatropamānāni /
utpalādīnyupameyāni /
bhānaṃ dīrghatvanīlatvādiviśeṣaṇaparyantaṃ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ /
ivaśabdaśca upamānopameyabhāvāvagatahetuḥ /
teneyamupamāsaṃpūrṇaiva prabodhāddhavalimitīyaṃ tvasitodaratvāpekṣayā luptatvenāpyuktā /
samāsopamā caiṣā pūrṇendubimbapratimamiti samāsasya vihitatvāt /
yadā tvatra vākyopamā vivakṣitā bhavati tadaitadevodāharaṇaṃ tadudāharaṇārthatvena
children.translated_text: Here the grove of night-lotuses, in bloom and qualified by having bees resting on its filaments, is the <s>upameya</s>; the orb of the full moon is the <s>upamāna</s>; whiteness is the common property. The word <s>pratimā</s> (image, likeness) is the cause of understanding the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation. And it rests in the <s>upamāna</s>. For here the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound is formed as: 'that whose image (likeness) is the orb of the full moon.' Thus the word <s>pratimā</s> rests in the <s>upamāna</s>. And even though it rests in the <s>upamāna</s>, the similarity of the <s>upameya</s> is understood through the meaning, since similarity has both [members] as its basis. And even when [the compound is analyzed] as a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> — 'similar to the orb of the full moon' (with the instrumental) — the similarity expressed by the zero-suffix rests in the <s>upameya</s>. And its understanding for the <s>upamāna</s> is through the meaning. Therefore, in the <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, the <s>upameya</s>-status is understood through the consideration of the similarity pertaining to the <s>upamāna</s>; in the <s>tatpuruṣa</s>, the <s>upamāna</s>-status is understood through the consideration of the similarity pertaining to the <s>upameya</s> — thus the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation here is [understood] through the meaning. And here, by the force of expressing the property of 'having bees resting on the filaments' that belongs to the <s>upameya</s>, another unstated common property — characterized by having a dark center — is also suggested. Just as the orb of the full moon has a dark center due to the mark of the hare, so too the grove of night-lotuses has one due to the bees resting on its filaments. Therefore, with respect to the property of having a dark center, this <s>upamā</s> is also <s>luptā</s> (elliptical), since one element is omitted. But in 'with eyes like blue lotuses' and the like, although the common properties of the eyes and blue lotuses — such as length, blueness, and so on — are not expressed by their own words, still, since they are included in the meaning being expressed by '<s>bhānti</s>' (they shine), the <s>upamā</s> is indeed complete, because all four elements are present. For here the eyes and the like are the <s>upamānas</s> (standards). The blue lotuses and the like are the <s>upameyas</s> (objects). The shining, extending to qualifications like length, blueness, and so on, is the common property. And the word <s>iva</s> is the cause of understanding the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation. Therefore this <s>upamā</s> is indeed complete. But 'white from blooming' — this one is also described as <s>luptā</s> (elliptical) with respect to the dark center. And this is also a compound simile (<s>samāsa-upamā</s>), since the compound 'like the orb of the full moon' is employed. But when a sentence-simile is intended here, this very example
should be reformulated as: 'The grove of night-lotuses was like the undivided moon.' [UKss 1.*21]
— in this manner it should be adapted.

children.text: evameṣā saṃpūrṇā vākyāvagamyā dvividhopamā pratīpāditā śrautī ārthī ca /
children.translated_text: Thus this full simile apprehended through a sentence has been demonstrated as twofold — <s>śrautī</s> (denotative) and <s>ārthī</s> (implied).
But the one apprehended through a compound has been described as essentially one kind only, being [always] implied (<s>ārtha</s>).

children.text:
yā tu taddhitāvaseyā saṃpūrṇā tasyā api dvaividhyaṃ śrautatvārthatvabhedena /
tatra tasyevetyanena hi yo vatirvidhīyate tasya ivārthe vidhīyamānatvādivaśabdavacchrautena rūpeṇa ubhayānuyāyitayā
children.translated_text: As for the full [simile] apprehended through a secondary suffix (<s>taddhita</s>), that too is twofold, by the distinction of denotative (<s>śrauta</s>) and implied (<s>ārtha</s>). Therein, the <s>vati</s> suffix that is prescribed in the sense of '<s>tasya iva</s>' (like that of), since it is prescribed in the sense of <s>iva</s>, like the word <s>iva</s> itself, through its denotative form and by following both,

children.text:
upamānopameyabhāvāvagatinibandhanatvam /
yaḥ punastena tulyamiti tulyārtho vatirvidhīyate tato brāhmaṇena tulyamadhīte brāhmaṇavadadhīte kṣatriya ityupameye yattadadhyayanakriyādvāreṇa viśrāntaṃ tulyatvaṃ tatparyālocanayā arthādupamānasyopamānatvamavagamyate /
tenārthastatra upamānopameyabhāvaḥ /
taduktam----
'vatinā ca karmasāmānyavacanena /
ṣaṣṭhīsaptamayantācca yo vatirnāmatastadabhidheye'iti /
karmasāmānyavacano vatiḥ 'tena tulyaṃ kriyā cedvatiḥ'; (pā. a. 5. 1. 115.)
children.translated_text: serves as the basis for understanding the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation. But when the <s>vati</s> suffix is prescribed in the sense of 'equal to,' i.e., '<s>tena tulyam</s>' (equal to that) — then in '<s>brāhmaṇena tulyam adhīte</s>, <s>brāhmaṇavad adhīte kṣatriyaḥ</s>' (the <s>kṣatriya</s> studies like a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>), the equality resting in the <s>upameya</s> through the medium of the action of studying, and the <s>upamāna</s>-status of the <s>upamāna</s> understood from the consideration of that — therefore the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation there is through the meaning. This was stated: 'and by the <s>vati</s> suffix and by a general term for action; and by the <s>vati</s> suffix derived from a noun ending in the sixth or seventh case, to express that [comparison].' The <s>vati</s> suffix that expresses general action [follows the rule] '<s>tena tulyaṃ kriyā ced vatiḥ</s>' (<s>Pāṇini</s> 5.1.115),
since it denotes equality of action.
And by that, the <s>upamā</s> (simile) is expressed.
'Expressible' — what was begun earlier is here connected.
From a noun ending in the sixth or seventh case — from a noun, i.e., from a nominal stem (<s>prātipadika</s>) — this is the connection.
An example of the former:

children.text: api sā sumukhī tiṣṭheddṛṣṭeḥ pathi kathaṃcana /
children.translated_text: Would that beautiful-faced one stand somehow in the path of [my] sight,
having arrived unsought, like rain from a cloudless [sky] that has fallen? [UKss 1.*22]

children.text:
aprārthitopasaṃpannā dṛṣṭeḥ pathi kathaṃcana patitā tiṣṭhediti saṃbandhaḥ /
atrānabhravṛṣṭirūpamānam, sumukhī upameyā /
aprārthitopasaṃpannatve sati dṛṣṭigocarapatitatvenāvasthānaṃ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ /
vatiśca kriyātulyatve vidhīyamāna upameye kriyādvāreṇa śabdena vṛttena viśrāntaḥ saṃstulyatvaparyālocanayopamānasyopamānatvamavagamayati /
tato 'trārthādupamānopameyabhāvaḥ pratīyate /
teneyaṃ saṃpūrṇāṃ ārthīca taddhitāvaseyā /
children.translated_text: The connection is: 'having arrived unsought, fallen somehow in the path of sight, would she stand.' Here, rain from a cloudless sky is the <s>upamāna</s>, the beautiful-faced one is the <s>upameya</s>. The common property is standing in the field of sight having arrived unsought. And the <s>vati</s> suffix, being prescribed for equality of action, rests in the <s>upameya</s> through the medium of the action by means of the word in use, and causes the understanding of the <s>upamāna</s>'s status as <s>upamāna</s> through the consideration of equality. Therefore, the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation here is understood through the meaning. Hence this is both full (<s>saṃpūrṇā</s>) and implied (<s>ārthī</s>), apprehended through a secondary suffix.
An example of the second:
Would the pangs of longing be as unrestrained for her too, as for me,
brought about by the God of Love, who strikes with sudden bursts? [UKss 1.*23]

children.text:
akāṇḍoḍḍāmaro 'navasare udbhaṭaḥ /
pracaṇḍa iti pāṭhāntaram /
utkalikāḥ utkaṇṭhāḥ /
atrāsmadartha upamānam /
tacchabdārtha upameyaḥ /
manmathena samarpitā yāstā nirargalāḥ utkalikāstatkartṛkaṃ bhavanaṃ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ /
vatiścevārthe vidhīyamānatvādivaśabdavadupamānopameyayorekataratrāpyaviśrāntaḥ śrautena rūpeṇopamānopameyabhāvameva dyotayati /
teneyaṃ saṃpūrṇā śrautī ca taddhitāvaseyā /
atra tu tasyā apīti pāṭhe ṣaṣṭhyantādvatarvidheyaḥ /
yadā tu tasyāmapīti pāṭhastadā saptamyantāt /
yaduktam 'upamāne yaḥ saṃśayaḥ sa upameyādyvāvartata'iti /
evameṣā vākyasamāsataddhitāvaseyā saṃpūrṇā trividhopamā pratipāditā /
tatra ca vākyataddhitāvaseyayorupamayoḥ pratyekaṃ śrautatvārthatvabhedena dvaividhyamuktam /
samāsāvaseyāyāstvārthatvameva /
ataḥ pañcaprakāraiṣā saṃpūrṇā /
children.translated_text: [The word] <s>akāṇḍoḍḍāmara</s> means 'untimely' [and] 'bursting forth without occasion.' <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> is an alternative reading. <s>Utkalikāḥ</s> means longings (<s>utkaṇṭhā</s>). Here, 'our' is the object of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>). The referent of 'that' [word] is the object to be compared (<s>upameya</s>). The unrestrained longings dispatched by <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), and the agitation caused by him — this is the common property (<s>sādhāraṇa dharma</s>). And the suffix <s>vat</s>, being prescribed in the sense of 'like' (<s>iva</s>), like the word <s>iva</s>, while not resting on either the <s>upamāna</s> or <s>upameya</s> alone, indicates the relationship of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> through its directly denoted form. Therefore this is a complete (<s>saṃpūrṇā</s>) and directly-denoted (<s>śrautī</s>) simile inferred from the <s>taddhita</s> suffix. But here, in the reading 'of her too,' the <s>vat</s> suffix is to be applied after the genitive case-ending. When, however, the reading is 'in her too,' then [it is applied] after the locative case-ending. As stated: 'the doubt regarding the <s>upamāna</s> is extended also to the <s>upameya</s>.' Thus, this complete simile of three kinds — inferable from sentence (<s>vākya</s>), compound (<s>samāsa</s>), and <s>taddhita</s> suffix — has been demonstrated. And among them, for similes inferable from sentence and from <s>taddhita</s> suffix, a twofold division has been stated, each having the distinction of being directly-denoted (<s>śrauta</s>) and meaning-based (<s>ārtha</s>). For the simile inferable from compound, however, only the meaning-based [type exists]. Therefore, this complete [simile] is of five kinds.

children.text:
yā tu luptaikadeśatvālluptopamā sā saṃkṣepopamā /
tasyāśca pañcavidhatvaṃ vākyāsamāsasubdhātukṛttaddhitāvaseyatvāt /
tatra vākye yā saṃkṣepopamā sā pūrvamudāhṛtā 'akhaṇḍenendunā tulyamiti'; /
atra hyasitodaratvasya anupāttatvātsādhāraṇadharmānupādānālluptaikadeśatvamapi vidyate /
children.translated_text: That which is an elliptical simile (<s>luptopamā</s>) due to having one component omitted is a condensed simile (<s>saṃkṣepopamā</s>). And it is of five kinds, because it can be inferred from sentence, compound, <s>subdhātu</s> (denominative) suffix, <s>kṛt</s> suffix, and <s>taddhita</s> suffix. Among these, the condensed simile occurring in a sentence has already been illustrated: '<s>akhaṇḍenendunā tulyam</s>' (comparable to an undivided moon); for here, since the quality of dark-bellied-ness is not taken up, there is also omission of one component through the non-uptake of the common property.

children.text:
samāsāvaseyā punaḥ saṃkṣepopamā trividhā /
ekadvitrilope bhāvāt /
ekalope dvividhā, sādhāraṇadharmavācina ivādervānupādānāt /
taduktaṃ 'sāmyavācakavicyute'riti /
'tadvāciviraheṇe'ti ca /
sāmyavācakaḥ sādhāraṇadharmavācī /
(sādhāraṇadharmaḥ) saundaryādiḥ /
tadvācī upamānopameyabhāvavācī ca ivādiḥ /
atra ca sarvatra prakaraṇe 'saṃkṣepābhihitāpyeṣā'iti, 'kvacit, samāsa'iti, 'nibadhyata'iti ca trayaṃ pratyekaṃ yathopayogamanuṣajyate /
children.translated_text: The condensed simile inferable from compound is again threefold — because of the possibility of omission of one, two, or three [components]. When one component is omitted, it is twofold — because of either the non-employment of the common property word or [the non-employment] of <s>iva</s> etc. This was stated: 'when the word expressing similarity is absent' and 'when the word denoting that [comparison] is absent.' The 'word expressing similarity' is the word denoting the common property. The common property is beauty and the like. Its denoting word, and <s>iva</s> etc., which denote the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship — here, throughout this entire section, the three phrases 'condensed though expressed,' 'sometimes,' 'in a compound,' and 'is bound' are each connected as appropriate.

children.text: tatra sāmyavāciviyogena samāse yā saṃkṣepopamā tasyāḥ pūrvamevodāharaṇamuktaṃ 'pūrṇendubimbapratimami'ti /
children.translated_text: Among these, the condensed simile in a compound with the absence of the similarity-denoting word has already been illustrated previously: '<s>pūrṇendubimbapratimam</s>' (resembling the orb of the full moon).
For here the quality of dark-bellied-ness, being inferable from the force of meaning, is not taken up explicitly through a word.
But when <s>iva</s> etc. are absent, the illustration of that [simile] is —
At that time, when the [air] was filled with flocks of <s>kādamba</s> birds uttering their cries in the rainy season,
the matted-haired one (<s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>, i.e. <s>Śiva</s>), tiger among the lords of the thirty [gods], with subsequent remorse, [UKss 1.*24]
turned his mind toward her — her whose face was like the glow of the moon, whose eyes were like petals of blue lotuses,

children.text: sarojakarṇikāgaurīṃ gaurīṃ prati mano dadhau // UKss_1.*25 //
children.translated_text: the fair one (<s>Gaurī</s>), golden as the pericarp of a lotus — toward <s>Gaurī</s>. [UKss 1.*25]

children.text:
kādambāḥ pakṣibhedāḥ /
sarojakarṇikāgaurīṃ gaurīmityatra sarojakarṇikā upamānaṃ, gaurī upameyā, gauratvaṃ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ /
taccatrayaṃ svakaṇṭhenopāttam /
ivādyarthastu upamānasya sādhāraṇadharmavācinā saha "upamānāni sāmānyavacanaiḥ" (pā. a. 2 / 1 / 55) iti yaḥ samāsastatsāmarthyadavagamyate /
teneyamivādiśabdalopālluptaikadeśā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kādambāḥ</s> are a particular kind of birds. In '<s>sarojakarṇikāgaurīṃ gaurīm</s>' here, the lotus pericarp (<s>sarojakarṇikā</s>) is the <s>upamāna</s>, <s>Gaurī</s> is the <s>upameya</s>, and the quality of golden hue (<s>gauratva</s>) is the common property. All three of these are taken up explicitly. But the meaning of <s>iva</s> etc. — the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship — is understood through the force of the compound formed according to the rule '<s>upamānāni sāmānyavacanaiḥ</s>' (<s>Pāṇini</s> 2.1.55: 'objects of comparison [compound] with words denoting common properties'). Therefore, this [simile] has one component omitted through the absence of the word <s>iva</s> etc.
Thus, the compound-based simile with one component omitted has been stated as twofold.

children.text:
dvitayalope tvekaprakārā bhavati, sādhāraṇadharmavācina ivādeśca yugapadaprayogāt /
taduktaṃ 'upamānopameyoktau sāmyatadvācivicyavāt'; /
atra
children.translated_text: With the omission of two [components], however, it is of one kind — because of the simultaneous non-employment of both the common-property word and <s>iva</s> etc. This was stated: 'when the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> are expressed, through the absence of the similarity[-word] and its denoting [word].' Here,

children.text:
sāmyaśabdena sāmyavācī śabdo lakṣyate /
sāmyavicyavāccopamāyā asaṃbhavāt /
tasyā udāharaṇaṃ 'tridaśādhīśaśārdūla'iti, nīlotpaladalekṣaṇam'iti ca /
'tridaśādhīśaśārdūlaḥ'ityatra ca tridaśādhiśa upameyaḥ, śārdūla upamānam /
tacca dvayaṃ svakaṇṭhenopāttam /
ivādyarthaḥ sādhāraṇaśca dharmastejasvitvādiḥ sāmarthyādavasīyate /
'nīlotpaladalekṣaṇām'ityatra tu nīlotpalapalāśānāmupamānatvaṃ, īkṣaṇayorupameyatā /
etayośca svakaṇṭheno pādānam /
nīlatvadīrghatvādisādhāraṇo dharma ivādyarthaśca upamānopameyabhāvātmakaḥ svaśabdena anupātto 'pi samāsavaśenārthasāmarthyādavasīyate /
'tridaśādhīśaśārdūla'ityasmāttu 'nīlotpaladalekṣaṇāmi'tyasya bahuvrīhitvakṛto viśeṣaḥ /
tatra hi "upamitaṃ vyāghrādibhiḥ"iti tatpuruṣo vihitaḥ /
evameṣā sādhāraṇadharmavācina ivādeścāprayogāt dvitayalope samāse saṃkṣepopamoktā /
children.translated_text: by the word 'similarity,' the word denoting similarity is indicated — because an <s>upamā</s> without the similarity [itself] is impossible. The illustration of that [simile] is '<s>tridaśādhīśaśārdūla</s>' (tiger among the lords of the thirty [gods]) and '<s>nīlotpaladalekṣaṇam</s>' (eyes like petals of blue lotuses). In '<s>tridaśādhīśaśārdūlaḥ</s>,' the lord of the thirty [gods] is the <s>upameya</s>, the tiger is the <s>upamāna</s>. Both of these are taken up explicitly. The meaning of <s>iva</s> etc. and the common property such as valor and the like are inferred from the force [of the compound]. In '<s>nīlotpaladalekṣaṇām</s>,' the petals of blue lotuses are the <s>upamāna</s>, the eyes are the <s>upameya</s>. Both of these are taken up explicitly. The common property — blueness, length, etc. — and the meaning of <s>iva</s> etc., i.e., the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship, though not taken up explicitly, are inferred from the force of meaning by virtue of the compound. The difference between '<s>tridaśādhīśaśārdūla</s>' and '<s>nīlotpaladalekṣaṇām</s>' is that the latter has the form of a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound. For in the former, a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound is prescribed by the rule '<s>upamitaṃ vyāghrādibhiḥ</s>' (compared with a tiger etc.). Thus, this condensed simile in a compound with the omission of two [components] has been stated — through the non-employment of the common-property word and <s>iva</s> etc.

children.text:
tritayalope tu sādhāraṇadharmavācina upameyābhidhāyina upamānopameyabhāvavācinaśca ivāderyugapadaprayogātsamāsavarttinī saṃkṣepopamā bhavati /
taduktaṃ "sāmyopameyatadvāciviyogācca"iti /
atrāpi pūrvavatsāmyopameyaśabdābhyāṃ tadvācī śabdau lakṣyate /
tasyā udāharaṇaṃ "śaśicchāyavadanāmi"ti /
atra hi śaśicchāyātulyā chāyā yasya tathāvidhaṃ vadanaṃ yasyā iti bahuvrīhigarme bahuvrīhau śaśikāntirupamānaṃ, vadanakāntirūpameyā /
tayośca sādhāraṇo dharma āhlādakatvādistulyatvaṃ ceti catuṣṭayamavagamyate /
śabdaspṛṣṭaṃ tūpamānameva śaśicchāyeti /
taditarasyopameyādestritayasya samāsasāmarthyenārthāvaseyatvāt /
evameṣā tritayalope samāsavartinī saṃkṣepopamā udāhṛtā /
tedavamatra catuḥprakārā luptā samāsopamā pratipāditā /
ekalope dve, dvitayalope ekā, tritayalope caiketi /
children.translated_text: With the omission of three [components], when the common-property word, the word denoting the <s>upameya</s>, and <s>iva</s> etc., which denote the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship, are simultaneously not employed, the condensed simile occurring in a compound arises. This was stated: 'and through the absence of the similarity[-word], the <s>upameya</s>[-word], and the word denoting that [relationship].' Here too, as before, by the words 'similarity' and '<s>upameya</s>,' the words denoting them are indicated. The illustration of that is '<s>śaśicchāyavadanām</s>' (one whose face has the glow of the moon). For here, in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound within a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, the beauty of the moon is the <s>upamāna</s>, and the beauty of the face is the <s>upameya</s>. And of these, the common property — the quality of being delightful and the like — and their equality: these four are understood. But what is explicitly touched by words is the <s>upamāna</s> alone, as '<s>śaśicchāyā</s>' (moon-glow). Since the remaining three — the <s>upameya</s> and the rest — are meaning-based, inferred from the force of the compound. Thus this condensed simile occurring in a compound with the omission of three [components] has been illustrated. Therefore here four kinds of elliptical compound-simile have been demonstrated: two in the omission of one, one in the omission of two, and one in the omission of three.

children.text:
subdhātupratyayāvaseyā punarupamā trividhā kyac kyaṅ kvipū pratyayāvaseyatvāt /
kyacpratyayāvaseyāpi trividhā karmopamānakatvādadhikaraṇopamānakatvācca /
taduktaṃ "tathopamānādācāre kyacpratyayabaloktitaḥ"iti /
yathā samāse saṃkṣepābhihitā upamā samāsasamarthyādavagamyamānā nibadhyate tathā kasmiṃścidviṣaye upamānātkarmaṇaḥ adhikaraṇādvā ācārārthe yathākramaṃ sautra aupasaṃkhyānikaśca yaḥ kyacpratyayastadbalena yāsau bhaṇitistatsāmarthyādapyavasīyamānā nibadhyate /
tasyā udāharaṇaṃ----
children.translated_text: The simile inferable from a <s>subdhātu</s> (denominative) suffix is again threefold — because it can be inferred from the suffixes <s>kyac</s>, <s>kyaṅ</s>, and <s>kvip</s>. The simile inferable from the <s>kyac</s> suffix is also threefold — because the <s>upamāna</s> can serve as the object (<s>karman</s>), or as the locus (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>). This was stated: 'likewise, from the <s>upamāna</s>, in the sense of conduct (<s>ācāra</s>), through the force of the <s>kyac</s> suffix, [simile] is expressed.' Just as a condensed simile expressed in a compound is understood and bound through the force of the compound, similarly, in certain cases, from the <s>upamāna</s> [serving as] object or locus, in the sense of conduct, the <s>kyac</s> suffix — which is respectively a Sūtra-prescribed and supplementary one — the expression through its force, the simile inferred [therefrom], is bound. An illustration of that —
He, though fulfilled by the entirety of sovereignty and prosperity, behaving as if wretched,
experienced the beautiful forest as if it were a hell (<s>narakīyati</s>). [UKss 1.*26]

children.text:
niḥśeṣaiśvaryasaṃpadā kṛtārtho 'pīti saṃbandhaḥ /
atra duḥsthamivātmānamācaranniti duḥsthaḥ kaściddāridṣādyupapluta upamānaṃ, bhagavadātmā upameyaḥ, ācārākhyaḥ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ kyacpratyayopāttaḥ /
atra copamānasādhāraṇadharmayoḥ śabdaspṛṣṭatvaṃ /
upameyasya upamānopameyabhāvasya ca sāmarthyādavagatiḥ /
teneyaṃ dvitayasya gamyamānārthatvāddvitayalope sati subdhātūpamā /
evamiyaṃ karmopamānikā subdhātūpamā udāhṛtā /
children.translated_text: The connection is: 'fulfilled by the entirety of sovereignty and prosperity.' Here, the <s>upamāna</s> is some wretched person afflicted by poverty and the like — [expressed through] '<s>duḥsthīyan</s>' meaning 'conducting himself as if wretched.' The <s>upameya</s> is the Lord himself. The common property is 'conduct' (<s>ācāra</s>), taken up by the <s>kyac</s> suffix. Here the <s>upamāna</s> and the common property are explicitly stated. The <s>upameya</s> and the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship are understood from the force [of the suffix]. Therefore this is a <s>subdhātu</s>-simile with the omission of two [components], since two are of inferred meaning. Thus this object-based (<s>karmopamānikā</s>) <s>subdhātu</s>-simile has been illustrated.

children.text:
adhikaraṇopamānikā tu 'narakīyati kānane'iti /
atra naraka upamānam, kānanamupameyam, kyacpratyayopāttstvācāraḥ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ /
ivādayastu kyacpratyayasāmarthenopamānopameyabhāvasyāvaseyatvādaprayuktāḥ /
teneyaṃ ekalope sati subdhātupamā /
evameṣā kyacpratyayāvagamyā dvividhā saṃkṣepopamokta /
children.translated_text: The locus-based (<s>adhikaraṇopamānikā</s>) one is '<s>narakīyati kānane</s>' (experiences the forest as hell). Here <s>naraka</s> (hell) is the <s>upamāna</s>, the forest (<s>kānana</s>) is the <s>upameya</s>, and the conduct (<s>ācāra</s>) taken up by the <s>kyac</s> suffix is the common property. And <s>iva</s> etc. are not employed because the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship is to be inferred through the force of the <s>kyac</s> suffix. Therefore this is a <s>subdhātu</s>-simile with the omission of one [component]. Thus this condensed simile, to be understood through the <s>kyac</s> suffix, has been stated as twofold.

children.text:
kyaṅpratyayasāmarthyāvagamyā tu kartrapamānikā saṃkṣepopamā bhavati /
tadāha"karturācāre kyaṅā se"ti, "tathe"ti, "upamānādācāra"iti /
kvaciditi ca pūrvoktasyātrānuṣaṅgaḥ /
karturupamānāduttareṃṇācāraviṣayeṇa kyaṅā sā saṃkṣepopamā kvacinnibadhyata ityarthaḥ /
tasyā udāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: The condensed simile to be understood through the force of the <s>kyaṅ</s> suffix is agent-based (<s>kartṛpamānikā</s>). He says: 'of the agent, in the sense of conduct, through <s>kyaṅ</s>, that [simile],' and 'likewise,' and 'from the <s>upamāna</s>, in the sense of conduct.' And 'sometimes' — this is carried over from what was said before. The meaning is: from the <s>upamāna</s> of the agent, with the subsequent [suffix] in the domain of conduct, through <s>kyaṅ</s>, that condensed simile is sometimes bound. An illustration of that —
As that blazing one [i.e. the god of love] gazed at [him], in the absence of his beloved,
the great radiance of [his] knowledge of reality began to behave like a firefly (<s>khadyotāyitum</s>). [UKss 1.*27]

children.text:
khadyoto jyotirmālikā /
atra khadyotāyitumityādau khadyota upamānam /
tattvajñānaṃ padārthakharūpayāthātathyaparicchedaḥ, tadātmakaṃ yattanmahadutkṛṣṭaṃ mahastejastadupameyam /
kyaṅkapratyayopāttaścācāraḥ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ /
kyaṅpratyayasāmarthyāvaseyatvāccātrevāderaprayogaḥ /
teneyamekalopena subdhātūpamopanibaddhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Khadyota</s> is a glow-worm (firefly). Here, in '<s>khadyotāyitum</s>' and the like, the firefly is the <s>upamāna</s>. The knowledge of reality — the discernment of the true nature of things — that great, i.e. supreme, radiance (<s>mahas</s>) of which it consists: that is the <s>upameya</s>. The conduct (<s>ācāra</s>) taken up by the <s>kyaṅ</s> suffix is the common property. And because of being inferable through the force of the <s>kyaṅ</s> suffix, <s>iva</s> etc. are not employed here. Therefore this is a <s>subdhātu</s>-simile bound with the omission of one [component].

children.text:
kvacit viṣaye kartrupamānikā sā saṃkṣepopamā kvipā nibadhyate /
sa ca kvip "sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ kvibvā vaktavyaḥ"ityanena vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: In certain cases, the agent-based condensed simile is bound through <s>kvip</s>. And that <s>kvip</s> is prescribed by the rule: '<s>sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ kvibvā vaktavyaḥ</s>' (the <s>kvip</s> suffix optionally applies after all nominal stems).

children.text:
taduktaṃ "sā kvipā kvacidi"ti /
atrāpi tatheti, upamānādācāra iti, karturiti ca trayamanuṣajyate /
tasyā udāharaṇam----
"kṛśānuvajjagadi'jagadupameyam, ācāraśca sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ kvipsāmarthyadavagamyate /
atra copamānopameyayoḥ śabdopāttatvādivādīnāmācārasya ca arthasāmārthyavaseyatvāttaddvitayalopaḥ /
na khalvaśrūyamāṇasya kvipor'thābhidhāyitā vaktuṃ śakyā /
evameṣā subdhātvavaseyā trividhā saṃkṣepopamā pratipāditā /
kyackyaṅkvipparatyayāvaseyatvāt /
kyacpratyayasāmarthyāvaseyā tu dvividhā /
karmādhikaraṇopamānakatvāt /
kyappratyayāvaseyā tvekaprakārā /
kvippratyayāvaseyāpyekaprakāraiva bhavati /
tadevameṣā caturvidhā subdhātupratyayāvaseyā saṃkṣepopamoktā /
children.translated_text: This was stated: 'that [simile], through <s>kvip</s>, sometimes.' Here too, the three [phrases] 'likewise,' 'from the <s>upamāna</s>, in the sense of conduct,' and 'of the agent' are carried over. An illustration of that: '<s>kṛśānuvajjagat</s>' (the world, like fire) — the world is the <s>upameya</s>, and conduct as common property is understood through the force of <s>kvip</s>. Here, since the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> are explicitly stated, and since the conduct [i.e. the meaning of <s>iva</s>] is inferred from the force of meaning, there is the omission of those two [components]. For one cannot say that the inaudible <s>kvip</s> [suffix] expresses meaning. Thus this threefold condensed simile inferred from <s>subdhātu</s> suffixes has been demonstrated — because of being inferred from the <s>kyac</s>, <s>kyaṅ</s>, and <s>kvip</s> suffixes. That inferred from the <s>kyac</s> suffix is twofold — because the <s>upamāna</s> can serve as object or locus. That inferred from the <s>kyaṅ</s> suffix is of one kind. That inferred from the <s>kvip</s> suffix is also of one kind. Thus this condensed simile inferred from <s>subdhātu</s> suffixes has been stated as fourfold.

children.text:
kṛtpratyayasāmarthyāvaseyā saṃkṣepopamā dvividhā, karmopamānikā kartrupamānikā ca /
taduktaṃ 'upamāne karmaṇi vā kartari vā yo ṇamulkaṣādigatastadvācyā se'ti /
kaṣādigataḥ kaṣādyanuprayogaka ityarthaḥ /
karmopamānikāyāstasyā udāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: The condensed simile inferred from the force of a <s>kṛt</s> suffix is twofold — object-based and agent-based. This was stated: 'when the <s>upamāna</s> [serves as] object or agent, the <s>ṇamul</s> [suffix] following <s>kaṣā</s> etc. — that [simile] is expressed by it.' '<s>Kaṣādigata</s>' means: accompanied by the usage of <s>kaṣā</s> etc. The illustration of the object-based one of that [simile] —
The fire of love (<s>smarānala</s>), blazing, burned the mind of the other [i.e. an ordinary being] in the same way as [it burned] his mind,
of him whose intellect was drawn toward <s>Umā</s> by the power of <s>tapas</s> (austerity). [UKss 1.*28]

children.text:
atra itarasya prākṛtasya saṃbandhi mana upamānaṃ, bhagavanmana upameyaṃ, dahyamānatvaṃ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ /
tacca trayaṃ śabdaspṛṣṭam /
upamānopameyabhāvastvatra ṇamulsāmarthyādivādīnāmaprayoge 'pi gamyate /
teneyamekalope saṃkṣepopamā karmopamānikā kṛtpratyayāvaseyā /
children.translated_text: Here, the mind of the other, i.e. an ordinary being, is the <s>upamāna</s>; the mind of the Lord is the <s>upameya</s>; the quality of being burned is the common property. All three of these are explicitly stated. The <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship is understood here from the force of the <s>ṇamul</s> [suffix], even without the employment of <s>iva</s> etc. Therefore this is a condensed simile with the omission of one [component], object-based, inferred from a <s>kṛt</s> suffix.
The illustration of the agent-based one of that [simile] —
He, though his body was burned, [yet] his self abiding solely in valor,
touched by <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love), thought the thought of an ordinary being. [UKss 1.*29]

children.text:
vigrahaḥ śarīram /
atra sāmānyabhūtaḥ prāṇī guṇātiśayaśūnya upaprānaṃ, tacchabdanirdiṣṭaśca bhagavānupameyaḥ, cintayitṛtvaṃ sādhāraṇo dharmo, ṇamulsāmarthyācca ivāderaprayoge 'pyupamānopameyabhāvāvasāyaḥ /
teneyamekalope sati kartrupamānikā saṃkṣepopamā kṛtpratyayāvaseyā /
evameṣā kṛtpratyayāvaseyā saṃkṣepopamā dvividhā pratipādatā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vigraha</s> means body. Here, an ordinary being (<s>sāmānyabhūta prāṇī</s>), devoid of the excellence of qualities, is the <s>upamāna</s>; the Lord, referred to by that word, is the <s>upameya</s>; the state of being a thinker (<s>cintayitṛtva</s>) is the common property; and from the force of the <s>ṇamul</s> suffix, even without the employment of <s>iva</s> etc., the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship is ascertained. Therefore this is an agent-based condensed simile with the omission of one [component], inferred from a <s>kṛt</s> suffix. Thus this condensed simile inferred from a <s>kṛt</s> suffix has been demonstrated as twofold.

children.text:
yā tu taddhitasāmarthyāvaseyā vatiśabdādavagamyate, sā saṃpūrṇatvātpūrvamuktā /
anyā tvasaṃpūrṇā kalpabādeḥ taddhitsya prayogādavasīyate /
taduktaṃ 'kalpapprabhṛtibhiranyaiśca taddhitaiḥ sā nibadhyate kavibhiḥ'iti /
prabhṛtiśabdenātra 'ive pratikṛtau'ityādivihitānāṃ kanādīnāṃ parigrahaḥ /
tasyā udāharaṇam-----
children.translated_text: That which is inferred from the force of a <s>taddhita</s> suffix, understood from the word <s>vat</s>, is a complete [simile] and has already been stated previously. But the other, which is incomplete, is inferred from the employment of <s>taddhita</s> suffixes such as <s>kalpa</s>, <s>bā</s>, and the like. This was stated: 'through <s>kalpa</s> and other <s>taddhita</s> suffixes, it is bound by poets.' By the word <s>prabhṛti</s> (and so forth) here, the suffixes <s>ka</s> etc., prescribed by rules such as '<s>ive pratikṛtau</s>' (in the sense of resemblance, like a replica), are included. An illustration of that —
Like an outcaste (<s>caṇḍālakalpa</s>), scorched by <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love), when I have disappeared,

children.text: saṃjātātulanairāśyā kiṃ sā śokānmṛtā bhavet // UKss_1.*30 //
children.translated_text: having conceived matchless despair — might she have died from grief? [UKss 1.*30]

children.text:
atra caṇḍāla upamānaṃ, mayītyasmadartha upameyaḥ, kalpappratyayena ca sādṛśyamupāttm /
prakṛtyarthasadṛśer'the bhagavatkātyāyanadṛśā kalpabādīnāṃ vidhānāt krauryādistu dharmaḥ svaśabdānupātto 'pi sāmarthyādatrāvasīyate /
teneyamekalope sati taddhitāvagamyā saṃkṣepopamā /
evamaśvaka ityatrāpi draṣṭavyam /
ivārthopalakṣite sadṛśe kano vidhānāt /
āyaḥśūlika ityādau tu tritayalopena taddhitasāmarthādupamāvasāyaḥ /
tathāhi, atrāyaḥśūlenānvicchatīti vigṛhya "ayaḥśūladaṇḍājinābhyā"miti ṭhagvadhīyate /
atra cāyaḥśūlamupamānaṃ, arthānveṣaṇopāyaḥ kaścidupameyaḥ tīkṣṇatvādiḥ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ upamānopameyabhāvaśceti catuṣṭayamavagamyate /
tanmadhyātsvaśabdaspuṣṭamupamānamayaḥśūleneti /
śiṣṭaśabdasya tu tritayasyātrārthasāmarthyādavagatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, 'caṇḍāla' is the <s>upamāna</s> (object of comparison), 'in me' (mayī) is the <s>upameya</s> (subject of comparison) in the sense of 'this person,' and the similarity is conveyed by the suffix <s>kalpa</s>. Since, according to the view of the revered <s>Kātyāyana</s>, suffixes like <s>kalpa</s> etc. are prescribed for meanings similar to the meaning of the base, the <s>dharma</s> (common property) such as cruelty etc., though not explicitly stated by its own word, is determined here through contextual force. Therefore, when there is elision of one element, this is a <s>saṃkṣepopamā</s> (condensed simile) understood through the <s>taddhita</s> (secondary suffix). The same should be observed in 'aśvaka' as well, since the suffix <s>ka</s> is prescribed in the sense of similarity indicated by the meaning of <s>iva</s>. In cases like 'āyaḥśūlika,' however, the determination of <s>upamā</s> (simile) is through the force of the <s>taddhita</s> with elision of three elements. That is to say, here, analyzing it as 'one who seeks by means of an iron spear' (āyaḥśūlena anvicchatīti), the suffix <s>ṭhak</s> is applied according to the rule 'āyaḥśūladaṇḍājinābhyām.' Here, the four elements are understood: the iron spear is the <s>upamāna</s> (object of comparison), some means of seeking one's goal is the <s>upameya</s> (subject of comparison), sharpness etc. is the <s>sādhāraṇa dharma</s> (common property), and the relation of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>. Among these four, the <s>upamāna</s> 'by the iron spear' (āyaḥśūlena) is made explicit by its own word. The remaining three, however, are understood here through the force of contextual meaning.

children.text:
nanu cātropamānenāyaḥśūlenārthānveṣaṇopāyasyopameyasya tadbhāvādhyavasānenāpāditābhedasya pratīyamānatvādatiśayoktiriyaṃ na tūpamā /
tatkathametadupamānodāharaṇam /
ucyate /
yathā 'śaśicchāyavadanām'ityatra satyapi śaśicchāyāpracchāditarūpatve vadanacchāyāyāḥ kathañcidbhedapratipattipuraḥ-- sarīkāreṇopamābhedatvamupanyastaṃ tathātrāpi bhaviṣyatītyadoṣaḥ /
tenāyaḥ--śūlika ityatra tritayalope sati taddhitāvaseyā saṃkṣepopamā bhavati ev śvā mumūrṣati kūlaṃ pipatipatītyādāvapi yadi maraṇapatanādyānuguṇyasya upameyabhūtasya tadbhāvādhyavasānātsanvācyayā icchayopamānabhūtayā samāpāditābhedasya pratīyamānasya bhedāvagatinibandhanaṃ kiñcidvidyate tadopamābhedatvaṃ vācyam /
children.translated_text: Objection: Here, since the <s>upameya</s> (subject of comparison), namely the means of seeking one's goal, is identified with the <s>upamāna</s> (object of comparison), the iron spear, through superimposition of non-difference (<s>tadbhāvādhyavasāna</s>), and since this is what is cognized, this would be <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), not <s>upamā</s> (simile). How then can this be cited as an example of <s>upamā</s>? The answer is: Just as in 'śaśicchāyavadanām' (one whose face is like moonlight), even though the true form of the face is concealed by the moonlight-likeness, the status as a variety of <s>upamā</s> is maintained because there is somehow a cognition of difference as a precondition — so too it will be here, and there is no fault. Therefore, in 'āyaḥśūlika,' when three elements are elided, there is indeed a <s>saṃkṣepopamā</s> (condensed simile) to be understood through the <s>taddhita</s>. Even in expressions like 'the dog wishes to die' (śvā mumūrṣati), 'the bank is about to fall' (kūlaṃ pipatiṣati), etc., if there exists some basis for cognizing difference — between the <s>upameya</s> (subject of comparison), namely the suitability for death, falling, etc., and the <s>upamāna</s> (object of comparison), namely the desire expressed by the <s>san</s> suffix, with which it is identified through superimposition of non-difference — then the status as a variety of <s>upamā</s> should be stated.

children.text:
anyathā tvatiśayoktibhedatāsyāvaseyā /
yadāha sanvidhau bhagavānkātyāyanaḥ--"āśaṅkāyāmacetaneṣūpasaṃkhyānam""na vā tulyakāraṇātvādicchāyā hi pravṛttita upalabdhiri"ti, "upamānādvā siddhamiti" ca /
atra hi 'na vā tulyakāraṇatvādi'tyādinā tadbhāvadhyavasānaṃ sūcitam /
'upamānādvā siddhami'ti tūpamānopameyabhāvaḥ pratipāditaḥ /
iyaṃ ca ghātoḥ sano vidhānāttadantasya ca dhātutvātsubdhātūpamāvat dhātudhātūpamāvaseyā /
evaṃ vartamānasāmīpyādāvapyupamābhedatvamatiśayoktibhedatvaṃ vā yathāpratīti yojyam /
cūrṇikārasya tvevamādau tadbhāvādhyavasānasamāśrayema nātiśayoktibhedatvameveṣṭam /
yadāha"na tiṅantenopamānamastī"ti /
ata eva daṇḍinā "limpatīva tamo 'ṅgāni varṣatīvāñjanaṃ nabhaḥ /
asatpuruṣaseveva dṛṣṭirniṣphalatāṃ gatā"ityādergarbhīkṛtātiśayotprekṣābedatvameva mahatā prapañcenābhyadhāyi /
tena kadā devadatta grāmaṃ gamiṣyasi, eṣa gacchāmītyādāvapi vartamānasāmīpye vartamānarūpatayā bhaviṣyatkālasyādhyavasānādatiśayoktibhedatvameva vācyam /
evamanyatrāpyūhyam /
evameṣā vākyasamāsasubdhātukṛttaddhitāvaseyā saṃkṣepo pamā pañcavidhā pratipāditā /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, its status as a variety of <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) should be determined. As the revered <s>Kātyāyana</s> states regarding the <s>san</s> construction: 'In the case of apprehension, the inclusion of inanimate objects is to be added,' 'Or not, because the cause is similar — for the operation is based on the apprehension of desire,' and 'Or it is established from the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison).' Here, by the statement 'Or not, because the cause is similar' etc., the superimposition of identity (<s>tadbhāvādhyavasāna</s>) is indicated. But by 'Or it is established from the <s>upamāna</s>,' the relation of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> is established. And since the <s>san</s> suffix is prescribed after a verbal root and the form ending in it is itself a verbal root, this should be understood as a root-to-root <s>upamā</s>, like a <s>sub-dhātu upamā</s> (simile through a verbal derivative). Similarly, in cases of proximity to the present tense etc., the status as a variety of <s>upamā</s> or as a variety of <s>atiśayokti</s> should be applied according to the actual cognition. However, for the <s>Cūrṇikāra</s> (the author of the prose commentary), in such cases, relying on the superimposition of identity, only the status as a variety of <s>atiśayokti</s> is preferred. As he states: 'There is no <s>upamāna</s> (comparison) with a finite verb form (<s>tiṅanta</s>).' For this very reason, <s>Daṇḍin</s> extensively demonstrated that examples like 'Darkness smears the limbs as it were, the sky rains collyrium as it were, like the service of a wicked person, sight has become fruitless' are varieties of <s>garbhīkṛtātiśayotprekṣā</s> (embedded hyperbolic fancy). Therefore, even in expressions like 'When will you go to the village, <s>Devadatta</s>?' — 'I am going now,' where the future time is superimposed upon through the form of the present tense due to proximity, the status as a variety of <s>atiśayokti</s> alone should be stated. The same should be inferred in other cases as well. Thus, this <s>saṃkṣepopamā</s> (condensed simile), to be understood through <s>vākya</s> (sentence), <s>samāsa</s> (compound), <s>sub-dhātu</s> (verbal derivative), <s>kṛt</s> (primary suffix), and <s>taddhita</s> (secondary suffix), has been demonstrated to be fivefold.

children.text:
saṃpūrṇā tu vākyāsamāsataddhitabhedena trividhā pūrvamuktā /
āsāmeva cāvāntarabhedā anye nirdiṣṭāḥ /
tathāhi, saṃpūrṇayorvākyataddhitopamayoḥ śrautatvārthatvabhedena pratyekaṃ dvaividhyamuktam /
saṃkṣepopamāyāśca samāsopamāyā ekadvayatrayalopena caturbidhatvam /
ekalopasya hi tatra dvaividhyamuktam, ivādeḥ sādhāraṇadharmavācinaśca lopat sabdhātūpamāyāścaturvidhatvam, kyackyaṅkvippratyāyāvaseyatvāt /
kyacpratyāyāvaseyā hi karmādhakaraṇopamānakatvena dvividhoktā /
kṛtpratyāyāvaseyāyāśca kartṛkarmopamānakatvena dvividhatvam /
tadevameṣā saptadaśavidhā granthakṛtā upamā pratipāditā /
tadāhuḥ---
children.translated_text: The <s>saṃpūrṇā</s> (complete simile), on the other hand, was previously stated to be threefold, distinguished as <s>vākya</s> (sentence), <s>samāsa</s> (compound), and <s>taddhita</s> (secondary suffix) types. And further sub-varieties of these have been indicated. That is to say, for the complete <s>vākya</s>-<s>upamā</s> and <s>taddhita</s>-<s>upamā</s>, a twofold division of each was stated based on the distinction between explicit (<s>śrauta</s>) and implied (<s>ārtha</s>). And for the <s>saṃkṣepopamā</s> (condensed simile), the <s>samāsa</s>-<s>upamā</s> is fourfold through elision of one, two, or three elements. The single elision was stated to be twofold — through elision of <s>iva</s> etc. and of the word expressing the <s>sādhāraṇa dharma</s> (common property). The <s>sub-dhātu upamā</s> (verbal-derivative simile) is fourfold, being understood through the suffixes <s>kyac</s>, <s>kyaṅ</s>, <s>kvip</s>, and other affixes. The <s>kyac</s>-derived one was stated to be twofold, having the <s>upamāna</s> (object of comparison) as either <s>karman</s> (object) or <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (location). And the <s>kṛt</s>-derived one is twofold, having the <s>upamāna</s> as either <s>kartṛ</s> (agent) or <s>karman</s> (object). Thus, this <s>upamā</s> has been demonstrated by the author of the treatise to be of seventeen varieties. They state:
From <s>kṛt</s> (primary suffixes), <s>taddhita</s> (secondary suffixes), <s>samāsa</s> (compounds), <s>sub-dhātu</s> (verbal derivatives), and <s>vākya</s> (sentences),
<s>upamā</s> (simile) is understood to be twofold: <s>pūrṇā</s> (complete) and <s>luptaikadeśā</s> (with partial elision).
Through elision of one, two, or three elements, the elided type is threefold.
The first two varieties are each twofold, while the third is of one form only.
Thus.

children.text: pūrvau bhedau dvidhā cātreti sādhāraṇadharmavācilopāccaikalopasya dvaividhyam /
children.translated_text: 'The first two varieties are each twofold' — this means the twofold division of the single elision is due to the elision of the word expressing the <s>sādhāraṇa dharma</s> (common property).

The elision of two elements is also twofold: through the absence of the word expressing the <s>sādhāraṇa dharma</s> (common property) together with <s>iva</s> etc., and through the absence of the word expressing the <s>upameya</s> (subject of comparison) together with <s>iva</s> etc.

children.text: eṣā copamā vicitrabhedatve satyapi yatraiva cetohāritvamasti tatraivālaṅkāratāṃ pratipadyate na sarvatretyuktam //
children.translated_text: And this <s>upamā</s> (simile), even though it has manifold varieties, attains the status of an <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure of speech) only where it possesses the power to captivate the mind (<s>cetohāritva</s>), not everywhere — thus it has been stated.
<s>Prativastūpamā</s> (counter-subject simile) —
Where, in the proximity of the <s>upamāna</s> (object of comparison), a word expressing similarity is used by the learned,

children.text: upameyasya ca kavibhiḥ sā prativastūpamā gaditā // UKss_1.22 //
children.translated_text: and likewise for the <s>upameya</s> (subject of comparison) — that is called <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-subject simile) by the poets. (UKss 1.22)

children.text:
yatropamānopameyayoḥ saṃnidhāne sāmyavācinaḥ padasyāsakṛdupādānaṃ kriyate sā parativastūpamā /
nanu yadi sāmyavācinaḥ padasya tatrāsakṛdupādānaṃ kriyate tato 'nekavākyatvamāpatati /
na cānekasmin vākye ivādīni prayujyante, ekavākyaniṣṭhatayā teṣāmabhidhāsāmarthyāvasitatvāt /
ataścevādīnāmaprayoge kathaṃ tatropamānopameyabhāvāvasāya ityāsaṅkyāha----
children.translated_text: Where, in the proximity of both <s>upamāna</s> (object of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (subject of comparison), the word expressing similarity is employed more than once — that is <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-subject simile). Objection: If the word expressing similarity is employed more than once there, then the problem of having multiple sentences arises. And particles like <s>iva</s> etc. are not used across multiple sentences, since their denotative capacity is determined as pertaining to a single sentence. Therefore, when <s>iva</s> etc. are not employed, how can the relation of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> be determined? Anticipating this objection, he says:
One of the two obtains the status of <s>upameya</s> (subject of comparison) by virtue of being contextually relevant (<s>prākaraṇika</s>),
and the other obtains the status of <s>upamāna</s> (object of comparison) — thus there is no need for a word denoting <s>upamā</s> (simile). (UKss 1.23)

Even in the absence of <s>iva</s> etc. due to multiple sentences, the relation of <s>upamāna</s> (object of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (subject of comparison) is here determined through the force of meaning, by consideration of what is contextually relevant (<s>prākaraṇika</s>) and what is not — this is the meaning.
They state:
Even when <s>iva</s> etc. are not apprehended, <s>upamā</s> (simile) is sometimes discerned through the semantic structure of words (<s>śabdasaṃskāra</s>),
and in other cases it is based solely on the meaning (<s>kevalārthanibandhanā</s>).
Thus.

children.text:
iha prakāratrayeṇa upamāyāḥ pratipattiḥ /
kvacidavādiśabdasāmarthyādupamā vācyabhūtā pratīyate, yathā candra iva mukhamasyā ityādau /
kvacittu tattadviśiṣṭasaṃskārasahāyācchabdātsvārthābhidhānamukhena lakṣyamāṇāyāstasyāḥ pratipattiḥ, yathā śastrīśyāmeti /
atra hi
children.translated_text: Here, the cognition of <s>upamā</s> (simile) occurs in three ways. In some cases, <s>upamā</s> is cognized as directly expressed (<s>vācya</s>) through the force of words like <s>iva</s> etc., as in 'her face is like the moon' (candra iva mukham asyāḥ) and the like. In other cases, however, the cognition of <s>upamā</s> occurs through indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), by way of the word's denoting its own meaning, aided by specific semantic conditioning (<s>saṃskāra</s>), as in '<s>śastrīśyāmā</s>' (dark like a blade). For here,
through the two words '<s>śastrī</s>' and '<s>śyāmā</s>,' endowed with semantic conditioning such as the unity of a single word through compounding etc.,

children.text:
svārthābhidhānavyavadhānena lakṣyamāṇopamā gamyate /
kvacittūpamānopameyanibandhanaśabdasaṃskārābhāve 'pi kevalādevārthasāmarthyāttasyāḥ pratipattiḥ, yathā rūpakadīpakaprativastūpamādiṣvityarthaḥ /
ataścāsyāṃ prativastūpamāyāṃ kevalenaivārthasāmarthyenopamānopameyatvamavagamyate ityadoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>upamā</s> (simile) is understood as indicated (<s>lakṣyamāṇā</s>) through the mediation of denoting their own meanings. In yet other cases, even in the absence of semantic conditioning based on words for <s>upamāna</s> (object of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (subject of comparison), the cognition of <s>upamā</s> occurs solely through the force of meaning alone, as in <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>dīpaka</s> (illuminator), <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-subject simile), and the like — this is the meaning. Therefore, in this <s>prativastūpamā</s>, the status of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> is understood solely through the force of meaning — and there is no fault in this.
An example of this:
Rare in the world are such excellences of virtue and beauty;

children.text: niśāḥ kiyatyo varṣe 'pi yākhindiḥ pūrṇamaṇḍalaḥ // UKss_1.*31 //
children.translated_text: how many nights in the year, indeed, have the full orb of the moon? (UKss 1.*31)

children.text:
viralāḥ svalpāḥ /
tādṛśaḥ pārvatīvarttinyo yāḥ śīlasaundaryasaṃpadaḥ tatsadṛsyaḥ /
śīlaṃ susvabhāvatā /
saundaryaṃ lāvaṇyam /
atra saṃvatsaramadhyavartinyo 'khaṇḍaśaśibimbā rātrayo dvādaśa upamānam /
śīlasaundaryayoḥ saṃbhārāḥ sakalalokotkṛṣṭāḥ katipayajanajuṣa upameyāḥ /
sādhāraṇaśca dharmo viralatvam /

children.translated_text: And in the proximity of the <s>upamāna</s> (object of comparison), this is expressed as 'how many' (kiyatyaḥ).
In the proximity of the <s>upameya</s> (subject of comparison), however, it is expressed as 'rare' (viralāḥ).

Even without the employment of <s>iva</s> etc., the relation of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> is determined here through consideration of what is contextually relevant (<s>prākaraṇika</s>) and what is not.
Therefore, this is a <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-subject simile), because the common basis (<s>sādhāraṇopanibandhā</s>) applies to each subject matter individually.

'Viralāḥ' means 'few.' 'Tādṛśaḥ' means those excellences of virtue and beauty that belong to <s>Pārvatī</s>, or those resembling them. '<s>Śīla</s>' (virtue) means good character. '<s>Saundarya</s>' (beauty) means loveliness. Here, the nights within the year that have an unbroken lunar disc — twelve in number — are the <s>upamāna</s> (object of comparison). The endowments of virtue and beauty, surpassing all people, enjoyed by only a few individuals, are the <s>upameya</s> (subject of comparison). And the <s>sādhāraṇa dharma</s> (common property) is rareness.
Thus ends the first <s>varga</s> (chapter) in the <s>Laghuvṛtti</s> (concise commentary) on the <s>Udbhaṭālaṅkārasārasaṃgraha</s>, composed by the illustrious <s>Pratīhārendurāja</s>.
Now begins the second <s>varga</s> (chapter).
<s>Ākṣepa</s> (ironic denial), <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration), <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), <s>vibhāvanā</s> (poetic causation),
<s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) and <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) — these <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures of speech) are recognized by other authorities. (UKss 2.1)
In 'samāsātiśayoktī ca,' the word <s>ukti</s> (expression) connects individually with each of the words <s>samāsa</s> and <s>atiśaya</s>.
<s>Ākṣepa</s> (ironic denial):
That which is a seeming prohibition of the desired, made with the intention of expressing a distinction,

children.text: ākṣepa iti taṃ santaḥ śaṃsanti kavayaḥ sadā // UKss_2.2 //
children.translated_text: is called <s>ākṣepa</s> (ironic denial) — so the excellent poets always declare. (UKss 2.2)

children.text:
iha kācidvakrabhaṇitistathāvidhā saṃbhavati yasyāṃ vidhitsitor'tho niṣedhavyājena saṃskriyate, na tu niṣidhyate /
tatra vidhitsitasyārthasya yaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ kriyate sa pratiṣedha iva bhavati, na tu pratiṣedha eva /
avāntaravākyārthatvena tatra vākyasyāparyavasānāt /
avāntaravākyārthatā ca tatra niṣedhasya vidhitsitārthavirodhādbhavati /
tatra hi vidhitsitor'thaḥ pūrvopakrāntatvena sthemnāvatiṣṭhamānaḥ svavirūddhatvena niṣedhaṃ niṣedhatātparyātpracyāvyasvagataviseṣābhidhānāyāvāntaravākyārthīkaroti /
ato 'nantaroktena prakāreṇeṣṭasyārthasya viśeṣamabhidhātuṃ yatra niṣedha iva na tu niṣedha eva, asāviṣṭārthanirākaraṇasya leśena saṃbhavadākṣepasaṃjñako 'laṅkāraḥ satkavibhirabhidhīyate /
santaḥ kavaya iti saṃbandhaḥ /
tasya bhedadvitayopadarśanāyāha---
children.translated_text: Here, there exists a certain kind of oblique expression (<s>vakrabhaṇiti</s>) in which the intended meaning is embellished through the semblance of negation, but is not actually negated. In such cases, the prohibition of the intended meaning appears to be a prohibition, but is not truly a prohibition, because the sentence does not terminate at the meaning of the subordinate clause. The subordinate status of the negation arises from its contradiction with the intended meaning. For the intended meaning, firmly established by virtue of having been previously introduced, dislodges the negation from its prohibitive purport through being contrary to it, and makes it serve as a subordinate clause for the purpose of expressing a distinction pertaining to itself. Therefore, where there is a seeming negation — not an actual negation — of the desired meaning, for the purpose of expressing a distinction in the manner just described, that figure of speech (<s>alaṅkāra</s>), which has a trace of apparent rejection of the desired meaning, is called <s>ākṣepa</s> by accomplished poets. 'Excellent poets' (<s>santaḥ kavayaḥ</s>) is the syntactic connection. To illustrate its two varieties, he says:
And it is considered to be twofold, having as its domain what is yet to be stated and what has already been stated.

<s>Ākṣepa</s> (ironic denial) is twofold because the expression of negation is made with reference to what is yet to be stated (<s>vakṣyamāṇa</s>) and what has already been stated (<s>ukta</s>) — this is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu 'pratiṣedha iveṣṭasya'ityākṣepalakṣaṇamuktam /
iṣṭatvaṃ cecchākarmatā /
yasya ca vastuna icchākarmatā tasya nāvaśyamuktikriyāṃ prati karmatvaṃ bhavati /
iṣyamāṇaṃ hi kadāciducyate kadācinna /
ataśceṣṭasyoktikarmatāmāśritya yadetadākṣepasya vakṣyamāṇoktaviṣayatayā dvaividhyamuktaṃ tanna saṃgacchate ityāśaṅkyāha----
children.translated_text: Objection: The definition of <s>ākṣepa</s> was stated as 'a seeming prohibition of the desired.' And 'being desired' means being the object of will (<s>icchākarmatā</s>). But that which is the object of will does not necessarily become the object of the act of speaking. For what is desired is sometimes spoken and sometimes not. Therefore, this twofold division of <s>ākṣepa</s> into that whose domain is what is yet to be stated and what has already been stated, based on the desired thing's being the object of speaking, does not hold — anticipating this objection, he says:

children.text: niṣedheneva tadbandho vidheyasya ca kīrtitaḥ // UKss_2.3 //
children.translated_text: And it is declared that the binding of what is to be enjoined is accomplished through what appears to be a negation. (UKss 2.3)

children.text:
vidheyasya vidhātuṃ jñāpayitumabhimatasya yo niṣedha iva tenāyaṃ vakṣyamāṇoktaviṣaya ākṣepo nibadhyate /
etaduktaṃ bhavati----vidhānakarmatādvāreṇaivātra iṣṭatvamavasīyate /
nibandhanāntarābhāvāt /
vidhānakarmatā ca vidhānātmikāyā ukteḥ karmatā /
sāca dvividhā, ārthī
children.translated_text: This <s>ākṣepa</s> (ironic denial), whose domain is what is yet to be stated or what has already been stated, is composed through what appears to be a negation of what is intended to be enjoined — that is, what is intended to be made known. This is what is meant: here, 'being desired' (<s>iṣṭatva</s>) is determined only through the medium of being the object of enjoinment (<s>vidhānakarmatā</s>), since there is no other basis. And being the object of enjoinment means being the object of a statement (<s>ukti</s>) whose nature is enjoinment. This is twofold: implicit (<s>ārthī</s>)

children.text:
śābdī ca /
yatra svaśabdavyāpāramantareṇāpi śabdāntaravyāpārasahāyaniṣedhamukhenaiva vidhitsitor'tho 'vagamyate tatrārthī /
tatra ca vakṣyamāṇaviṣaya ākṣepaḥ /
yatra tu vidhimukhenaiva vaktumiṣṭasyārthasyopādānaṃ kriyate tatra śābdī /
tatra coktaviṣayatā ākṣepasya /
evaṃ cānantaroditaya nītyā śābdenārthena ca vidhinā yadaṃvasitamiṣṭaṃ tasyoktikriyākarmatvasaṃbhavāduktikriyāyāḥ karmabhūto yor'thastadāśrayaṃ
children.translated_text: and explicit (<s>śābdī</s>). Where the intended meaning is understood solely through negation aided by the operation of another word, without the operation of its own word, there it is implicit (<s>ārthī</s>). And there, the <s>ākṣepa</s> has as its domain what is yet to be stated (<s>vakṣyamāṇaviṣaya</s>). But where the desired meaning is first presented through a positive statement (<s>vidhimukha</s>), there it is explicit (<s>śābdī</s>). And there, the <s>ākṣepa</s> has as its domain what has already been stated (<s>uktaviṣaya</s>). Thus, by the principle just stated, since what is determined as desired through enjoinment — whether explicit or implicit — can indeed be the object of the act of speaking, and since the meaning that is the object of the act of speaking serves as the basis,
the status of having as its domain what is yet to be stated, and the status of having as its domain what has already been stated, are both established for <s>ākṣepa</s> (ironic denial).
An example of <s>ākṣepa</s> whose domain is what is yet to be stated:
Ah, such is the greatness of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), that even upon <s>Rudra</s> (Śiva), such a state is seen!

children.text: iyadāstāṃ samudrāmbhaḥ kumbhairmāne tu ke vayam // UKss_2.*1 //
children.translated_text: Let this much suffice — if the ocean's waters were measured by pots, then who are we? (UKss 2.*1)

children.text:
aho iti vismaye /
atra manmathamāhātmyaṃ tadavasthāviśeṣasaṃsparśena pratipādayitumiṣṭam /
tacca tasya tathāpratipādanamiyadāstāmityādinā niṣiddham /
niṣedhaścātrābhidheyatvavirodhāt /
abhidheyatvena ca virodhaṃ vakti /
ānantyena tasya tathāvidhasya vaktumaśakyatvāt /
rudre 'pi nāma īdṛśī daśeti hi sāmānyarūpatvena manmathamāhātmyaṃ pratipāditaṃ na tu viśeṣarūpatayā /
ato vaktumiṣṭānāṃ smaramāhātmyāvasthāviśeṣāṇāmayamānantyenābhidhānaniṣedha iva natu niṣedha eva /
vivakṣitārthavirodhenāvāntaravākyārthatvāt /
tathāhi, atra samudrāmbhasaḥ kumbhairmātumaśakyatvaṃ yadasmadarthakartṛkamabhihitaṃ tatsādṛśyenānantyaviśiṣṭatvenotkarṣayitumiṣṭānāṃ manmathamāhātmyāvasthāviśeṣāṇāṃ pūrvaṃ pratipipādayiṣitatvena labdhapratiṣṭhānāṃ vākyārthatvam /
ataśca tadabhidhānaniṣedhasya tadvirodhādatrāvāntaravākyārthatā /
na cāvāntaravākyārtho vākyaviśrāntisthānatayā vaktuṃ śakyaḥ /
na khalu raktaḥ paṭo bhavatītyatra raktatvāvacchinnapaṭabhavanaparatvādvākyasya paṭabhavanaparyavasānamātratvaṃ subhaṇam /
ato 'trāpi niṣedhasyāvāntaravākyārthatvena vākyaviśrāntisthānatvābhāvānniṣedharūpatvamiva na tu niṣedharūpatā /
sa ca niṣedho 'trāvāntaravākyatvātpradhānavākyārthānuguṇyena pravartamānaḥ khakaṇṭhenābhidhānaṃ manmathamāhātmyāvasthaviśeṣāṇāṃ niṣedhati, na punararthasāmarthyāvaseyamapi /
ataśca samudrāmbhasaḥ kumbhairptātumaśakyatvamasmadarthakartṛkaṃ svakaṇṭhenābhihitaṃ yattatsādṛśyenāvasite saṃvijñānapadaśūnye smaramāhātmyāvasthāviśeṣāṇāmānantyalakṣaṇe viśeṣe vākyasya paryavasānaṃ tenāyamiṣṭamarthaṃ pratiṣedhavyājena viśeṣe 'vasthāpayati tasmādākṣepaḥ /
atra ca 'aho smarasya māhātmyaṃ yadrudre 'pi daśedṛśī'ityetacchabdavyāpārasahāyena'iyadāstām'iti niṣedhenaiva svakaṇṭhenānupāttānāmapi manmathamāhātmyāvasthāviśeṣāṇāṃ vakṣyamāṇatayā sūcanam /
teṣāṃ ca tathā sūcitānāṃ niṣedhavyājena saṃvijñānapadaśūnyānantyabhedapratipādanam /
ato vakṣyamāṇaviṣayatā ākṣepasya /
children.translated_text: '<s>Aho</s>' expresses wonder. Here the greatness of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) is desired to be conveyed through contact with that particular state. And that manner of conveying it is prohibited by [the phrase] 'let this much suffice' and so on. The prohibition here is because of conflict with expressibility. And it declares the conflict as being with expressibility, because of the impossibility of stating such a thing due to its infinitude. For 'even in <s>Rudra</s>, such is the state!' — by this, the greatness of <s>Manmatha</s> is conveyed in a general form, not in a specific form. Therefore, this is a prohibition of expression, as it were, of the specific states of the greatness of <s>Smara</s> (Love) that are desired to be stated, [prohibition] on account of their infinitude — but not truly a prohibition, because, being contrary to the intended meaning, it serves as a subordinate sentence-meaning. For thus: the impossibility of measuring the ocean-water with pots, stated here as having our purpose as its agent, by analogy with that, the sentence-meaning consists of the specific states of the greatness of <s>Manmatha</s> that were previously desired to be conveyed and that have obtained their foundation through being distinguished by infinitude as what is to be elevated. And therefore, the prohibition of their expression, being contrary to that, has the status of a subordinate sentence-meaning here. And a subordinate sentence-meaning cannot be stated as the resting-place of the sentence. For in 'the cloth is dyed,' one cannot properly say that the sentence terminates merely in the being-of-cloth, since the sentence has as its purpose the being-of-cloth delimited by dyed-ness. Therefore, here too, since the prohibition, being a subordinate sentence-meaning, is not the resting-place of the sentence, it has the semblance of being a prohibition but is not actually a prohibition. And that prohibition here, being a subordinate sentence, operates in conformity with the principal sentence-meaning: it prohibits the explicit expression of the specific states of the greatness of <s>Manmatha</s>, but not what is to be inferred from the force of meaning. Therefore, the impossibility of measuring the ocean-water with pots, stated explicitly as having our purpose as its agent, by analogy with that, the sentence terminates in the specific quality of infinitude — devoid of any verbal designation — of the specific states of the greatness of <s>Smara</s>. Thus, this [figure] establishes the intended meaning in a specific form under the guise of prohibition; therefore it is <s>ākṣepa</s> (feigned denial). And here, by the statement 'Oh, the greatness of <s>Smara</s>, that even in <s>Rudra</s> such is the state!' — aided by the function of those words — through the prohibition itself in 'let this much suffice,' there is an indication, as something to be stated, of specific states of the greatness of <s>Manmatha</s> that are not explicitly taken up in one's own voice. And the conveyance of those thus indicated, under the guise of prohibition, as infinite varieties devoid of verbal designation. Therefore the <s>ākṣepa</s> (feigned denial) pertains to what is to be stated.
An example of [<s>ākṣepa</s>] pertaining to what has been stated:
Thus as he pondered, [it is] remarkable that his pondering had no limit;

children.text: kva vā kāmavikalpānāmantaḥ kālasya cekṣitaḥ // UKss_2.*2 //
children.translated_text: where indeed has the end of the elaborations of desire or of time been seen?

children.text:
atra citratvasyoktasyoktiḥ kva veti prasiddhatvādākṣipyate /
pūrvatra khalu viruddhatvamākṣepanibandhanamuktam, iha tu prasiddhatvam /
dvābhyāmeva ca prakārābhyāmākṣepo bhavati viruddhatvena prasiddhatvena ca /
uktaṃca---"vastu prasiddhamiti yadviruddhamiti vāsya vacanamākṣipya /
anyattathātvasidydhai yatra brūyātsa ākṣepaḥ"iti /
prasiddhatvaṃ cātra samarthayituṃ kālasādṛśyasamuktam /
yathā kālasyānto nekṣyate tadvat kāmavikalpānām /
ato naivātra catratvam /
anyatrāpyasya rūpasya paridṛṣṭatvāditi /
kālatulyatayā cātra kāmavikalpānāmānantyātmako viseṣaḥ saṃvijñānapadaśūnyo 'bhidhitsitaḥ /
tasya ca citratayā sāmānyena pūrvamupakrāntasyādhunā niṣedhavaśena saṃvijñānapadaśūnyena vivakṣitena rūpeṇa vākyārthīṃbhūtatvānniṣedhasya pūrvavadavāntaravākyārthatā /
tena kvavetyayaṃ niṣedha iva natu niṣedha eva /
tenātrokta viṣayatā ākṣepasya /
tadāhuḥ----
children.translated_text: Here, the remarkableness that has been stated is objected to by 'where indeed?' on the grounds of its being well-known. Earlier, contradiction was stated as the basis for <s>ākṣepa</s>; here, however, it is well-knownness. And <s>ākṣepa</s> arises by these two means only — through contradiction and through well-knownness. As stated: 'Where, having objected to one's statement that a thing is well-known or contradictory, one speaks something else to establish its being-so — that is <s>ākṣepa</s>.' And well-knownness here is supported by the analogy with time. Just as the end of time is not seen, so too of the elaborations of desire. Therefore there is nothing remarkable here, since this form is observed elsewhere too. And here, the specific quality of infinitude — devoid of verbal designation — of the elaborations of desire, by analogy with time, is what is desired to be conveyed. And since this was first introduced in general terms as 'remarkableness,' and is now, through the force of prohibition, made into the sentence-meaning in the intended form that is devoid of verbal designation, the prohibition has, as before, the status of a subordinate sentence-meaning. Therefore 'where indeed?' is a prohibition, as it were, but not actually a prohibition. Therefore here the <s>ākṣepa</s> pertains to what has been stated. Thus they say:
Where there is prohibition — regarding a meaning touched by words or even a meaning desired to be stated —
and that [prohibition] becomes a component of that [meaning] through its contradiction: that is <s>ākṣepa</s> (feigned denial).
Thus.

children.text:
śabdena spṛśyate (spṛṣṭe?) vaktumiṣṭe uktaviṣaye ākṣepe /
vakṣyamāṇaviṣaye tu vivakṣitasya ārthatā /
śabdāntaravyāpārasahāyaniṣedhamukhena
children.translated_text: 'Touched by words' (<s>śabdaspṛṣṭa</s>) — [concerns] <s>ākṣepa</s> pertaining to a stated subject. 'Desired to be stated' (<s>vaktumiṣṭa</s>) — [concerns] <s>ākṣepa</s> pertaining to a subject yet to be stated. In the latter, the intended meaning [has the status of being] a meaning [inferred through]

children.text:
tasyopasthāpyamānatvāt /
yaścātrobhayatrāpi niṣedhaḥ kriyate sa vivakṣitārthavirodhātsvatātparyaṃ tyaktvā vivakṣitamevārthaṃ saṃkurvaṃstadaṅgatāṃ pratipadyate /
ato 'tra dvividha ākṣepo bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: the prohibition, aided by the function of other words, by which it is brought to mind. And the prohibition that is made in both cases here, by conflicting with the intended meaning, abandons its own purport and, while serving the intended meaning itself, assumes the status of a component thereof. Therefore, the meaning is that <s>ākṣepa</s> is of two kinds.
<s>Arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration through another matter):
Where the statement of the corroborator comes first and that of the other [the corroborated] comes after,
or in reverse order — whether with the word '<s>hi</s>' or otherwise too —
that should be known as <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration through another matter).

children.text:
yatra samarthyasamarthakabhāvaḥ sor'thāntaranyāsaḥ /
tatra hi samarthakasya samarthakatāvagatihetuṃ vyāptiṃ pakṣadharmatvaṃ cānupanyasyārthāntarasyevopanyāsaḥ kriyate /
vyāptipakṣadharmatvayoḥ svaśabdenānupāttayorapi garbhīkṛtatvāt /
ato 'sāvarthāntaranyāsaḥ /
sa ca caturvidhaḥ /
tatra samarthake pūrvamabhihite samarthyasya yatra paścādabhidhānaṃ tatra dvau prakārau bhavataḥ /
hiśabdābhivyaktatvaṃ samarthyasamarthakabhāvasyaivakaḥ prakāraḥ /
taduktaṃ "samarthakasya pūrvaṃ yadvaco 'nyasya ca pṛṣṭhataḥ" /
iti, "hiśabdoktye"ti ca /
tasyodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: Where there is the relation of corroborated and corroborator, that is <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>. For therein the introduction of what is another matter, as it were, is made for the corroborator without explicitly presenting the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) and the property-of-the-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>) that are the grounds for understanding its corroborating nature. Because the pervasion and the property-of-the-subject, though not explicitly taken up by their own words, are incorporated within. Therefore it is <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>. And it is of four kinds. Where the corroborator is stated first and the corroborated is stated afterwards, there are two types. One type is where the relation of corroborated and corroborator is made manifest by the word '<s>hi</s>.' As stated: 'where the statement of the corroborator comes first and that of the other comes after' and 'with the word <s>hi</s>.' Its example:
There is nothing that one does not do, for the world is intent on its purposes;

children.text: eṣa śarvo 'pi bhagavān baṭūbhūya sma vartate // UKss_2.*3 //
children.translated_text: even this blessed <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) conducted himself as a young student (<s>baṭu</s>).

children.text:
baṭūbhūya acirakṛtopanayanatvamāpadya /
atra śarvasya sarvalokātiśāyino baṭūbhāvena vṛttimanupapadyamānatayāśaṅkya tatsamarthanāya samarthakaṃ pūrvamevopanyastaṃ "tannāsti yanna kurute"iti /
atyantakāryikatvādanucitamapi rūpamanubhūtavān /
śarvastadanyaivaṃvidhapuruṣavaditi /
atra ca hiśabdenābhivyaktaḥ samarthyasamarthakabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Baṭūbhūya</s>' means having assumed the state of one who has recently undergone the investiture ceremony (<s>upanayana</s>). Here, since <s>Śarva</s>'s conduct as a young student is untenable as he surpasses all the world, having suspected [the need for justification], the corroborator is presented first for its justification: 'there is nothing that one does not do.' Because of extreme purposefulness, he experienced even an unsuitable form — <s>Śarva</s>, like any such person. And here the relation of corroborated and corroborator is made manifest by the word '<s>hi</s>.'

children.text:
yatra pūrveṇaiva krameṇa samarthyasamarthakayorupanyāse hiśabdaścārthasāmarthyavaseyārthatvānna prayujyate tatra dvitīyor'thāntaranyāsabhedo bhavati /
taduktaṃ "anyathāpi ca"iti /
hiśabdoktimantareṇāpītyarthaḥ /
tasyodāharaṇ---
children.translated_text: Where, in the same order of presentation of corroborated and corroborator, the word '<s>hi</s>' is not employed because its meaning is to be inferred from the force of meaning — there is the second type of <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>. As stated: 'or otherwise too.' Meaning: even without the expression by the word '<s>hi</s>.' Its example:
Concealed conduct is praised in the examination of women's dispositions;
therefore <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) set forth, having assumed the body of a young Brahmin student (<s>bāṭavī</s>).

children.text:
bhāvaḥ āśayaḥ /
bāṭavīṃ brahmacārisaṃbandhinīm /
atra dhūrjaṭerbaṭuveṣālambanena pracchannā śasyate vṛttiḥ"ityādinā /
yoṣidāśayaparīkṣaṇapravṛttatvāddhūrjaṭiḥ pracchannāṃ vṛttimāśritavāniti /
hiśabdaścātrātaḥśabdasāmarthyena yasmādityasyārthasyāvagatatvānnopāttaḥ /
evametau samarthakapūrvopanyāsāvarthāntaranyāsau dvāvevoktau /
yatrāpi caitadviparyayeṇa sāmarthyasya pūrvamupanyāsaḥ paścātsamarthakasya, tatrāpi samarthyasamarthakabhāve hiśabdāvagater'thākṣipte ca sati dvaividhyam /
taduktaṃ 'viparyayeṇa vā yatsyāddhiśabdoktyānyathāpi vā'iti /
pūrvasyodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhāva</s>' means intention, disposition. '<s>Bāṭavīm</s>' means pertaining to a Brahmin student (<s>brahmacārin</s>). Here, <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>'s adoption of concealed conduct by taking the guise of a student — by the [statement] 'concealed conduct is praised' and so on — because of being engaged in examining the dispositions of women, <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> adopted concealed conduct.
