And the word '<s>hi</s>' is not employed here because, by the force of the word '<s>atas</s>' (therefore), the meaning 'because' (<s>yasmāt</s>) is already understood. Thus these two types of <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> with the corroborator presented first have been stated. Where also, in reverse of this, the corroborated is presented first and the corroborator afterwards, there too, the twofold division arises from the understanding of the corroborated-corroborator relation by the word '<s>hi</s>' and from its being implied by the meaning. As stated: 'or in reverse order, whether with the word <s>hi</s> or otherwise too.' Example of the first:
Then <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) resorted to meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), having established himself by himself;

children.text: visaṃvadeddhi pratyakṣaṃ nirdhyātaṃ dhyānato na tu // UKss_2.*5 //
children.translated_text: for perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) may deceive, but what is meditated upon through <s>dhyāna</s> [does] not.

children.text:
atra harasya vyavahitādyarthaviṣayatvenāpratihatabāhyendriyavṛttitvāt sati bāhyendriyajanyapratyakṣasaṃbhave dhyānāśrayaṇamayuktatvena saṃbhāvyaṃ tatsamarthanāyoktaṃ 'visaṃvadeddhi pratyakṣam'ityādi /
atyantāvisaṃvādakopalabdhyupāyārthitvādydhānamāsthitavān hara iti /
children.translated_text: Here, since <s>Hara</s>, regarding an object such as a remote thing, does not have his external sense-faculties obstructed, and since external-sense-generated perception is possible, his resorting to meditation is suspected as being unjustified. To justify that, it is said: 'for perception may deceive' and so on. Because of desiring a means of apprehension that is absolutely non-deceiving, <s>Hara</s> resorted to meditation.

children.text: hiśabdānabhivyakte tu samarthyasamarthakabhāve yatra samarthyasya pūrvamupanyāsastatrodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: Where the relation of corroborated and corroborator is not made manifest by the word '<s>hi</s>', and the corroborated is presented first — its example:
He saw <s>Umā</s> performing extremely severe austerities (<s>tapas</s>);

children.text: asaṃbhāvyapatīcchānāṃ kanyānāṃ kā parā gatiḥ // UKss_2.*6 //
children.translated_text: for maidens who desire an inconceivable husband, what other recourse is there?

children.text:
bahūnāmabhimatavaraprāptyupāyānāṃ prārthanādīnāṃ saṃbhave kasmādbhagavatī tapasā śarīramāyāsitavatītyāśaṅkya tatsamarthanāyābhihitaṃ 'asaṃbhāvyapatīcchanām'iti /
duḥprāpabhartrabhilāṣitvāttapaḥ samāśritavatī /
tapāṃsi bhagavatīṃ khedayanti /
tāni punaḥ sā tathāvidhānyupārjayati /
children.translated_text: When there exists the possibility of many means such as entreaties for obtaining the desired husband, why did the blessed goddess subject her body to austerity? — having suspected [this], for its justification it is said: 'for maidens who desire an inconceivable husband...' Because of desiring a husband who is difficult to obtain, she resorted to austerity. The austerities afflict the blessed goddess; and she in turn generates further such austerities.

children.text:
atastapastapyate tapastapaḥkarmakasyaiveti kartuḥ karmavadbhāvaḥ /
evameva caturvidhor'thāntaranyāso 'bhihitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is heated — the agent of austerity's action acquires the status of its object. Thus this fourfold <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> has been stated.

children.text:
nanu yadi samarthyasamarthakabhāve satyarthāntaranyāso bhavati /
evaṃsatyaprastutapraśaṃsādṛṣṭāntayorapi samarthyasamarthakabhāvasadbhāvādarthāntaranyāsatāprasaṅgaḥ /
tathāhi /
"prīṇitapraṇayi svādu kāle pariṇataṃ( ca yat) vinā puruṣakārema phalaṃ paśyata śākhinām"ityāsyāmaprastutapraṃśasāyāṃ viśeṣātsāmānyasya pratipattiryathā secanādikaṃ puruṣavyāpāramantareṇa vanaśākhināṃ vividhaguṇopetasya phalasya prasūtirdaivapradhānā evametatsarvaṃ jagati daivapradhānamiti /
atra ca samarthyasamarthakabhāvo vidyate /
sarvaṃ jagacceṣṭitaṃ daivapradhānaṃ puruṣakārānvayavyatirekānanuvidhāyitvādvanaśākhiphalavaditi /
tataśca
children.translated_text: Now, [objection:] if <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> arises when there is the relation of corroborated and corroborator, then in that case, since the relation of corroborated and corroborator also exists in <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustrative example), there would be the absurd consequence that they too are <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>. For example, in the <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>: 'Pleasing to the well-disposed, sweet, ripened in due season — behold the fruit of trees, [produced] without human effort!' — here, from the specific, the general is understood: just as the bearing of fruit endowed with various qualities by forest trees without any human activity such as watering is primarily due to fate, so too everything in this world is primarily due to fate. And here the relation of corroborated and corroborator exists: everything in the world is primarily due to fate, not following the presence and absence of human effort, like the fruit of forest trees. And therefore,
the absurd consequence that even there it would be <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> — this is the fault of the definition having too wide an extension.
In <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustrative example) too, the relation of corroborated and corroborator exists.

children.text: tathāhi "tvayi dṛṣṭa eva tasyā nirvāti mano manobhavajvalitam /
children.translated_text: For instance: 'At the very sight of you, her mind, blazing with the fire of love, is extinguished;
for in the light of the cool-rayed [moon], the night-lily of the <s>kumudvatī</s> (lotus pond) blossoms.'

children.text:
ityatra yathā candraguṇapakṣapātitvena kumudinyāścandrāloke kumudaṃ vikasati, tadvadguṇapakṣapātitvāttsyāstvaddarśane mano manmathāgniprajvalitamupaśāmyatīti samarthyasamarthakabhāvo 'vagamyate /
tena dṛṣṭānte 'pyarthāntaranyāsatāprasaṅga ityāśaṅkyāha----
children.translated_text: Here, just as the night-lily of the lotus pond blossoms in the moonlight because of being partial to the moon's qualities, so too her mind, blazing with the fire of desire, is pacified at the sight of you because of being partial to your qualities — thus the relation of corroborated and corroborator is understood. Therefore, the absurd consequence that even <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> would be <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> [arises]. Anticipating this, he says:
Because of the corroboration of the contextually relevant meaning,
[<s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>] stands apart from <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustrative example).

children.text:
satyamaprastutapraśaṃsāyāṃ dṛṣṭānte ca samarthyasamarthakabhāvo 'vagāmyate /
na tu tatrārthāntaranyāsavatsamarthyasamarthakabhāvasya saṃbhavaḥ /
arthāntaranyāse hi sarthyasya yathāyogaṃ pūrvottarakālabhāvitvena svakaṇṭhenopāttsaya samarthanam, aprastutapraśaṃsāyāṃ tpaprakṛtasāmarthyena prakṛtamākṣipyate, na tu svakaṇṭhenopādīyate, yathā pūrvopavarṇite udāharaṇe /
tatra hi vanaśākhināṃ phaladarśanenāprakṛtena daivapradhānena samagrajagadgocaraṃ daivaprādhānyaṃ prakṛtamākṣipyate, na tu tasyārthāntaranyāsavatsvakaṇṭhenopādānam /
ataśca tatra satyapi samarthyasamarthakabhāve śabdopakrāntaprakṛtārthaniṣṭhatvābhāvānnārthāntaranyāsatvam /
dṛṣṭānte 'pica dvayorapi samarthyasamarthakayoḥ svakaṇṭhenopāttatvātsatyapi svakaṇṭhopāttaprakṛtārthaniṣṭhatve dṛṣṭāntasya samarthyasamarthakabhāvapuraḥsarīkāreṇa pravartamānatvānna bhavatyaryāntaranyāsatvam /
na khalu tasya samarthyasamarthakabhāvapuraḥsarakāreṇa pravṛttiḥ /
bimbapratibimbabhāvamātrasya śabdaspṛṣṭatvāt /
arthāddhi tatra samarthyasamarthakabhāvāvasāyaḥ /
arthāntaranyāse tu samarthyasamarthakabhāvenaivopakramaḥ /

children.translated_text: Therefore, where the introduction of another matter has as its inception the relation of corroborated and corroborator, there it is <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>; hence the absurd consequence that <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> would be <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> does not arise.
This has been stated as 'because of the corroboration of the contextually relevant meaning' and so on.
Here the word 'contextually relevant' (<s>prakṛta</s>) should be understood as referring to the contextually relevant meaning that is taken up in one's own voice and culminates [in the sentence].
And 'corroboration' here is taken up as belonging to the initial stage of inception.

True, in <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> the relation of corroborated and corroborator is understood. But the relation of corroborated and corroborator does not obtain there in the same way as in <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>. For in <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>, the corroboration of the corroborated, which is taken up explicitly in one's own voice as belonging to the prior or subsequent stage as appropriate, [is done directly]; but in <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>, the contextually relevant [meaning] is implied by the force of the irrelevant, and is not taken up in one's own voice — as in the example described above. For there, the contextually relevant [idea] that everything in the world is primarily due to fate is implied by the irrelevant [illustration of] seeing the fruit of forest trees, and is not explicitly adopted. Therefore, although the relation of corroborated and corroborator exists there, it is not <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>, because of the absence of culmination in the contextually relevant meaning initiated by words. In <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> too, even though both the corroborated and corroborator are taken up in one's own voice, and even though there is culmination in the contextually relevant meaning taken up in one's own voice, because the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> operates with the relation of corroborated and corroborator as its precursor, it is not <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>. For its operation is not with the relation of corroborated and corroborator as its precursor; rather, only the image-and-reflection relation (<s>bimbapratibimbabhāva</s>) is what is touched by the words. The understanding of the corroborated-corroborator relation there is from the meaning [alone]. But in <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>, the very inception is through the relation of corroborated and corroborator.
<s>Vyatireka</s> (contrast):
The presentation of a distinction between the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) and the object of comparison (<s>upameya</s>) —

children.text: nimittādṛṣṭidṛṣṭibhyāṃ vyatireko dvidhī tu saḥ // UKss_2.6 //
children.translated_text: through the non-perception and the perception of the ground [of comparison] — that <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) is of two kinds.

children.text:
upamānopameyayoḥ parasparaṃ yatra viśeṣaḥ khyāpyate sa vyatirekaḥ /
tatra hyupamānādupameyasyopameyādupamānasya vā kenacidviśeṣeṇātireka ādhikyaṃ tasmādyvatirekaḥ /
sa ca dvividhaḥ /
tatra viśeṣakhyāpananimittasyārthasāmarthyādākṣepādekaḥ prakāraḥ /
aparastu tasya svaśabdena pratipādanāt /
taduktaṃ 'nimittādṛṣṭidṛṣṭibhyāṃ dvidhā'iti /
etāvapi ca bhedau pratyekaṃ dvividhau /
kvaciddhi arthasāmārthyātpratīyamāne upamānopameyabhāve pūrvoktena prakāradvayena vyatirekaḥ khyāpyate, kvacittu ivādibhirupātaiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vyatireka</s> (contrast) is where the distinction between the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> is made known mutually. For therein, the superiority (<s>ātireka</s>) — the excess — of the <s>upameya</s> over the <s>upamāna</s>, or of the <s>upamāna</s> over the <s>upameya</s>, by some distinguishing feature, constitutes <s>vyatireka</s>. And it is twofold. Therein, one kind is when the ground of the distinction being made known is implied through the force of meaning. The other is when that [ground] is stated through its own word. This was stated: 'twofold, through the unseen and seen ground.' And each of these two varieties is itself twofold. For sometimes, when the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship is understood through the force of meaning, the contrast is made known in the two previously stated manners; and sometimes through the employment of <s>iva</s> etc.
Therein, where the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship is understood through the force of meaning, the illustration of the first variety in the first pair of manners —
She, having gone to the peak of <s>Gaurī</s> [mountain], saw <s>Umā</s>, emaciated by austerity,
surpassing from afar the slender form of the moon whose radiance had been drunk by <s>Rāhu</s>. [UKss 2.*7]

children.text:
rāhuṇā pītā dravadravyasyodakādeḥ svagalabilāntarbhāvanaṃ yattadvadātmābhyantarīkṛtā prabhā yasya sa tathoktaḥ /
atra
children.translated_text: 'Drunk by <s>Rāhu</s>' — just as a liquid substance like water is made to enter the interior of one's own throat-cavity, so too the radiance that has been drawn within himself — the one of whom this is so is described thus. Here,

children.text: rāhuṇā pītā dravadravyasyodakādeḥ svagalabilāntarbhāvanaṃ yattadvadātmābhyantarīkṛtā prabhā yasya ta tathoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Drunk by <s>Rāhu</s>' — just as a liquid substance like water is made to enter the interior of one's own throat-cavity, so too the radiance that has been drawn within himself — the one of whom this is so is described thus.

children.text:
atra rāhupītaprabhatvaviśiṣṭasyendostanurupamānaṃ, tapaḥkṛśā pārvatyupameyā, anayoḥ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ svabhāvataḥ saundarye sati nimittavaśādvicchāyatvam /
tacca svakaṇṭhenānupāttamapi padārthasvarūpaparyālocanayā labhyate /
evamivādyabhāve 'pyupamānopameyabhāvasyātra sāmarthyātpratipattirjayantīmiti ca upamānādupameyasya viśeṣaḥ khyāpitaḥ /
tasya ca viśeṣasya khyāpyamānasya nimittamatra na svakaṇṭhenopāttaṃ, arthasāmarthyāttu tadavagamyate /
rāhurinduprabhāpāne tathā na samarthaḥ yathā tapaḥsātiśayatvātpārvatyāḥ kṣāmatve iti rāhuto 'pi tapaḥsātiśayatvamupamānādupameyasya viśeṣanimittamatrāvagamyate /
evamayamanupāttanimitto vyatirekaḥ /
upāttanimittastu-----
children.translated_text: Here the slender form (<s>tanu</s>) of the moon, qualified by having its radiance drunk by <s>Rāhu</s>, is the <s>upamāna</s>; <s>Pārvatī</s>, emaciated by austerity, is the <s>upameya</s>; the common property of these two is paleness arising from some cause despite inherent beauty. And this, though not explicitly stated, is obtained through the consideration of the true nature of the word-meanings. Even in the absence of <s>iva</s> etc., the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship is here apprehended through the force [of meaning]. And by [the word] '<s>jayantīm</s>' (surpassing), the superiority of the <s>upameya</s> over the <s>upamāna</s> is made known. The ground of that distinction being made known is here not explicitly stated, but is understood from the force of meaning — namely, that <s>Rāhu</s> is not as capable of drinking the moon's radiance as austerity is of causing <s>Pārvatī's</s> emaciation due to its excessive intensity. Thus, the excessive intensity of austerity, even more than <s>Rāhu</s>, is understood here as the ground of the <s>upameya's</s> superiority over the <s>upamāna</s>. Thus this is a <s>vyatireka</s> with an unstated ground. But [the one] with a stated ground —

children.text: padmaṃ ca niśi niḥśrīkaṃ divācandraṃ ca niṣprabham /
children.translated_text: The lotus at night is bereft of splendor, and the moon by day is devoid of radiance;
with her face of ever-gleaming luster, she put them both to shame. [UKss 2.*8]

children.text:
mukhamupameyam /
padmaminduścopamānam /
taccātra dvayaṃ svakaṇṭhaspṛṣṭam /
tayostu sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ kāntimattādirupamānopameyabhāvaścetyatadubhayaṃ sāmarthyādavagamyate /
na khalvatra vakṣyamāṇavyatirekavadupamānopameyabhāvasya dyotakā ivādaya upāttāḥ /
adhaḥprakurvatīmiti copamānādupameyasya viśeṣaḥ khyāpitaḥ /
tatra ca nimittamupāttamupamānopameyobhayādhāratvena /
upamānayostāvatpadmacandrayorniśi divā ca yathākramaṃ niḥśrīkatvaniṣprabhatve, upameye tu rātrindivaṃ sphuracchāyatā /
ato viśeṣe nimittadarśanenāyaṃ vyatirekaḥ /
children.translated_text: The face is the <s>upameya</s>. The lotus and the moon are the <s>upamāna</s>. Both of these are explicitly stated. But their common property — the quality of possessing beauty and the like — and the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship are understood from the force [of meaning]. Indeed, here the <s>iva</s> etc. that indicate the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship, as in the <s>vyatireka</s> to be discussed below, are not employed. And by '<s>adhaḥ prakurvatīm</s>' (putting to shame), the superiority of the <s>upameya</s> over the <s>upamāna</s> is made known. The ground of that [superiority] is explicitly stated, pertaining to both the <s>upamāna</s> and the <s>upameya</s>. As for the <s>upamānas</s>, the lotus and moon, at night and by day respectively, the absence of splendor and the absence of radiance [are stated]; but for the <s>upameya</s>, the luster gleams day and night. Therefore, this is a <s>vyatireka</s> through the showing of the ground for the distinction.

children.text:
tadevaṃ yatrevādinopamānopameyabhāvo nāvadyotitastatra dvividho vyatireko darśitaḥ /
ivādyupāte tūpamānopameyabhāve yo vyatirekastamāha----
children.translated_text: Thus, where the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship is not indicated by <s>iva</s> etc., a twofold <s>vyatireka</s> has been shown. But when the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship is established through the employment of <s>iva</s> etc., the <s>vyatireka</s> of that kind he now states —
That which is an illustration through dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>), conjoined with [words like] '<s>yathā</s>' and '<s>iva</s>,'
that too is considered <s>vyatireka</s> here, because it is connected with the establishment of a distinguishing feature. [UKss 2.7]

children.text:
'yo vaidharmyeṇa dṛṣṭānta'iti 'viśeṣāpādanānvayāda'ti ca vyatirekalakṣaṇaṃ yojitam /
vaidharmyaṃ hyupameyadharmasyopamāne vigamaḥ /
yathevādisamanvita ityanena yathevādyavadyotitatvamupamānopameyabhāvasyāha /
tasyodāharaṇam-----
children.translated_text: The definition of <s>vyatireka</s> is expressed by combining 'that which is an illustration through dissimilarity' with 'because it is connected with the establishment of a distinguishing feature.' <s>Vaidharmya</s> (dissimilarity) is the absence in the <s>upamāna</s> of a quality belonging to the <s>upameya</s>. By 'conjoined with <s>yathā</s>, <s>iva</s>, etc.,' he states that the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship is indicated by <s>yathā</s>, <s>iva</s>, etc. An illustration of that —
[She who was] established in harsh austerity, [sustained by] the diet of fallen leaves, water, and wind,
who bore no unprecedented pride, unlike other ascetics. [UKss 2.*9]

children.text:
śīrṇaparṇāmbuvātānāmāśo bhakṣaṇam /
atrānyatapasvina upamānaṃ, bhagavatyupameyā, sādhāraṇaśca dharmaḥ kaṣṭe tapasyavasthitatvāccetasaḥ sollāsatā /
vatiścātra garvodvahananibandhanaṃ yattaccetasaḥ sollāsatvaṃ tannibandhanamupamānopameyabhāvamavagamayati /
garvaṃ na samudvahantīmityupamānādupameyasya viśeṣaḥ piratipāditaḥ /
anye kila tapasvinaḥ sātiśayatapovaśātsamullasitacittāḥ santo garvaṃ samudvahanti, bhagavatī tvatyantamupaśāntacittatvānna tathā /
evaṃ cātra garvopakramāvasthāpekṣamupamānopameyayoḥ sādṛśyaṃ, tadanirvāhāttūpamānādupameyasya vyatirekaḥ /
anirvāhe ca nimittamatra svakaṇṭhenānupāttamapyarthasāmarthyādavagamyate atyantopaśāntacittatvaṃ nāma /
evamayaṃ nimittādarśane batyupāttopamānopameyabhāvo vyatireka udāhṛtaḥ /
nimittopādāne tu tasyodāharaṇamunneyam /
evamete catvāro vyatirekāḥ pratipāditāḥ /
nimittadarśanādarśanābhyāṃ yau vyatarekau tayoḥ
children.translated_text: The diet (<s>āśa</s>) of fallen leaves, water, and wind means the eating thereof. Here, other ascetics are the <s>upamāna</s>, the Goddess (<s>Bhagavatī</s>) is the <s>upameya</s>, and the common property is the exaltation of spirit from being established in harsh austerity. The <s>vat</s> suffix here is the basis for bearing pride; the exaltation of spirit (<s>sollāsatva</s>) that is the ground for that [pride-bearing] causes the understanding of the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship. By 'not bearing pride,' the superiority of the <s>upameya</s> over the <s>upamāna</s> is demonstrated. Other ascetics, with their spirits elated due to the excess of their austerity, bear pride; but the Goddess, due to having an extremely tranquil mind, does not [bear pride] in that way. Thus here, the similarity between the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> is with respect to the preliminary state of pride, but due to its non-completion, the contrast of the <s>upameya</s> from the <s>upamāna</s> [arises]. And the ground for the non-completion, though not explicitly stated here, is understood from the force of meaning — namely, the extremely tranquil nature of her mind. Thus this <s>vyatireka</s> with the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship established through <s>vat</s>, without showing the ground, has been illustrated. But for the one with the showing of the ground, the illustration should be inferred. Thus these four kinds of <s>vyatireka</s> have been demonstrated. Since the two <s>vyatirekas</s> [distinguished] by the showing and non-showing of the ground

children.text:
pratyekamupamānopameyabhāvasya ivādyupādānānupādānābhyāṃ dvibhedatvāt /
eṣāmapi caturṇāṃ vyatirekāṇāṃ śliṣṭoktiyogyaśabdopādāne sati punarapare pūrvopakrāntenaiva rūpeṇa catvāro bhedā bhavanti /
tadāha-----
children.translated_text: each have twofold variety through the employment or non-employment of <s>iva</s> etc. for the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship. And when, for these four kinds of <s>vyatireka</s>, words suitable for <s>śliṣṭa</s> (paronomastic) expression are employed, four more varieties arise in the same form as previously described. He states this —
When, through the separate employment of a word suitable for <s>śliṣṭa</s> (paronomastic) expression,

children.text: viśeṣāpādanaṃ yatsyādyvatarekaḥ sa ca smṛtaḥ // UKss_2.8 //
children.translated_text: the establishment of a distinguishing feature occurs — that too is considered <s>vyatireka</s>. [UKss 2.8]

children.text:
'ekaprayatnoccāryāṇāmi'tyādivakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇaṃ śliṣṭam /
śliṣṭālaṅkārasamucitaṃ yaduccāraṇaṃ tatsamucitasya śabdasya yadā tantreṇa sadṛśaśabdāntaropādānahetutayā vā prayogo na kriyate api tu pṛthak pṛthaguccāraṇaṃ, tadā viśeṣāpādane sati vyatareko bhavati /
tasyodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: 'Pronounced with a single effort' and so forth — [this describes] the characteristic of <s>śliṣṭa</s> (paronomasia) to be stated later. When a word suitable for the <s>śliṣṭa</s> ornament is employed not in combination — not as a cause for the employment of another similar word — but rather separately, then when the establishment of a distinguishing feature occurs, <s>vyatireka</s> obtains. An illustration of that —
The winter splendor (<s>śaiśirī śrī</s>), renowned through the <s>tapas</s> (austerity/cold) of a single month,
[she was] far surpassing and putting it below, through her long-enduring <s>tapas</s>. [UKss 2.*10]

children.text:
atra śiśiraśobhā upamānaṃ, bhagavatī upameyā, tayośca sādhāraṇo dharmastapoyuktatvaṃ nāma /
ekatra tapā
children.translated_text: Here, the beauty of winter is the <s>upamāna</s>, the Goddess is the <s>upameya</s>, and the common property of the two is the quality of being conjoined with <s>tapas</s>. In one case, <s>tapas</s>

children.text:
māgho māsaḥ, aparatra tvabhyudayahetuḥ kṛcchrācaraṇam /
ivādayaścātrānupāttā api sāmarthyādavagamyante /
vyatirekastu dūrādvidadhatīmadha iti /
tasya ca nimittaṃ māsaikyaṃ dīrdhatvaṃ ca tapasoḥ /
children.translated_text: The ground of that [contrast] is the oneness of the month versus the duration of the <s>tapas</s>.
And that is explicitly stated as pertaining to the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> respectively.

children.text: tatra ca vatyādinā anupātte upamānopameyabhāve nimittadarśanena vyatireka udāhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, when the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship is not established by <s>vat</s> etc., the <s>vyatireka</s> with the showing of the ground has been illustrated.

children.text: evamanayā diśāanyadapi śliṣṭoktiyogyaśabdanibandhe sati vyatarekasya pūrvoktanayena bhedatrayamudāhāryam //
children.translated_text: In this manner, following this direction, the other three varieties of <s>vyatireka</s> when words suitable for <s>śliṣṭa</s> expression are employed should also be illustrated according to the previously stated method.

means the month of <s>Māgha</s> (the cold month), while in the other, it means the arduous practice that is the cause of spiritual elevation. And <s>iva</s> etc., though not employed, are understood from the force [of meaning]. The contrast is [expressed by] 'far surpassing and putting below.'
<s>Vibhāvanā</s> (causally incongruous description) —
When, despite the negation of an action, the result of that action [is described as occurring] — that <s>vibhāvanā</s> (incongruity of cause)

children.text: jñeyā vibhāvanaivāsau samādhau sulabhe sati // UKss_2.9 //
children.translated_text: should be known as the [ornament called] <s>vibhāvanā</s>, when the resolution [of the incongruity] is easily available. [UKss 2.9]

children.text:
iha yatkiṃcijjñāyate tatsarvaṃ kriyāphalam /
kriyāmukhena kāraṇebhyaḥ kāryotpatteḥ prātītikena rūpeṇa paridṛśyamānatvāt sarveṣāṃ phalabhūtānāṃ kriyaivāvyavahataṃ kāraṇam yatra ca kriyā pratiṣidhyate atha ca kriyāphalasyotpattirupadiśyate tatra vibhāvanākhyo 'laṃkāraḥ /
kāraṇavigame kilakāryasya tatrotpattirupavarṇyate /
ato viruddhābhāsā bhāvanā utpādanā, tena vibhāvanā /
nanvevaṃ sati vyarthadoṣatvaprasaṅgaḥ 'viruddhārthaṃ mataṃ vyartham'iti ata āha---samādhau sulabhe satīti /
samādhiḥ parihāraḥ /
yatra virodhasya sulabhaḥ parahāra ityarthaḥ /
tasyā udāharaṇam-----
children.translated_text: Whatever is known in this world — all of that is the result of an action. Since the production of effects from causes through the medium of action is universally observed in its experiential form, action is indeed the uninterrupted cause of all results. Where an action is negated and yet the production of the result of that action is described — there the ornament called <s>vibhāvanā</s> [obtains]. For the arising of an effect where the cause is absent is described there. Therefore, it is an apparent contradiction (<s>viruddhābhāsā</s>) in the bringing about (<s>bhāvanā</s>) or production — hence <s>vibhāvanā</s>. Now, if this is so, then the fault of purposelessness (<s>vyarthadoṣa</s>) would follow, since 'what has contradictory meaning is considered purposeless.' Therefore he says: 'when the resolution is easily available.' The resolution (<s>samādhi</s>) means the solution. The meaning is: where the resolution of the contradiction is easily [available]. An illustration of that —
[She], whose bodily line was yellow without the application of saffron,
and who bore the seal of lips that were copper-red without lac-dye. [UKss 2.*11]

children.text:
aṅgalekhā śarīrayaṣṭiḥ /
kāramīraṃ kuṅkumam /
yeyaṃ pītacchāyatā śarīrasya sā nāyikānāṃ kuṅkumasamālambhanalakṣaṇakriyākāryā prāryaṇa paridṛśyate, bhagavatyāstu śarīre pītacchāyatvaṃ na kuṅkumasamālambhanenotpāditam /
ataḥ kuṅkumasamālambhanalakṣaṇāyāḥ kriyāyā vigame phalasya pītacchāyatvasyātropadeśaḥ /
parihāraścātra svābhāvikatayā tacchāyatvamiti /

children.translated_text: Therefore this is <s>vibhāvanā</s>.

children.text: analaktakatāmrākṣāmityatrālaktakakāraṇikāyā rāgakriyāyā niṣedhe tatphalasya lauhityasya utpattiḥ svābhāvikī nirdiṣṭā /
children.translated_text: In '<s>analaktakatāmrākṣām</s>' (copper-red-eyed without lac-dye), when the action of coloring caused by lac-dye is negated, the natural arising of its result — redness — is stated.
Therefore [this too is] <s>vibhāvanā</s>.

children.text: atra ca kuṅkumādisaṃpādyena piñcaratvādinā upamānabhūtena svābhāvikasya piñjaratvāderupameyabhūtasyābhedādhyavasāyo 'tiśayoktyā draṣṭavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: And here, the identification without difference (<s>abhedādhyavasāya</s>) of the natural yellowness etc. (which is the <s>upameya</s>) with the yellowness etc. produced by saffron and the like (which is the <s>upamāna</s>) should be understood as involving <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole).

<s>Aṅgalekhā</s> means the outline of the body. <s>Kāśmīra</s> means saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>). The yellow hue of the body that is ordinarily seen as caused by the action of applying saffron in the case of heroines — in the Goddess's body, however, the yellow hue was not produced by the application of saffron. Therefore, here there is the description of the result — the yellow hue — despite the absence of the action characterized by the application of saffron. And the resolution here is that the hue is natural.
<s>Samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) —
Through a sentence concerned with the primary subject, with qualifiers common to that [subject],
the narration of an unintended subject — [this] has been declared as <s>samāsokti</s>. [UKss 2.10]

children.text:
yatra prastutārthaniṣṭhaṃ vākyaṃ tatsamānairviśeṣaṇaistenāprakṛtenārthena tulyāni yāni viśeṣaṇāni taddvāreṇa sādṛśyavaśādaprastutamarthamupamānabhūtaṃ kathayati, sā saṃkṣepeṇopamānopameyalakṣaṇārthadvatayābhidhānātsamāsoktiḥ /
tasyā udāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: Where a sentence whose purpose is the primary subject (<s>prastutārtha</s>), through qualifiers common to it — i.e., qualifiers that are equal to that non-primary subject — by means of those [qualifiers], narrates an unintended subject (<s>aprastuta artha</s>), which serves as the <s>upamāna</s>, through the force of similarity — that, because it concisely expresses two meanings characterized by <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>, is <s>samāsokti</s>. An illustration of that —
[She], whose flowers were the radiance of her teeth, beautiful with the tender shoots of her hands,
slender, gone to the forest, with a row of six-footed ones [bees] hidden in her matted locks. [UKss 2.*12]

children.text:
atra dantaprabhāpāṇijaṭā bhagavatīviśeṣaṇabhūtā yathākramaṃ latāgatasumanaḥpallavaṣaṭcaraṇarūpeṇa āropeṇa vyā(ptāḥ) (?) tadbhāvamāpadyante /
tanutvaṃ tu bhagavatīlatayoḥ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ /
vanaśabdena ca rūpakapratibhotpattihetunā śleṣeṇa bhagavatītapaścaryādhārabhūtamudakaṃ latādhāreṇa kānanena rūpyate /
ata etānyatra prakṛtāyā bhagavatyā aprakṛtayā latayā samānāni viśeṣaṇāni /
tatsāmarthyena ca prakṛtayā bhagavatyā upameyabhūtayā latā upamānatvenākṣipyate /
teneyaṃ samāsoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the teeth-radiance, hands, and matted locks, which are qualifiers of the Goddess, are respectively superimposed upon — they assume the nature of — flowers, tender shoots, and bees belonging to a creeper. And slenderness (<s>tanutva</s>) is the common property of the Goddess and the creeper. By the word 'forest' (<s>vana</s>), through paronomasia (<s>śleṣa</s>) that serves as the cause for the arising of the metaphorical suggestion, the water that is the site of the Goddess's austerity is figured as the forest that is the support of the creeper. Therefore, these qualifiers here are common to the primary subject, the Goddess, and the non-primary subject, the creeper. And through their force, the creeper is suggested as the <s>upamāna</s> for the Goddess, who is the <s>upameya</s> and the primary subject. Therefore this is <s>samāsokti</s>.
<s>Atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) —
That speech (<s>vacas</s>) which, on account of some ground, has a scope that transcends the world,
the learned consider that <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) as an ornament. [UKss 2.11]
Where non-difference is expressed [despite actual] difference, or diversity [despite actual] non-difference,
or where what is merely imagined is presented [as real] — [all these] are called <s>atiśayokti</s>. [UKss 2.12]
Where, between cause and effect, through the reversal of temporal sequence,

children.text: āśubhāvaṃ samālambya badhyate so 'pi pūrvavat // UKss_2.13 //
children.translated_text: rapidity of occurrence is invoked — that too [is <s>atiśayokti</s>], as before. [UKss 2.13]

children.text:
yadvacanaṃ kiṃcitkāraṇamāśritya lokātikrāntagocaramupanibadhyate sātiśayoktiḥ /
tasyāśca catvāro bhedāḥ yatra bhede anyatve ananyatvamaikyaṃ sa ekaḥ /
anyatrābhede aikye nānātvaṃ bhedo yatra sa dvitīyaḥ /
tathā bahiravidyamānasyārthasya saṃbhāvanāmātreṇopanibandhe tṛtayaḥ /
kāryakāraṇayostu kāryasya śīghramevotpādātpaurvāparyaviparyayeṇa caturtho bhedaḥ /
tatrādyasaya bhedasyodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: Any statement that, relying on some ground, is expressed in a scope that transcends the world — that is <s>atiśayokti</s>. And it has four varieties. Where non-difference (identity) is expressed despite [actual] difference — that is the first. Where diversity (difference) is expressed despite [actual] non-difference (identity) — that is the second. Where an object not externally existent is presented on the basis of mere imagination — that is the third. Between cause and effect, due to the very rapid production of the effect, the reversal of temporal sequence [constitutes] the fourth variety. Among these, the illustration of the first — [the variety involving] difference —
With her own beauty-wealth, set ablaze by the radiance of <s>tapas</s>,
though emaciated, appearing as decidedly non-emaciated. [UKss 2.*13]

children.text:
atra yāsāvakārśyāvasthā bhagavatyāḥ pūrvamabhūttato bhinnamapi tapojanitaṃ kārśyaṃ tadabhedenopanibaddhamakṛśāmeveti /
tatra ca nimittaṃ tapastejasā saviśeṣatvamāpāditaḥ saundaryasaṃbhāraḥ /
ato nimittavaśena lokātikrānto gocaro 'sya vākyasya /
teneyamataśayoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the state of non-emaciation that the Goddess formerly possessed — the emaciation born of austerity, though different from that, is presented as identical with it [by saying] 'non-emaciated indeed.' And the ground for that is the accumulation of beauty endowed with special distinction by the splendor of austerity. Therefore, on account of the ground, the scope of this statement transcends the world. Hence this is <s>atiśayokti</s>.
The illustration of the second variety —
And the Lord thought: 'Ah, what loveliness!
Through austerity, a change from her maidenhood is perceived in her.' [UKss 2.*14]

children.text:
atra bhagavatī kumārībhāve 'pi vartamānā taduttarakālabhāvinī yāsauyauvanāvasthā tadyuktatvenopanibaddhā kaumārādanyatvamiti /
nimittaṃ cātra tapojanitā ramaṇīyatā /
tenāyamabhede bhedopanibandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the Goddess, while still in the state of maidenhood, is presented as endowed with the state of youth that is chronologically subsequent to that — [she is described as having] change from maidenhood. And the ground here is the loveliness born of austerity. Therefore this is the presentation of difference despite [actual] non-difference.
The illustration of the third variety —
If a streak of the moon's radiance were to fall upon a blooming lotus,
there would be a comparison for the pearl-rosary in the hand of this one. [UKss 2.*15]

children.text:
śaśidyotacchaṭā candraprakāśaprakāraḥ /
asyāḥ kare muktāphalākṣamālāyāstadā upamā syāditi saṃbandhaḥ /
atra rajanikarakarasaṃparke sati kamalasya saṃkocāvalokanādvikāśitvaṃ bahirasaṃbhavadapi kaviprajāpatinā pratibhopajanitena svavyāpāreṇa saṃbhavadrūpatayā pradarśitam /
ato 'tra saṃbhāvyamānārthanibandhaḥ /
tasya ca lokātikrāntagocarasyārthasya saṃbhāvanāyā nimittaṃ bhagavatīkarādhāratayā muktāphalākṣamālāvalokanam /
tathāhi-ayaṃ tāvallokātikrānto 'paridṛṣṭapūrvo 'smābhiḥ gaurīkaramuktāphalākṣamālayorādhārādheyabhāvo 'valokitaḥ /
tatsajātīyasya padmasya vikāśinaścandrakarāṇāṃ ca yadyādhārādheyabhāvaḥ syāttadātropamānopameyabhāvo bhavediti saṃbhāvanā pravṛttā /
ato 'tra sajātīyapadārthadarśanādbaharasaṃbhavadapi vastu saṃbhavadrūpatayopavarṇyate /
children.translated_text: The rays of the moon (<s>śaśidyotacchaṭā</s>) are the manner of moonlight. The connection is: then there would be a simile for the string of pearl rosary-beads in her hand. Here, even though the blooming of the lotus is externally impossible when in contact with the rays of the moon — since observation shows the lotus closes [under moonlight] — the poet-creator (<s>kaviprajāpati</s>) has presented it as having a possible form through his own creative activity born of imaginative insight. Therefore, the basis here is in a supposed meaning (<s>saṃbhāvyamānārtha</s>). And the ground for the supposition of that meaning, which lies beyond the scope of the ordinary world, is the observation of the relationship of support and supported between the Goddess's hand and the pearl rosary. For this is the case: this relation of support and supported between <s>Gaurī</s>'s hand and the pearl rosary, which has never been seen before by us and transcends ordinary experience, has been observed. If there were such a relation of support and supported between the blooming lotus (of the same kind) and the moonbeams, then there would be the relation of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> — thus the supposition has proceeded. Therefore, here, by observing a similar object, even something externally impossible is described as having a possible form.

children.text:
ekasmin khalu padārthe paridṛṣṭe anyasminnanavalokite 'pi tatsajātīyasaṃbhāvanā pravartate /
yathā dākṣiṇātyasyaikasminnuṣṭre paridṛṣṭe satyaparidṛṣṭoṣṭrāntarasaṃbhāvanā /
ato 'tra saṃbhāvanā sanimittā /
anena ca prakāreṇātropamānābhāvaḥ prakṛtasya vastunaḥ pradarśyate nāstyanyatkiṃcidasyopamānamiti /
ata eva saṃbhāvyamānatayārthasyopanibaddhasya nirācikīrṣayā yadiśabdaḥ prayuktaḥ /
yadiśabdena hyatrāśaṅkā dyotyate /
āśaṅkā cāniścitasadbhāve vastuni bhavati /
yaccāniścitasadbhāvaṃ kavivedhasā saṃbhavadrūpatayopadarśitaṃ vastu tasya purāṇaprajāpatinirmitapadārthaviṣayāyā tadviruddhayā lokapratītyā yānnirākriyamāṇatvaṃ tāvannirupamatvaṃ pratīyate /
evamayaṃ tṛtīyo bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, when one object is observed, even without another being seen, the supposition of something of the same kind arises. Just as for a southerner, upon seeing one camel, the supposition of another unseen camel [arises]. Therefore the supposition here has a ground. And by this method, the absence of a standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) for the subject in question is demonstrated — [that is,] there is no other standard of comparison for this [object]. For this very reason, the word <s>yadi</s> (if) is used, with the intention of rejecting the meaning that has been composed as merely supposed. For the word <s>yadi</s> here indicates doubt. And doubt arises regarding a thing whose existence is uncertain. And that thing of uncertain existence, which has been presented by the poet-creator as having a possible form through the reversal of the form established by the ancient Creator — through the desire to express an excellence of quality — its being refuted by the worldly cognition that pertains to things created by the ancient Creator and is contrary [to the poet's presentation] — that very refutation is understood as being without a standard of comparison (<s>nirupamatva</s>). Thus this is the third variety [of nirupamā].
The fourth, however:

children.text: manye ca nipatantyasyāḥ kaṭākṣā dikṣu pṛṣṭhataḥ /
children.translated_text: I think her sidelong glances fall in the directions behind [her],
while the streams of <s>Kāma</s>'s (love-god's) arrows mostly go ahead. [UKss 2.*16]

children.text:
atra dikṣu kaṭākṣapātaḥ kāraṇam /
smarabāṇaparamparāgamanaṃ tu kāryam /
kāryakāraṇayostu kāraṇasya naisargikaṃ prāgbhāvitvaṃ kāryasya tu paścādbhāvitvam /
iha tu viparyayaḥ /

children.translated_text: Because the effect is presented as preceding.

children.text: paścādbhāvitatvena ca kāraṇasya kaṭākṣā dikṣu pṛṣṭhataḥ paścāt patanti agre smarabāṇaparamparā gacchantīti atra nimittaṃ (anu) kāryasya śīghramevotpādaḥ /
children.translated_text: And because the cause [is presented] as following after — the sidelong glances fall behind in the directions, while the streams of <s>Kāma</s>'s arrows go ahead — the reason here is the exceedingly swift arising of the effect.
Therefore this statement has a scope that transcends the ordinary world, by reason [of the reversal].
Hence [this is] <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole).

Here, the falling of sidelong glances in the directions is the cause. And the going forth of the streams of <s>Kāma</s>'s arrows is the effect. But of cause and effect, the cause naturally precedes and the effect follows after. Here, however, there is a reversal.

Thus ends the second chapter (<s>varga</s>) of the concise commentary (<s>laghuvṛtti</s>) on <s>Udbhaṭa</s>'s <s>Alaṅkārasārasaṃgraha</s>, composed by the great and illustrious <s>Pratīhārendurāja</s>.
Now the third chapter (<s>varga</s>).
<s>Yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration), then <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), and <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) likewise —
others declare these three as <s>alaṅkāras</s> (poetic figures) in the ornamentation of speech. [UKss 3.1]
<s>Yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration):
Of many things that have been stated and are dissimilar in their properties,
the sequential specification is called <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration in order). [UKss 3.2]

children.text:
pūrvamuddiṣṭānāmarthānāṃ yadā krameṇārthāntarāṇyanunirdiśyante tadā yathāsaṃkhyākhyo 'laṅkāraḥ /
tatra hi saṃkhyopalakṣitakramānatikrameṇa śabdenānupātto 'pi padārthānāmanvayaḥ samāśrīyate /
ato yathākramaṃ padārthānāmanvayadhvananādetasyālaṅkārasya yathāsaṃkhyatā /
sa cālaṅkāro bahūnāmalpaśo 'pyupanibadhyamāno yataḥ śobhābaddho bhavati ato bhūyasāmityuktam /
dvayorhi tasyopanibadhyamānasya yāvaccaturguṇatvādirūpatayopanibandho na kṛtaḥ tāvacchobhopetatvaṃ na bhavati /
bhūyasāṃ punararthānāṃ tadyathāsaṃkhyamalpenaiva prayāsenaramyaṃ bhavati /
tatra hi tasya dviguṇasya triguṇasya vopanibandhe śobhātiśayo jāyate /
children.translated_text: When things that have been stated first are subsequently specified in order with other things, that is the <s>alaṅkāra</s> called <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s>. For therein, without transgressing the order indicated by the enumeration, the connection of things — even though not explicitly carried along by words — is inferred. Therefore, through the suggestion of the orderly connection of things, this figure has the character of enumeration (<s>yathāsaṃkhyatā</s>). And this figure, since it becomes endowed with beauty when applied to many [things] even in small measure, the word 'of many' was used. For when it is applied to only two, as long as the application has not been made in the form of fourfold and so on, there is no beauty. But the <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> of many things becomes charming with very little effort. For in the application of the twofold or threefold [enumeration], a surpassing beauty arises.
This was stated:

children.text: taddviguṇaṃ triguṇaṃ vā bahuṣūddiṣṭeṣu jāyate ramyam /
children.translated_text: That same [enumeration], in twofold or threefold form, when many things have been stated, becomes charming.

children.text: yatteṣu pathaiva tato dvayostu bahūśo nibadhnīyāt //
children.translated_text: Therefore, since it follows the same path for those [things], one should bind it extensively for pairs.
Thus.

children.text:
nanu "mṛṇālahaṃse"tyādāvupavarṇayiṣyamāṇe udāharaṇe mṛṇālādibhya upamānebhyo bāhvādīnāmupameyānāṃ viśeṣakhyāpanādyvatirekālaṅkāreṇa sahṛdayahṛdayāṇyāvarjyante, na tu yathāsaṃkhyena /
tatkathaṃ yathāsaṃkhyamalaṅkāra ityāśaṅkyoktam--"asadharmaṇāmiti" /
yatrāpi hi sādharmyabhāvādupamānopameyabhāvābhāvena vyatirekāderupanibandhābhāvastatrāpyayaṃ śobhātiśayamāvahatītyarthaḥ /
yathā----
children.translated_text: Now, in the example to be discussed, beginning with '<s>mṛṇālahaṃsa</s>' (lotus-stalk, swan), since the hearts of connoisseurs are captivated by the figure of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) through the declaration of the special distinction of the <s>upameyas</s> (objects compared) — such as arms and the like — from the <s>upamānas</s> (standards) such as lotus-stalks and the like, and not by <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s>, how then is <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> a [separate] figure? — Anticipating this objection, he said: 'dissimilar in their properties.' Even where, due to the absence of similarity, there is no <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation, and consequently no basis for <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) and the like, even there this [yathāsaṃkhya] produces a surpassing beauty — this is the meaning. For example:
<s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Caturānana</s> (four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>), having the colors of lampblack, snow, and gold respectively,
with <s>Suparṇa</s> (Garuḍa), bull, and swan as vehicles, abiding in the ocean, mountain, and lotus — may they grant us well-being!
Thus.

children.text:
atra hi hariprabhṛtīnāṃ trayāṇāmuddiṣṭānāṃ kajjalaruktvasuparṇavāhanatvajalanidhisthatvādayo dharmāḥ krameṇānunirdiṣṭāḥ /
na ca tatra parasparasādharmyaṃ vidyate /
atha ca kramaparyālocanayā arthānāmānurūpyeṇa samanvayapratīteḥ śobhātiśayo vidyate /
tenāsya sādharmyādyabhāve 'pi pṛthagalaṅkāratāpratilambhādyatra sādharmyādi vidyate tatrāpyalaṅkāratvaṃ durnivāram /

children.translated_text: Therefore, in the example beginning with '<s>mṛṇālahaṃsa</s>' (lotus-stalk, swan), <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> should be viewed as a subordinate part (<s>aṅga</s>) of the figure of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast).
Therefore this is a <s>saṅkara</s> (mixture) in the relation of subordinate and principal (<s>aṅga-aṅgin</s>).
As will be stated: 'Where [figures] stand through mutual assistance,
and do not attain their own independent existence — that is <s>saṅkara</s> (mixture).'

For here, of the three — <s>Hari</s> and the rest — who have been stated, the properties of having the color of lampblack, having <s>Suparṇa</s> as vehicle, and abiding in the ocean, and so forth, are specified in order. And among them, there is no mutual similarity. Nevertheless, by the consideration of order, through the cognition of the fitting connection of things in correspondence, there is a surpassing beauty. Therefore, since this [figure] obtains a separate status as a figure even in the absence of similarity and the like, where there is similarity and the like, its figurative status is irresistible.
Thus. Therefore, <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> should be taught as a separate figure. An example of that:
Lotus-stalks, swans, and lotuses — with arms, gait, and faces

children.text: nirjayantyānayā vyaktaṃ nalinyaḥ sakalā jitāḥ // UKss_3.*1 //
children.translated_text: she clearly defeats them; by her, all lotus-ponds are conquered. [UKss 3.*1]
Here, for the stated [items] — arms, gait, and faces — lotus-stalks, swans, and lotuses are specified in order.

And by virtue of that, since the connection of those [items] — though not explicitly carried by words — is implicitly contained, and because there is oblique expression (<s>vakrabhaṇiti</s>), this is the figure <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s>.
<s>Utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy):
When the desire to express similarity in its [direct] form is absent, [the figure that is] expressed by words such as <s>iva</s> (as if) and the like,
through the attribution of the qualities and actions of something else — that is <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), endowed with surpassing [beauty]. [UKss 3.3]

children.text:
yatrevādipadanibandhaḥ sāmyasya ca rūpaṃ na vivakṣyate tatrotprekṣākhyo 'laṅkāraḥ /
nanvevaṃ satyasaṃbhavo nāma lakṣaṇadoṣaḥ prāptaḥ /
dyotyasyopamānopameyabhāvasyābhāve sati ivādīnāmaprayogaprasaṅgādityāśaṅkyoktaṃ "atadguṇakriyāyogādi"ti /
dravyadharmaḥ siddho guṇaḥ /
sādhyasvabhāvastu kriyā /
idaṃ khalu viśvaṃ
children.translated_text: Where the binding of words like <s>iva</s> and the like occurs, but the [direct] form of similarity is not intended to be expressed — there arises the figure called <s>utprekṣā</s>. Now, if this is so, the definitional defect called 'impossibility of occurrence' (<s>asaṃbhava</s>) would follow — because in the absence of the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relationship that is to be indicated, the employment of <s>iva</s> and the like would be unwarranted — anticipating this objection, he said: 'through the attribution of qualities and actions of something else.' A quality (<s>guṇa</s>) is an established property of a substance. An action (<s>kriyā</s>) is that whose nature is to be accomplished. Indeed, this universe

children.text:
svatantraparatantrapadārthātmakatvāddvavidham /
yaśca svatantraḥ padārthaḥ sa dharmītyabhidhīyate /
tacca idaṃ taditi sarvanāmapratyavamarśayogyatvāddravyam /
paratantrasya padārthasya dharmarūpatā /
tasya ca dvaividhyam /
siddhasādhyatābhedāt /
tatra yaḥ siddho dharmaḥ sa guṇaḥ /
yastu sādhyaḥ sā kriyā /
etāvantaśca laukikāḥ padārthāḥ /
sāmānyādīnāmatraiva pratītikena rūpeṇāntarbhūtatvāt /
atra asauprakṛto yor'thastasya ye kriyāguṇā anantaroktalakṣaṇāstadyogātsāmyarūpāvivakṣāyāmapi ivādiśabdapravṛttiravaraddhā /
yatra kilopamānopameyabhāvena sāmyaṃ tatropamānasādṛśyādupamānavartināṃ kriyāguṇānāṃ upameyapratītirbhavati /
utprekṣāyāmapi ca yo 'sāvasaḥ aprakṛtastasya ye kriyāguṇāste tasminnaprakṛte vastunyupamānatayānulliṅgite 'pi prakṛte vastunyāsajyante /
tenātadguṇakrayāyogādasyā ivādivācyatvam /
ata evānyadharmāṇāṃ svadharmibhūtādvastuna utkalitānāṃ rasabhāvadyabhivyaktayanuguṇatayāvastvantarādhyastatvena labdhaprakarṣāṇāmīkṣaṇādiyamutprekṣā /
nanvevamapi sutarāmasaṃbhavaḥ /
na hi vastvantaradharmā vastvantare samāsaktuṃ śakyā ityāśaṅkyoktam---atiśayānviteti /
purāṇaprajāpativahitarūpavaparyāsena kavivedhasā padārthasya guṇātiśayavivakṣayā rūpāntaramapyāsaktuṃ śakyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: is of two kinds, consisting of independent and dependent objects. That which is an independent object is called the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>). And that, being worthy of being indicated by pronouns such as 'this' and 'that,' is a substance (<s>dravya</s>). The dependent object has the nature of a property (<s>dharma</s>). And that is of two kinds, by the distinction of established and to-be-accomplished. Therein, the established property is a quality (<s>guṇa</s>). That which is to be accomplished is an action (<s>kriyā</s>). And these are the extent of worldly objects, since universals and the like are included here in their cognizable form. Here, the qualities and actions — having the characteristics just described — of the object that is not the subject at hand (<s>aprakṛta</s>), through their attribution, even when the desire to express the form of similarity is absent, the employment of words like <s>iva</s> is unimpeded. For where similarity is [expressed] through the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relationship, the cognition of the qualities and actions of the <s>upamāna</s> with respect to the <s>upameya</s> arises from the similarity to the <s>upamāna</s>. In <s>utprekṣā</s> too, the qualities and actions of that which is not the subject (<s>aprakṛta</s>) — those are attributed to the subject (<s>prakṛta</s>) even though the non-subject thing is not indicated as an <s>upamāna</s>. Therefore, through the attribution of qualities and actions of something else, this [figure] is expressible by <s>iva</s> and the like. For this very reason, this <s>utprekṣā</s> arises from the perception of properties of another entity — properties that are drawn forth from their own property-possessor, that conform to the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), and the like, and that have obtained excellence by being superimposed on another entity. Now, even so, the impossibility [of occurrence] is all the more [evident]. For the properties of one entity cannot be attached to another — anticipating this objection, he said: 'endowed with surpassing [beauty].' The meaning is: through the desire to express an excellence of quality in the object, even another form can be attached by the poet-creator, through the reversal of the form established by the ancient Creator.

children.text:
iyaṃ cotprekṣā bahirasaṃbhavataḥ padārthasya saṃbhavadrūpatayopavarṇanāllokātikrāntaviṣayā saṃbhāvanā /
tasyāśca dvaividhyam, bhāvasyābhāvasya ca bahirasaṃbhavata upavarṇyamānatvāt /
tadāha----
children.translated_text: And this <s>utprekṣā</s> is a supposition (<s>saṃbhāvanā</s>) pertaining to a domain that transcends the ordinary world, since an object that is externally impossible is described as having a possible form. And it is twofold, because both an existent thing (<s>bhāva</s>) and a non-existent thing (<s>abhāva</s>) are described as externally impossible. He says:
This supposition, pertaining to a domain that transcends the ordinary world, [arises] from the imagining of existence or non-existence —

children.text: yeyaṃ lokātikrāntaviṣayā saṃbhāvanā utprekṣā sā bhāvasyābhāvasya cābhimānāt dvaividhyaṃ bhajata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: this supposition that pertains to a domain transcending the ordinary world — [which is] <s>utprekṣā</s> — becomes twofold from the imagining of existence and of non-existence.
Now, if <s>utprekṣā</s> is said to occur when there is the binding of <s>iva</s> and the like,
then in [the verse] 'Infused by the breath of serpents clinging to sandalwood,
this <s>Malaya</s> breeze causes travelers to swoon in spring' —
and other such [cases], since <s>iva</s> and the like are not employed, the absurd consequence of there being no <s>utprekṣā</s> would follow — anticipating this objection, he says:
it is expressed by <s>iva</s> and the like when expressible. [UKss 3.4]

children.text:
dvividhā khalūtprekṣā /
kācidivādiprayoge sati bhavati, kācittvaprayujyamāneṣvapīvādīṣvarthasāmarthyādagamyamāneṣu /
tatra yā vācyā svakaṇṭhenevādibhirvaktavyā sā ivādībhirucyate /
yā tvarthasāmarthyakṣiptairivādibhiravagamte tatrevādīnāmaprayogaḥ /
'candanāsaktabhujaga'ityādau ca malayamārutasya yadetanmanmathāvirbhāvanibandhanatvātpathikamūrcchāhetutvaṃ tatra bhujaganiśvāsamūrcchitatve kāraṇatvenotprekṣyamāṇe ivādyarthor'thasāmarthyādavagamyate /
tenevādīnāmaprayogaḥ /
ivādiśabdasāmarthyāvaseyāyāmevotprekṣāyāmivādīnāṃ prayogāt /
tatra bhāvābhimānenotprekṣāyāṃ tasyā guṇayogādhyāsena pravṛttāyā udāharaṇam---
children.translated_text: <s>Utprekṣā</s> is indeed of two kinds. One arises when <s>iva</s> and the like are employed; the other, even when <s>iva</s> and the like are not employed, is understood through the force of meaning. Therein, that which is expressible — to be stated by one's own voice through <s>iva</s> and the like — is expressed by <s>iva</s> and the like. But that which is understood through <s>iva</s> and the like implied by the force of meaning — there, <s>iva</s> and the like are not employed. And in 'serpents clinging to sandalwood' and the like, the fact that the <s>Malaya</s> breeze causes travelers to swoon because it is the occasion for the manifestation of <s>Kāma</s> (love) — when the cause [of the swooning] is fancied as being the breath of serpents — the meaning of <s>iva</s> and the like is understood through the force of meaning. Therefore, <s>iva</s> and the like are not employed. [They are employed] only in the <s>utprekṣā</s> that is to be understood through the force of the word <s>iva</s> and the like, since <s>iva</s> and the like are [then] employed. An example of the <s>utprekṣā</s> that proceeds from the imagining of existence, operating through the superimposition of a quality:
By her prayers (<s>japa</s>), with gazes ever fixed on the orb of the sun, drinking the heat as it were,
a dark mark fell on her face, as if from the delusion of the moon. [UKss 3.*2]

children.text:
asyā mukhe japairhetubhūtaiḥ śyāmikāṅkena patitamiti saṃbandhaḥ /
atra japāsaktā bhagavatī arkamavalokayatīti tasyāḥ śaśāṅkasadṛse mukhe śyāmikā saṃjātā /
taccātra tasyāḥ śyamikāyā janma atiśayoktyā pātarūpatayā pratipāditaṃ patitamiti /
sā cātra śyāmika śaśilāñchanena śaśena tulyā /
atastasyāḥ śaśilāñchanaśaśatulyatvādupasarjanopameyaṃrūpakaṃ śyāmikaivāṅka ityupanibaddham /
tasya cāṅkasya śyāmikoparaktasya bhagavatīvadananipāte kāraṇatvenendubhrāntirutprekṣitā /
yadetacchaśino lāñchanaṃ śyāmikārūpaṃ tadbhagavatīvadana indubhrāntyeva nipatitamiti /
indubhrāntiśca guṇaḥ /
siddharūpatve sati dravyadharmatvāt /
evaṃ cātra śaśasadṛśī śyāmikā caitanyaśūnyatvena bhagavatīvadanamindubhrāntyā na gocarīkaroti /
atha ca tasyāḥ śaśabhāvamāpāditāyā indubhramalakṣaṇena cetanadharmeṇa saṃbandho nibaddhaḥ /
tenātra tasya vastvantarasya cetanasya yo 'sau guṇo bhramalakṣaṇastadyogādivādeḥ pravṛttiḥ /
indubhramaśca bhāvarūpo guṇaḥ śaśīkṛtaśyamikākartṛkatayā kavinibaddhena vaktrā bhagavatābhimānenādhyavasitaḥ /
teneyamatadguṇayogena bhāvābhimānena utprekṣā /
children.translated_text: The connection is: a dark mark fell on her face, caused by her prayers. Here, the Goddess, devoted to her prayers, gazes at the sun, and thereby a dark spot (<s>śyāmikā</s>) has appeared on her face that resembles the moon. And here, the arising of that dark spot is presented through <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) in the form of falling — 'it fell.' And here, that dark spot is similar to the hare that is the mark of the moon. Therefore, since the dark spot is similar to the hare-mark of the moon, a subordinate <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) of the <s>upameya</s> is constructed: 'the dark spot itself is a mark' (<s>śyāmikā eva aṅkaḥ</s>). And for that mark — colored by the dark spot — the delusion of the moon is fancied as the cause of its falling on the Goddess's face. That is: this mark of the moon in the form of a dark spot fell on the Goddess's face through the delusion of [taking her face for] the moon. And the delusion of the moon is a quality — because it is a property of a substance while having an established form. And thus here, the dark spot, being devoid of consciousness, like the hare, does not make the Goddess's face the object [of its action] through the delusion of the moon. Yet, after the dark spot has been made to assume the nature of the hare, a connection with the property of a conscious being — characterized by delusion — has been constructed. Therefore, here, through the attribution of the quality of delusion belonging to another entity — a conscious one — the employment of <s>iva</s> occurs. And the delusion of the moon is a quality of the nature of existence (<s>bhāva</s>), determined through the imagining of the speaker, the Blessed One, who was composed by the poet as the agent, with the dark spot having been made into [the hare of] the moon. Therefore this is an <s>utprekṣā</s> through the imagining of existence, by the attribution of a quality.

children.text:
evaṃ kriyāyogādhyāsādbhāvābhimānena yotprekṣā tasyāmudāhāryam /
abhāvaviṣayāyāḥ punaḥ kriyādhyāsena pravṛttāyāstasyā udāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: Similarly, an example should be given for the <s>utprekṣā</s> that proceeds from the imagining of existence through the superimposition of an action. An example of the [utprekṣā] that pertains to non-existence, operating through the superimposition of an action:
The two cheek-surfaces of hers, having become thus,
having reached such a state of emaciation, as if not seeing each other — alas! [UKss 3.*3]

children.text:
atra kapolaphalakayostapovaśāt kṣāmatvamāpannayoḥ parasparādarśanamabhāvarūpaṃ sādhyatvāt kriyārūpakṣāmatāyāṃ kāraṇatayotprekṣitam /
teneyamataktriyāyogādabhāvābhimānenotprekṣā /
evamatadguṇayogādabhāvābhimānena yā utprekṣā tasyāmudāhāryam /
children.translated_text: Here, since the non-seeing of each other by the two cheek-surfaces that have become emaciated due to the power of <s>tapas</s> (austerity) is something to be established as being of the nature of absence, the emaciation, which is of the nature of action, is imagined as a cause [of that non-seeing]. Therefore this is an <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) through the supposition of absence due to the inapplicability of such action. Similarly, the <s>utprekṣā</s> through the supposition of absence due to the inapplicability of such a quality should be illustrated.
<s>Svabhāvokti</s> (description of natural behavior) —
The portrayal of the characteristic gestures (<s>hevāka</s>) of some [creature] such as a fawn, etc.,
engaged in an activity, is declared to be <s>svabhāvokti</s> (description of natural behavior). [UKss 3.5]

children.text:
bhṛgabālādeḥ svasamucite vyāpāre pravṛttasya ye hevākāḥ svajātyānurūpyeṇābhiniveśaviśeṣāstadupanibandhaḥ svabhāvoktiḥ /
tasyāścālaṅkāratvamasādhāraṇapadārthasvarūpadhvananāt /
tasyā udāharaṇam-----
children.translated_text: <s>Svabhāvokti</s> is the portrayal of the <s>hevākas</s> — the distinctive mannerisms conforming to one's own species — of a young deer and the like engaged in an activity proper to its own nature. And its status as an <s>alaṃkāra</s> (ornament) is due to its suggesting the essential nature of an uncommon object. An illustration of that —
Sniffing for a moment, half-turned, pushing forward with his horn for a moment,
this young deer (<s>mṛgārbhaka</s>) playfully fusses over her out of affection. [UKss 3.*4]
<s>Naṃṣṭvā</s> means 'having sniffed.'
Since the elision of the nasal is optionally prescribed by the rule '<s>jāntanaśāṃ vibhāṣā</s>,' the non-application [of the elision rule here is justified].

children.text: atra mṛgapotakasya mātaramiva vatsalāṃ bhagavatīṃ praṇayanirbhareṇa cerasā vyākulīkurvataḥ svabhāvo nibaddhaḥ kṣaṇamaparidṛśyamānatvamardhakāyena parivṛttiḥ śṛṅgeṇa ca nodanamityevamātmā //
children.translated_text: Here, the natural behavior of the young deer is depicted — of one who, with gestures full of affection, fusses over the revered lady as if she were his own mother: momentary disappearance from view, half-turning of the body, and pushing with his horn — such is his nature.
Thus ends the third <s>varga</s> (chapter) in the <s>Laghuvivṛtti</s> (concise commentary) on the <s>Udbhaṭālaṅkārasārasaṃgraha</s>, composed by <s>Śrīmahāpratīhāra Indurāja</s>.
Now, the fourth <s>varga</s> (chapter).
<s>Preyas</s> (the endearing), <s>rasavat</s> (the sapid), <s>ūrjasvin</s> (the vigorous), <s>paryāyokta</s> (the circumlocutory), <s>samāhita</s> (the composed),
<s>udātta</s> (the exalted) of two kinds, and likewise <s>śliṣṭa</s> (the polished) — these are the <s>alaṃkāras</s> (ornaments) recognized by the learned. [UKss 4.1]

children.text:
preyorasavaditi samudāyānmatup /
śliṣṭamiti /
tathā udāttavaddvavidhaṃ śliṣṭamityarthaḥ /
vipratipattinirāsārthaṃ cātra śliṣṭasya dvaividhyamuktam /

children.translated_text: For <s>Bhāmaha</s> states: 'it is threefold, due to co-expression (<s>sahoktya</s>), simile (<s>upamā</s>), and statement of cause (<s>hetunirdeśa</s>)' — thus declaring <s>śliṣṭa</s> to be threefold.
Therefore, 'likewise' (<s>tathā</s>) is said in order to refute the contrary opinion.
As for <s>udātta</s>, 'of two kinds' is a restatement for the purpose of providing an example.

children.text: yathā udāttasya dvaividhyaṃ pramāṇopapannatvādaṅgīkṛtaṃ tathā śliṣṭasyāpi tadaṅgīkartavyamityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: just as the twofold nature of <s>udātta</s> is accepted because it is established by authority, so too the twofold nature of <s>śliṣṭa</s> should be accepted.

'<s>Preyas</s>, <s>rasavat</s>' — the <s>matup</s> suffix applies to the group as a whole. '<s>Śliṣṭam</s>' — the meaning is: just as <s>udātta</s> is twofold, so too <s>śliṣṭa</s> is twofold. And here the twofold nature of <s>śliṣṭa</s> is stated in order to refute a contrary opinion.
First, <s>preyas</s> (the endearing) —
That poetry which is composed by the learned through indications such as <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent expressions) and the like
of the <s>bhāvas</s> (emotional states) such as <s>rati</s> (love) and others, is declared to be <s>preyas</s> (the endearing). [UKss 4.2]

The <s>bhāvas</s> such as <s>rati</s> (love) and others are of three kinds: <s>sthāyins</s> (permanent emotions), <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions), and <s>sātvikas</s> (involuntary physical reactions).
Among these: '<s>Rati</s> (love), <s>hāsa</s> (mirth), <s>śoka</s> (sorrow), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>utsāha</s> (energy), <s>bhaya</s> (fear),
<s>jugupsā</s> (disgust), and <s>vismaya</s> (wonder) — these are proclaimed as the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> (permanent emotions).
<s>Nirveda</s> (despondency), <s>glāni</s> (languor), <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), likewise <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), <s>śrama</s> (fatigue),

children.text: ālasyaṃ caiva dainyaṃ ca cintā mohaḥ smṛtirdhṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>ālasya</s> (indolence), <s>dainya</s> (wretchedness), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection), <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness),

children.text: vrīḍā capalata harṣa āvego jaḍatā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>vrīḍā</s> (shame), <s>capalatā</s> (fickleness), <s>harṣa</s> (joy), <s>āvega</s> (agitation), <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupefaction),

children.text: garvo viṣāda autsukyaṃ nidrāpasmāra eva ca //
children.translated_text: <s>garva</s> (arrogance), <s>viṣāda</s> (despondency), <s>autsukyam</s> (longing), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), and <s>apasmāra</s> (epilepsy),
<s>supta</s> (dreaming), <s>vibodha</s> (awakening), <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation), <s>avahittha</s> (dissimulation), and <s>ugratā</s> (ferocity),
<s>mati</s> (discernment), <s>vyādhi</s> (sickness), likewise <s>unmāda</s> (insanity), and also <s>maraṇa</s> (death),
and
<s>trāsa</s> (fright) and <s>vitarka</s> (conjecture) — these are to be known as the <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions).
These <s>bhāvas</s> are thirty-three in number.'
'<s>Stambha</s> (stupor), <s>sveda</s> (perspiration), <s>romāñca</s> (horripilation), <s>svarabheda</s> (voice-change), <s>vepathu</s> (trembling),
<s>vaivarṇya</s> (change of color), <s>aśru</s> (tears), and <s>pralaya</s> (fainting) — these eight are declared as <s>sātvika</s> (involuntary physical reactions).'

children.text:
eteṣāṃ pañcāśatsaṃkhyānāṃ bhāvānāṃ sūcakāścatvāro 'nubhāvādayaḥ /
te cānubhāvo vibhāvo vyabhicārī svaśabdaśca /
children.translated_text: Of these fifty <s>bhāvas</s>, there are four indicators beginning with <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent expression). These are: <s>anubhāva</s>, <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant), <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion), and <s>svaśabda</s> (the [emotion's] own name).

children.text:
tatrānubhāvaścaturvidhaḥ /
āṅgiko vācikaḥ sāttvika āhāryaśca /
āṅgiko hastābhinayādiḥ /

children.translated_text: The <s>vācika</s> is the employment of vocal intonation (<s>kāku</s>) and the like.
The <s>sāttvika</s> is stupor (<s>stambha</s>) and the like.
The <s>āhārya</s> is the use of head-ornaments (<s>pratiśīrṣa</s>), jackets (<s>kañcuka</s>), and the like.
Thus, this fourfold <s>anubhāva</s>, being an effect, leads to the cognition of the <s>bhāvas</s> (emotional states) that are its causes.

Among these, <s>anubhāva</s> is fourfold: <s>āṅgika</s> (gestural), <s>vācika</s> (verbal), <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary), and <s>āhārya</s> (artificial). The <s>āṅgika</s> is hand-gestures (<s>hastābhinaya</s>) and the like.

children.text:
vibhāvastu dvividhaḥ /
ālambanoddīpanarūpatvāt /
tatrālamvanavibhāvo yadāśrayeṇa ratyādīnāmudayaḥ, yathā rāmādeḥ sītādiḥ /
uddīpanavibhāvastu yadvaśena ratyādīnāṃ bhāvānāmatiśayena dīptatā bhavati, yathā ṛtumālyānulepanādiḥ /
evameṣa dvividho vibhāvo ratyādīnāṃ kāraṇabhūtaḥ /
sa ca kāraṇatvātkāryabhūtān ratyādīn
children.translated_text: The <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) is twofold, being of the nature of <s>ālambana</s> (foundational) and <s>uddīpana</s> (stimulating). Among these, the <s>ālambanavibhāva</s> is that by whose support the arising of <s>rati</s> (love) and other [emotions] occurs — for example, <s>Sītā</s> and others in relation to <s>Rāma</s> and others. The <s>uddīpanavibhāva</s> is that by whose influence there is an intensification of the <s>bhāvas</s> such as <s>rati</s> etc. — for example, the season, garlands, ointments, and the like. Thus this twofold <s>vibhāva</s> is the cause of <s>rati</s> and the other [emotions]. And being a cause, it leads to the cognition of its effects — <s>rati</s> and the others —

children.text:
gamayati yathātibahalanīlajaladodayo vṛṣṭim /
yathā hi kāryasya suvivecitasya kāraṇaṃ pratyavyabhicāritā evaṃ kāraṇasyāpi suvivecitasya kāryaṃ pratyavyabhicāritā vyavahāre bāhulyena dṛśyate /
ato vibhāvaḥ kāraṇatvāt ratyādīnkāryabhūtān gamayati /
vyabhicārī tu ratyādikānāṃ sthāyināṃ bhāvānāmavasthāviśeṣarūpo nirvedādiḥ /
sa ca sahacāritvāt sthāyināṃ bhāvānāmavasthāviśeṣarūpo nirvedādiḥ /
sa ca sahacāritvāt sthāyino bhāvānpratapādayati rathasyaikamiva cakraṃ cakrāntaram /
svaśabdastu ratyādiḥ /
sa ca vācakatvādbhāvān gamayati /
ratyādīnāṃ ca śabdānāṃ yadyapyanubhāvaikagocarasvalakṣaṇasvabhāvaratyādyavagatinibandhanatvaṃ nopalabhyate, tathāpyaṃśena ratyādyavagatinibandhanatvamanubhāvādivadvidyata eva /
yathā khalvanubhāvādayo na svalakṣaṇatayā bhāvānavagamayanti apitu sāmānyarūpatayā tadvatsvaśabdā apītyāstām /
children.translated_text: just as a very dense dark cloud indicates rain. For just as there is an invariable concomitance between a well-ascertained effect and its cause, so too the invariable concomitance between a well-ascertained cause and its effect is abundantly seen in common experience. Therefore, the <s>vibhāva</s>, being a cause, leads to the cognition of <s>rati</s> and other [emotions] that are its effects. The <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion), however, is a particular state of the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent) <s>bhāvas</s> such as <s>rati</s> etc. — namely <s>nirveda</s> (despondency) and the like. And being a concomitant, it indicates the <s>sthāyin</s> <s>bhāvas</s>, just as one wheel of a chariot [indicates] the other wheel. The <s>svaśabda</s> (own name) is '<s>rati</s>' and the like. And it leads to the cognition of the <s>bhāvas</s> by virtue of being their designating word. And even though it is not found that the words '<s>rati</s>' etc. have as their basis for cognizing <s>rati</s> etc. their own characteristic nature, which pertains exclusively to the domain of <s>anubhāva</s>, nevertheless, partially, their being a basis for cognizing <s>rati</s> etc. does exist, just like <s>anubhāva</s> and the others. For just as <s>anubhāvas</s> etc. do not lead to the cognition of <s>bhāvas</s> through their particular nature but through their general nature, so too do the <s>svaśabdas</s> (own names) — but enough of this.

children.text:
evamete bhāvānāmavagatihetavaścātvāraḥ /
yaduktaṃ bhaṭṭodbhaṭena "catūrūpā bhāvā"iti /
tadeṣāṃ ratyādikānāṃ bhāvānāṃ pañcāśatsaṃkhyānāṃ yānyanubhāvādibhiścatuḥsaṃkhyaiḥ samastatvena vyastatvena ca yathāyogaṃ sūcanāni svalakṣaṇasvarūpāṇāṃ sāmānyāvasthāpāditānāṃ pratipādanāni taiḥ kāvyamupanibadhyamānaṃ preyasvat /
preyaḥśabdavācyena priyatareṇa ratyālambanena vibhāvanena ratirupalakṣyate /
tayā ca sāhacaryādratyādayo bhāvāḥ pañcāśadavagamyante /
evaṃ ca bhāvakāvyasya preyasvaditi lakṣaṇayā vyapadeśaḥ /
atra ca bhāvānāmalaṅkāratā, kāvyamalaṅkāryam /
tasyodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: Thus, these four are the means of cognizing the <s>bhāvas</s>. As <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s> (Master <s>Udbhaṭa</s>) has said: 'the <s>bhāvas</s> have four forms.' Accordingly, the poetry that is composed through the indications — collectively and individually, as appropriate — by means of these four, namely <s>anubhāva</s> and the rest, of the fifty <s>bhāvas</s> beginning with <s>rati</s>, whose particular natures have been established in their general form, that is <s>preyas</s> (the endearing). By the word <s>preyas</s>, which means 'dearer,' i.e. the object of love (<s>ratyālambana</s>), <s>rati</s> is figuratively indicated through being its <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant). And through association with <s>rati</s>, the fifty <s>bhāvas</s> beginning with <s>rati</s> are cognized. Thus, the designation of a poem centered on <s>bhāvas</s> as '<s>preyas</s>' is through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification). And here, the <s>bhāvas</s> are the <s>alaṃkāras</s> (ornaments); the poem is what is ornamented. An illustration of that —
And she, out of motherly affection for her child (<s>sutavātsalya</s>), impartially desirous,
began to soothe [the young deer], having placed him on her own lap. [UKss 4.*1]

children.text:
ātmanaḥ kroḍe kṛtveti saṃbandhaḥ /
atrātmano vakṣasi nidhānamāṅgīko 'bhinayaḥ, ullāpanaṃ sāntvanaṃ vācikaḥ /
imamiti idaṃśabdena parāmṛṣṭo yo mṛgārbhakaḥ sa ālambanavibhāvaḥ /
vātsalyonmīlitaścautsukyātmā vyabhicārībhāvaḥ /
sutavāllabhyanirviśeṣatvena hi spṛhāyā
children.translated_text: The syntactic connection is: 'having placed [him] on her own lap.' Here, the placing on her own breast is the <s>āṅgika</s> (gestural) <s>abhinaya</s> (enactment); the soothing (<s>ullāpana</s>) is the <s>vācika</s> (verbal) [enactment]. The young deer, referred to by the word '<s>imam</s>' (this one), is the <s>ālambanavibhāva</s> (foundational determinant). The <s>vyabhicāribhāva</s> (transitory emotion) is longing (<s>autsukyātman</s>), aroused by maternal affection (<s>vātsalya</s>). For through the impartiality of her desire in comparison with her own child,

children.text:
raterautsukyabhedābhisaṃbandhaḥ pratīyate /
svaśabdastu spṛheti /
evamayaṃ ratyātmako bhāvo vātsalyasvabhāvaścaturbhiranubhāvādibhiratrāvagamitaḥ /
anyeṣvapi bhāveṣvevamudāhāryam /
children.translated_text: the connection of <s>rati</s> (love) with the modification of longing (<s>autsukyabheda</s>) is implied. The <s>svaśabda</s> (own name) is '<s>spṛhā</s>' (desire). Thus this <s>bhāva</s>, whose essence is <s>rati</s> (love) and whose nature is maternal affection (<s>vātsalya</s>), has been here made cognizable through the four [means] beginning with <s>anubhāva</s>. The same should be illustrated for other <s>bhāvas</s> as well.
<s>Rasavat</s> (the sapid) —
<s>Rasavat</s> is that [poetry] which clearly displays the <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) such as <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) and others,
grounded in <s>svaśabda</s> (own name), <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion), <s>saṃcārin</s> (transitory emotion), <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant), and <s>abhinaya</s> (enactment). [UKss 4.3]
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic), <s>hāsya</s> (the comic), <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic), <s>raudra</s> (the furious), <s>vīra</s> (the heroic), <s>bhayānaka</s> (the terrible),

children.text: bībhatsādbhutaśāntāśca nava nāṭye rasāḥ smṛtāḥ // UKss_4.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>bībhatsa</s> (the odious), <s>adbhuta</s> (the marvelous), and <s>śānta</s> (the quiescent) — these nine are recognized as the <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) in drama (<s>nāṭya</s>). [UKss 4.4]

children.text:
ete ca śṛṅgārādayo nava yathāyogaṃ caturvargaprāptyupāyatayā taditaraparihāranibandhanataya ca ratyādīnāṃ sthāyināṃ navānāṃ bhāvānāṃ yaḥ paripoṣastadātmakāḥ /
atastathāvidhena rūpeṇāsvādyatvādāsvādabhedanibandhanena tāntrikeṇa rasaśabdenābhidhīyante /

children.translated_text: But in the case of <s>nirveda</s> (despondency) and the like, since there is no such savorable [quality], the technical term <s>rasa</s>, which is based on the distinction of its occasion for operation, does not apply.

However, if one intends merely the quality of being savorable, then even there the application of the term <s>rasa</s> is not contradictory, just as [the term applies to flavors] such as sweet, sour, and the like.

As has been stated, after enumerating the <s>rasas</s> beginning with <s>śṛṅgāra</s>: 'The <s>rasatva</s> (quality of being a <s>rasa</s>) of these has been stated by the teachers to be like that of sweet and other [flavors].
In <s>nirveda</s> and the like too, that [quality of being savored] abundantly exists — therefore they too are <s>rasas</s>.'

These nine, beginning with <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, are respectively of the nature of the full development (<s>paripoṣa</s>) of the nine <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent) <s>bhāvas</s> beginning with <s>rati</s> (love), which serve as the means of attaining the four goals of life (<s>caturvarga</s>) and as the basis for avoiding things other than those. Therefore, because they are savored (<s>āsvādya</s>) in that particular form, they are designated by the term <s>rasa</s>, which is a technical term based on the distinction of savoring (<s>āsvādabheda</s>).
On this, they say —
That through which the two [goals] other than the <s>caturvarga</s> (four aims of life) are respectively attained or to be avoided,
which, due to the distinction of consciousness (<s>caitanyabheda</s>), is savorable — that is regarded as <s>rasa</s> of such a nature.
Thus.

children.text:
sa iti /
caitanyabheda ityarthaḥ /
tādṛśa ityanena āsvādaviśeṣanibandhanatvaṃ śṛṅgarādiṣu tāntrikasya rasaśabdasyoktam /
eṣāṃ ca śṛṅgārādīnāṃ navānāṃ rasānāṃ svaśabdādibhiḥ pañcabhiravagatirbhavati /
yaduktaṃ bhaṭṭodbhaṭena--"pañcarūpā rasā"iti /
tatra svaśabdāḥ śṛṅgārādervācakāḥ śṛṅgārādayaḥ śabdāḥ /
sthāyino rasānāmupādānakāraṇaprakhyā ratyādayo nava bhāvāḥ /
saṃcāriṇastu nirvedādayo rasānāmavasthāviśeṣarūpāḥ /
vibhāvāstu teṣāṃ nimittakāraṇabhūtā yoṣidādayaḥ ṛtumālyānulepanādayaśca /
āṅgikādayastu catvāro rasānāṃ kāryabhūtā abhinayāḥ /
eteṣāṃ ca svaśabdādīnāṃ pañcānāṃ samastavyastatayā āspadatvādyena kāvyena sphuṭarūpatayā śṛṅgārādirasāvirbhāvo darśyate tatkāvyaṃ rasavat /
rasāḥ khalu tasyālaṅkārāḥ /
tasyodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: 'That' — the meaning is: due to the distinction of consciousness (<s>caitanyabheda</s>). By 'of such a nature,' the basis of the technical term <s>rasa</s> in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and the like is stated to be the distinction of savoring (<s>āsvādaviśeṣa</s>). And the cognition of these nine <s>rasas</s> beginning with <s>śṛṅgāra</s> arises through five [means] beginning with <s>svaśabda</s> (own name). As <s>Bhaṭṭodbhaṭa</s> (Master <s>Udbhaṭa</s>) has said: 'the <s>rasas</s> have five forms.' Among these, the <s>svaśabdas</s> are the words designating <s>śṛṅgāra</s> etc., namely the words '<s>śṛṅgāra</s>' and the like. The <s>sthāyins</s> (permanent emotions), resembling the material cause (<s>upādānakāraṇa</s>) of the <s>rasas</s>, are the nine <s>bhāvas</s> beginning with <s>rati</s>. The <s>saṃcārins</s> (transitory emotions) are <s>nirveda</s> and the like, being particular states of the <s>rasas</s>. The <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) are women and the like, and seasons, garlands, ointments, and the like, being the efficient causes of those [<s>rasas</s>]. The four <s>abhinayas</s> (enactments) beginning with <s>āṅgika</s> (gestural) are the effects of the <s>rasas</s>. The poetry in which the manifestation of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and the other <s>rasas</s> is shown clearly, through the collectively and individually serving as the basis of these five beginning with <s>svaśabda</s>, that poetry is <s>rasavat</s> (sapid). Indeed, the <s>rasas</s> are its <s>alaṃkāras</s> (ornaments). An illustration of that —
Thus, as he contemplated all the virtues of <s>Pārvatī</s>,
<s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love), having gathered his full resolve, grew mighty. [UKss 4.*2]
Though his body was perspiring, he bore a mass of horripilation (<s>pulakotkara</s>),
resembling an abundance of filaments from buds of <s>kadamba</s> flowers. [UKss 4.*3]
At one moment by a gaze pregnant with longing (<s>autsukyagarbhiṇī</s>), at another moment by one still with thought (<s>cintāniścala</s>),
at another moment by one languid with delight (<s>pramodālasa</s>) — her face adorned his face. [UKss 4.*4]

children.text:
kadambakalikākośaḥ kadambakalikābhyantaram /
atra bhagavata ābhilāṣikavipralambhaśṛṅgāro nibaddhaḥ /
tasya svaśabdaḥ 'kandarpaḥ prabala'iti /
sthāyī tatraiva svaśabdenonmīlitaḥ kandarpa iti /
ratiparipoṣātmako hi śṛṅgāro rasaḥ /
ratiśca yūnāṃ manmathātmikā /
ato rativiśeṣasya vācakatvātkandarpaśabdaḥ sthāyino 'tra svaśabdaḥ /
saṃcāriṇaścautsukyacintāharṣāḥ svaśabdenonmīlitāḥ. svedaromāñcau ca sātvikau svaśabdopāttau /
tayorapi ca saṃcāritvam /
sātvikānāṃ sthāyibhāvāvasthāviśeṣatvena nirvedādivatsaṃcāritvāt /
vibhāvastu 'iti bhāvayatastasya'iti nirdiṣṭaḥ /
bhagavatī hi tattadguṇopetatvena vibhāvyamānā vibhāvaḥ /
abhinayastvatrāpāṅgābhinayo nirdiṣṭo 'dṛśā'iti /
ato 'trābhilāṣikaḥ śṛṅgārarasaḥ svaśabdādibhiḥ pañcabhirabhivyajyate /
evamanye 'pi rasā udāhāryāḥ /
rasānāṃ bhāvānāṃ ca kāvyaśobhātiśayahetutvāt kiṃ kāvyālaṅkāratvamuta kāvyajīvitatvamiti na
