children.translated_text: '<s>Kadambakalikākośa</s>' means the interior of <s>kadamba</s> flower buds. Here, the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) of the Lord in the mode of <s>ābhilāṣikavipralambha</s> (love-in-longing-separation) is depicted. Its <s>svaśabda</s> (own name) is '<s>kandarpaḥ prabala</s>' (love grew mighty). The <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) is revealed therein by the <s>svaśabda</s> itself — '<s>kandarpa</s>' (love) — for the <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s> consists in the full development of <s>rati</s> (love), and <s>rati</s> among lovers is of the nature of <s>manmatha</s> (desire). Therefore, the word '<s>kandarpa</s>,' being the designator of this particular form of <s>rati</s>, is here the <s>svaśabda</s> of the <s>sthāyin</s>. The <s>saṃcārins</s> (transitory emotions) — longing (<s>autsukyam</s>), thought (<s>cintā</s>), and joy (<s>harṣa</s>) — are revealed by their own names. Perspiration (<s>sveda</s>) and horripilation (<s>romāñca</s>) are the two <s>sātvika</s> (involuntary) [reactions], taken up by their own names. And these two also function as <s>saṃcārins</s> (transitory emotions), since <s>sātvika</s> reactions, being particular states of the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s>, are <s>saṃcārins</s> like <s>nirveda</s> and the rest. The <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) is indicated by '<s>iti bhāvayatas tasya</s>' (as he thus contemplated), for the revered lady, being conceived as endowed with various virtues, is the <s>vibhāva</s>. The <s>abhinaya</s> (enactment) here is the glance-enactment (<s>apāṅgābhinaya</s>), indicated by the word '<s>dṛśā</s>' (with a glance). Therefore, here the <s>ābhilāṣika śṛṅgāra rasa</s> (erotic sentiment in the mode of longing) is manifested through the five [means] beginning with <s>svaśabda</s>. Other <s>rasas</s> too should be similarly illustrated. Since <s>rasas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s> are the cause of the superexcellence of beauty in poetry, whether they constitute the <s>alaṃkāra</s> (ornament) of poetry or the very life of poetry — that
is not discussed here, for fear of making the treatise too lengthy.
And the essential nature of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s> has not been analyzed here, since it is not the subject at hand and since much would have to be said.
<s>Ūrjasvin</s> (the vigorous) —
When <s>bhāvas</s> (emotional states) and <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) that have arisen improperly,

children.text: bhāvānāṃ ca rasānāṃ ca bandha ūrjasvi kathyate // UKss_4.5 //
children.translated_text: due to <s>kāma</s> (desire), <s>krodha</s> (anger), and the like, are depicted — that is called <s>ūrjasvin</s> (the vigorous). [UKss 4.5]

children.text:
kvacitkhalu rasabhāvānāṃ śāstrasaṃvidaviruddhena rūpeṇopanibandhaḥ kriyate, kvacittu tadviruddhena /
tatra yatra śāstrasaṃvidaviruddhena rūpeṇa teṣāmupanibandhastatra preyo 'laṅkāro rasavadalaṅkāraścābhihitaḥ /
yatra tu tadviruddhatvaṃ tanmūlakalokavyavahāraviruddhatvaṃ ca tadviṣayāṇāṃ rasabhāvanāmupanibandhe satyūrjasvikāvyaṃ bhavati /
tatra hi rāgadveṣamohakāraṇakā anaucityena rasabhāvā upanibadhyante /
ata eva tatra svakalpanāparikalpitatvena ūrjaso balasya vidyāmānatvādūrjakhivyapadeśaḥ /
'jyotsnātamisre'tyatra urjasviśabdaḥ (pā. a. 5 / 2 / 114) //
children.translated_text: Sometimes, the depiction of <s>rasas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s> is carried out in a form not contrary to the conventions of <s>śāstra</s> (treatise), and sometimes in a form contrary to them. Where their depiction is in a form not contrary to the conventions of <s>śāstra</s>, there the <s>preyas</s> (endearing) <s>alaṃkāra</s> and the <s>rasavat</s> (sapid) <s>alaṃkāra</s> have been described. But where there is contrariety to those [conventions] and contrariety to the worldly conduct that is rooted in them — when <s>rasas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s> pertaining to such a subject are depicted, then the poetry is <s>ūrjasvin</s> (vigorous). For there, <s>rasas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s> caused by passion (<s>rāga</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>) are depicted with impropriety (<s>anaucitya</s>). It is precisely for this reason that the designation <s>ūrjasvin</s> applies, because <s>ūrjas</s> (vigor, force) is present there, having been fashioned by the poet's own imagination. [The grammatical derivation follows the pattern of] '<s>jyotsnātamisre</s>' — by which the word <s>ūrjasvin</s> is formed (<s>Pāṇini</s> 5.2.114).
An illustration of that —

children.text: tathā kāmo 'sya vavṛdhe yathā himagireḥ sutām /
children.translated_text: So greatly did his desire grow that toward the daughter of the Snow Mountain (<s>Himagiri</s>),
he proceeded to seize [her] by force, having propitiating <s>Satyaratha</s> [i.e. having used truth as his vehicle]. [UKss 4.*5]

children.text:
atra sakalalokātiśāyino bhagavato 'kṛtavivāhakamārīviṣayatayā haṭhasaṃgrahaḥ śāstrasaṃvidviruddhaḥ pravṛddharāgakāraṇaku upanibaddhaḥ /
tena ūrjastitā /
tatra kāmo vavṛdhe ityayaṃ śṛṅgārasya svaśabdaḥ /
tasya ratiparipoṣātmakatvena kāmavṛddhisvabhāvatvāt kāmaśabdastvetadantargataḥ /
śṛṅgārasya yāsau sthāyibhūtā ratistasyāḥ svaśabdaḥ himagireḥ sutāmityālambanavibhāvaḥ /
haṭhenetyanenāvegalakṣaṇo vyabhicārībhāvaḥ pratipāditaḥ /
apāsya satpathamiti tu mogaḥ, saṃgrahītuṃ pravṛtta iti āṅgako 'nubhāvaḥ /
evamayamatra pañcabhiḥ svaśabdādibhirurjasvilakṣaṇaḥ śṛṅgāraḥ sūcitaḥ /
evamanyeṣvapi rasabhāveṣūrjasvi udāhāryam /
children.translated_text: Here, the forcible seizing (<s>haṭhasaṃgraha</s>) by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who surpasses all worlds, directed toward an unmarried maiden, is contrary to the conventions of <s>śāstra</s>, and is grounded in the cause of intensified passion. Thereby there is <s>ūrjasvitatā</s> (vigor). There, 'desire increased' — this is the proper term (<s>svaśabda</s>) for <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment). Since it has the nature of the nourishment of <s>rati</s> (love) and the nature of the increase of desire, the word <s>kāma</s> is included within it. The proper term for <s>rati</s>, which is the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion) of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, is given; 'the daughter of the <s>Himagiri</s> (Snow Mountain)' is the <s>ālambana-vibhāva</s> (foundational stimulus). By the word 'forcibly' (<s>haṭhena</s>), the <s>vyabhicāribhāva</s> (transitory emotion) characterized by impetuosity is indicated. 'Having abandoned the righteous path' is the <s>moga</s> (fruitless effort), and 'having set out to seize' is the bodily <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent). Thus, here the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> characterized by <s>ūrjasvin</s> (vigor) is indicated by five [elements] beginning with the proper term. In this manner, <s>ūrjasvin</s> should be illustrated in other <s>rasas</s> (sentiments) and <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions) as well.
<s>Paryāyokta</s> (indirect expression) —
<s>Paryāyokta</s> (indirect expression) is that which is expressed by another manner,
devoid of the functions of the denoted and the denoting, having the nature of comprehension. [UKss 4.6]

children.text:
vācakasyābhidhāyakasya svaśabdasya vṛttirvyāpāro vācyārthapratyāyanam /
vācyasya tvabhidheyasya vyāpāro vācyāntareṇa sahākāṅkṣāsaṃnidhiyogyatāmāhātmyātsaṃsargagamanam /
evaṃvidhaśca yo vācyavācakayorvyāpārastamantareṇāpi prakārāntareṇārthasāmarthyātmanāvagamasvabhāvena yadavagamyate tatparyāyeṇa svakaṇṭhānabhihitamapi sāntareṇa śabdavyāpāreṇāvagamyamānatvāt paryāyoktaṃ vastu /
tena ca svasaṃśleṣavaśena kāvyārtho 'laṅkiyate /
tasyodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: The function (<s>vṛtti</s>) of the denoting word (<s>vācaka</s>), that is, the expressing word (<s>abhidhāyaka</s>), its own word (<s>svaśabda</s>), is the operation of conveying the denoted meaning. The function of the denoted (<s>vācya</s>), that is, the thing to be expressed (<s>abhidheya</s>), is the apprehension of connection with another denoted object by virtue of expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), proximity (<s>saṃnidhi</s>), and fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>). That which is comprehended by another manner, through the power of meaning (<s>arthasāmarthya</s>), even without such a function of the denoted and the denoting — that, though not stated directly by one's own voice, being comprehended through an indirect operation of words, is the substance called <s>paryāyokta</s> (indirect expression). And by its own conjunction, the meaning of poetry is ornamented. An example of it —
By whom the women of the <s>Gajāsura</s> (elephant demon) were made to have disheveled hair, tearful,
with breasts reddened by the blows of hands, and with broken bangles. [UKss 4.*6]
He, by whom even one whose body was burnt was made thus agitated —
obeisance to that <s>Makaraketu</s> (Kāma, the god of love), whose valor is irresistible! [UKss 4.*7]

children.text: atra lambālakatvādayaḥ kāryarūpatvāt kāraṇabhūtaṃ gajāsuravadhaṃ vācyavācakavyāpārāspṛṣṭamapi gamayanti /
children.translated_text: Here, the disheveled hair and other effects, being in the nature of results (<s>kārya</s>), indicate the slaying of <s>Gajāsura</s>, which is the cause, even though it is untouched by the functions of the denoted and the denoting.

children.text: tena ca tathāvidhayā vicchittyā avagamyamānenārthena te lambālakatvādayor'thā alaṅkiyante /
children.translated_text: And by that meaning, comprehended through such a striking mode (<s>vicchitti</s>), the meanings of the disheveled hair and so forth are ornamented.
Therefore, <s>paryāyokta</s> (indirect expression) is an <s>alaṃkāra</s> (figure of speech).
<s>Samāhita</s> (composed) —
The restraint of the operation of <s>rasas</s> (sentiments), <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions), and their semblances (<s>ābhāsa</s>),
that which is devoid of the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) of another [sentiment] — that is called <s>samāhita</s> (composed). [UKss 4.7]

children.text:
iha rasabhāvānāṃ śāstrasamayāviruddhena tadviruddhena ca rūpeṇa dvaividhyamuktam /
tatra ye śāstrasamayāviruddhā rasabhāvāḥ te rasabhāvaśabdenātra
children.translated_text: Here, the twofold nature of <s>rasas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s> has been stated — in a form not contrary to the conventions of <s>śāstra</s>, and in a form contrary to them. Of these, the <s>rasas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s> that are not contrary to the conventions of <s>śāstra</s> are intended here by the term <s>rasabhāva</s>.

children.text:
vivakṣitāḥ /
tadviruddhāstu tadābhāsāḥ /
teṣāṃ rasabhāvānāṃ tadābhāsānāṃ ca yā vṛttiḥ svāśrayasaṃbandhātmikā tasyāḥ praśame nibadhyamāne samāhitālaṅkāro bhavati /
tatra hi teṣāṃ rasabhāvānāṃ samādhānaṃ samādhiḥ parihāro bhavati /
samāhitamiti bhāve ktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those that are contrary to them are the <s>tadābhāsas</s> (semblances). When the restraint of the operation (<s>vṛtti</s>) of those <s>rasas</s>, <s>bhāvas</s>, and their semblances — which has the nature of connection with its own substrate — is effected, the <s>samāhita</s> (composed) <s>alaṃkāra</s> arises. For therein, the composure (<s>samādhāna</s>) of those <s>rasas</s> and <s>bhāvas</s> means their removal (<s>samādhi</s>, i.e., <s>parihāra</s>). <s>Samāhita</s> — the <s>kta</s> suffix is used in the sense of the abstract state (<s>bhāva</s>).

children.text:
nanu yadi tasminkāvye rasādīnāṃ vṛttiḥ parihniyate, evaṃ sati pūrvarasādinivṛttyā rasādyantaropanibandhādrasavadādyalaṅkārānupraveśaḥ prasakta ityāśaṅkyoktaṃ---anyānubhāvaniḥśūnyarūpamiti /
anyasya rasādyantarasya ye 'nubhāvādayaḥ tairniḥśeṣeṇa śūnyaṃ rūpaṃ yasya tattathoktam /
yatra pūrveṣāṃ rasādīnāṃ vāsanāyā dārḍhyena teṣūpaśānteṣvapi rasādyantarāṇāṃ na svarūpamāvirbhavati, āvirbhavadapi vā kāryavaśena kenacittirodhīyate, tatra samāhitālaṅkāro bhavati /
tasyodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: Now, if in that poem the operation of <s>rasas</s> and others is removed, then, with the cessation of the prior <s>rasa</s> and others, the introduction of the <s>rasavat</s> (sentiment-possessing) and other <s>alaṃkāras</s> would be entailed through the establishment of another <s>rasa</s> — anticipating this objection, it is said: 'devoid of the <s>anubhāvas</s> of another.' That whose form is completely devoid of the <s>anubhāvas</s> and other elements of another <s>rasa</s> — that is so described. Where, due to the strength of the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the prior <s>rasas</s> and others, even when they have subsided, the nature of other <s>rasas</s> does not manifest, or even if manifesting, is concealed by something through the force of circumstances — there the <s>samāhita</s> <s>alaṃkāra</s> arises. An example of it —

children.text: atha kāntāṃ dṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā vibhramācca bhramaṃ bhrūvoḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having seen the lovely glance, and the playful movement of the eyebrows,
the serene glow of the face, and the body covered with horripilation and perspiration, [UKss 4.*8]
gathering all limbs inflamed by the fever of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love),
<s>Giriśa</s> (Śiva, Lord of the Mountain) approached the daughter of the mountain (<s>Girisutā</s>) with a greeting of blessing. [UKss 4.*9]

children.text:
samādadhannije rūpe 'vasthāpayan /
samādadhadityabhyastatvānnumo 'pravṛttiḥ /
atra bhagavatā śṛṅgārasya ye 'nubhāvāḥ kāntadṛṣṭyādayasteṣāmavahitthena ākārapracchādanātmakena bhāvena tirodhānaṃ vihitam /
yaduktaṃ---svastipūrvakamiti /
anena hyākāratirodhānamupadarśitam /
children.translated_text: <s>Samādadhat</s> means 'establishing in one's own form' (<s>nije rūpe avasthāpayan</s>). Because of the reduplicated form (<s>abhyastatvāt</s>), the augment <s>num</s> does not apply. Here, the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) of the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, such as the lovely glance and so forth, are concealed through <s>avahittha</s> (dissimulation), the <s>bhāva</s> whose nature is the concealment of outward expression. This is indicated by the phrase 'with a greeting of blessing' (<s>svastipūrvakam</s>). For by this, the concealment of outward expression is shown.
<s>Udātta</s> (the elevated) —
The <s>udātta</s> (elevated) is a subject endowed with wealth, as well as the conduct of great souls,
which has attained the status of a characterizing mark (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) and has come to be not the [main] narrative. [UKss 4.8]

children.text:
ṛddhiḥ suvarṇādidhanasaṃpattiḥ /
tadyuktaṃ vastūdāttam /
tena ca kāvyārtho 'laṃkriyate /
tasyodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛddhi</s> (wealth) means prosperity consisting of gold and other riches. A subject endowed with that is <s>udātta</s> (elevated). And by it, the meaning of poetry is ornamented. An example of it —
And he said: 'From whose lap, with pearls born of bamboo thickets and elephants,
even the <s>Śabarī</s> women have ornaments at will.' [UKss 4.*10]
With summits made of sapphire (<s>indranīla</s>), <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (cat's eye), and <s>padmarāga</s> (ruby), reaching into the sky,
where the peak <s>Gandhamādana</s> shines forth — [UKss 4.*11]
whose northern foothills (<s>upatyakā</s>) are lands of excellent gold,
and the great <s>Arvindhra</s> mountain has resorted to its foot — [UKss 4.*12]
of whom, when the earth was destroyed at the end of the age, in the <s>Pātāla</s>-flowing river,

children.text: patanaṃ na tayā sārdhamāyāmastu prakaṭyabhūt // UKss_4.*13 //
children.translated_text: there was no falling along with it; rather, its extent became manifest — [UKss 4.*13]

children.text:
yasya evaṃvidharūpatā himārdrerbhavatī suteti saṃbandhaḥ /
kroḍaḥ sūkaraḥ /
puṣṭyo maṇiviśeṣaḥ /
gandhamādanaṃ parvataviśeṣaḥ /
upatyakāḥ parvatādhāravartino bhūmibhāgāḥ /
pradhānaṃ svarṇaṃ kārtasvarādi /
arvindhraḥ parvataḥ /
saṃkṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: The connection is: 'the daughter of the <s>Himādri</s> (Snow Mountain) which has such a form.' <s>Kroḍa</s> means boar. <s>Puṣṭi</s> is a type of gem. <s>Gandhamādana</s> is a particular mountain. <s>Upatyakās</s> are tracts of land at the base of a mountain. <s>Pradhāna svarṇa</s> means finest gold, such as <s>kārtasvara</s> and the like. <s>Arvindhra</s> is a mountain. <s>Saṃkṣaya</s> —

children.text:
kalpāntaḥ /
bhūmeradhogamanādbhūmyāśliṣṭasya pradeśasya bhūmiviviktatvāddhimavataḥ kalpānte āyāmaḥ prakaṭībhūtaḥ /
atra ratnādisaṃbhāro nibaddhaḥ /
tenedamudāttam /
tasya cālaṅkāratvaṃ lokātiśāyiratnādikāryadhvananāt /
evametadṛddhimadvastunibandhanenaikamudāttamuktam /
children.translated_text: means the end of the cosmic age (<s>kalpānta</s>). Because of the earth's descent downward, the region attached to the earth became separated from the earth, and at the end of the age, the extent of the <s>Himavat</s> (Himālaya) became manifest. Here, the collection of gems and other [riches] is described. Therefore this is <s>udātta</s> (elevated). And its status as an <s>alaṃkāra</s> is because it suggests extraordinary gems and other effects beyond the ordinary world. Thus, one form of <s>udātta</s> through the description of a subject endowed with wealth has been stated.

children.text:
na kevalamṛddhimadvastūdāttaṃ yāvadarthaprāptāvanarthaparihāre codyatānāṃ vipulāśayānāṃ ceṣṭitamapi, taduktam----
caritaṃ ca mahātmanāmiti /
na ca vipulāśayaceṣṭite upanibadhyamāne tasya śṛṅgārādirasapratipattihetutvādrasavadalaṅkārānupraveśo 'tra subhaṇaḥ /
vipulāśayaceṣṭatasyātra vastvantaropalakṣaṇatvenāvāntaravākyārthībhūtatvāt /
na khalpatra mahāpuruṣaceṣṭitaṃ vākyatātparyagocaratāmanubhavati /
arathāntaropalakṣaṇaparatvāt /
yatra ca rasāstātprayeṇāva gamyante tatra teṣāṃ vākyaviśrāntisthānatvena caturvargataditaraprāptiparihāropāyabhūtasthāyibhāvaparipoṣātmanāsvādyamānatvādrasavadalaṅkāro
children.translated_text: Not only is a subject endowed with wealth <s>udātta</s> (elevated), but also the conduct of great-souled beings who strive for the removal of undesirable outcomes when the desired end has been attained, having vast intentions — as stated: 'and the conduct of great souls.' And when the conduct of one with vast intentions is described, the introduction of the <s>rasavat</s> <s>alaṃkāra</s> is not appropriate here, since such conduct would be a cause for the apprehension of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and other <s>rasas</s>. Because the conduct of the great-souled one here serves as a characterizing mark (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) for another subject matter, and thus becomes a subordinate sentence-meaning. For indeed the conduct of the great person does not become the purport of the sentence here, because it is directed toward characterizing another meaning. Where <s>rasas</s> are apprehended as the purport, there, because they are the resting place of the sentence and because the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion), which is the means for attaining the four goals of life (<s>caturvarga</s>) and avoiding their opposites, is savored in its fullness, the <s>rasavat</s> <s>alaṃkāra</s>

children.text:
bhavati /
tena kuto 'tra rasavadalaṅkāragandho 'pi /
taduktam---upalakṣaṇatāṃ prāptaṃ netivṛttatvamāgatamiti /
tasyodāharaṇam-----
children.translated_text: arises. Therefore, how can there be even a trace of the <s>rasavat</s> <s>alaṃkāra</s> here? As stated: 'which has attained the status of a characterizing mark and has come to be not the [main] narrative.' An example of it —
Of him, though rubbed again and again by the broad shoulders of the primordial boar (<s>Ādikroḍa</s>),
the daughter of the <s>Himādri</s> (Snow Mountain) stood unmoved and steady. [UKss 4.*14]

children.text: atra himavataḥ sthairye vākyārthībhūte bhagavato varāhavapuṣastrailokyoddharaṇodyuktasya ceṣṭitaṃ vīrarasapratipattihetubhūtamavāntaravākyārthatvādupalakṣaṇībhūtam /
children.translated_text: Here, the steadfastness of the <s>Himavat</s> (Himālaya) is the sentence-meaning, while the conduct of the <s>Bhagavān</s> in his boar incarnation (<s>Varāha</s>), striving for the rescue of the three worlds, which is a cause for the apprehension of <s>vīra rasa</s> (the heroic sentiment), has become a characterizing element (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) as a subordinate sentence-meaning.
<s>Ādikroḍa</s> means the primordial boar (<s>Ādivarāha</s>).
In this manner, it should be illustrated where other <s>rasas</s> too have become characterizing elements (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>).
<s>Śliṣṭa</s> (the coalescent) —
Of words that are pronounced with a single effort, and of those that bear the semblance of each other,
a composition distinguished by different qualities such as <s>svarita</s> (circumflex accent) and others — that is called <s>śliṣṭa</s> (coalescent) here. [UKss 4.9]
That which, through words of two kinds, produces the semblance of another <s>alaṃkāra</s> —
distinguished as pertaining to meaning and to sound — let that be recognized. [UKss 4.10]

children.text:
iha khalu śabdānāmanekārthānāṃ yugapadanekārthavivakṣāyāṃ dvayī gatiḥ arthabhedena tāvacchabdā bhidyante iti bhaṭṭodbhaṭasya siddhāntaḥ /
tatrārthabhedena bhidyamānāḥ śabdāḥ kecittantreṇa prayoktuṃ śakyāḥ kecinna /
yeṣāṃ halasvarasthānaprayatnādīnāṃ sāmyaṃ te tantreṇa prayoktuṃ śakyante /
yatra tu halāmekatvānekatvarūpatvātsvarāṇāṃ codāttatvānudāttatvādinā sthānānāṃ cauṣṭhyadantyauṣṭhatvādinā prayatnānāṃ ca laghutvālaghutvādinā bhedasteṣāṃ tantreṇa prayogaḥ kartumaśakyaḥ /
sādhāraṇarūpatvāttantrasya /
taduktam----
'sādhāraṇaṃ bhavettantram'iti /
evaṃ cāvasthite ye tantreṇoccārayituṃ śakyante te ekaprayatnoccāryāḥ /
tadbande satyarthaśleṣo bhavati /
taduktam----
ekaprayatnoccāryāṇāmiti /
tathā ye teṣāmevaikaprayatnoccāryāṇāṃ śabdānāṃ chāyāṃ sādṛśyaṃ bibhrati tadupanibandhe ca śabdaśliṣṭam /
śabdāntare uccāryamāṇe sādṛśyavaśenānuccāritasyāpi śabdāntarasya śliṣṭatvāt /
taduktam---tacchāyāṃ caiva bibhratām /
svaritādiguṇairbhinnairbandhaḥ śliṣṭamiti /
tathā---śabdoktiviśiṣṭaṃ tatpratīyatāmiti /
etacca śliṣṭaṃ dvividhamapyupamādyalaṅkārapratibhotpādanadvāreṇālaṅkāratāṃ pratipadyate /
ato 'nenānavakāśatvāt svaviṣaye 'laṅkārāntarāṇyapodyante, teṣāṃ viṣayāntare sāvakāśatvāt /
taduktam----
alaṅkārāntaragatāṃ pratibhāṃ janayatpadaiḥ /
dvividhairiti /
alaṅkārāntarāṇāmatra pratibhāmātraṃ na tu padabandha ityarthaḥ /
tadevaṃ śabdaśliṣṭamarthaśliṣṭaṃ ca lakṣitam /
tasyodāharaṇam---
children.translated_text: Now, since words have multiple meanings, when there is a simultaneous intention of multiple meanings, there are two possibilities. First, that words are differentiated by the differentiation of meaning — this is the established doctrine of <s>Bhaṭṭa Udbhaṭa</s>. Among words differentiated by meaning, some can be employed in a single combined usage (<s>tantra</s>) and some cannot. Those whose consonants, vowels, places of articulation, and efforts are identical can be employed in a combined usage. But where there is difference in consonants — being single or multiple in form — or in vowels — being <s>udātta</s> (acute), <s>anudātta</s> (grave), and so forth — or in places of articulation — being labial, dental-labial, and so forth — or in efforts — being light, non-light, and so forth — their combined usage cannot be effected, because a combined usage must have a common form. As stated: 'The combined usage (<s>tantra</s>) must be of a common form.' This being the case, those that can be pronounced in a combined usage are 'pronounced with a single effort' (<s>ekaprayatnoccārya</s>). When their combination is present, there is <s>arthaśleṣa</s> (coalescence of meaning). As stated: 'Of words pronounced with a single effort.' Likewise, those words pronounced with a single effort that bear the semblance, that is, the similarity, of each other — when their combination is effected, there is <s>śabdaśliṣṭa</s> (coalescence of sound), because even when another word is being pronounced, the other unspoken word is coalesced through similarity. As stated: 'and of those that bear the semblance of each other'; 'a composition distinguished by different qualities such as <s>svarita</s> and others — that is <s>śliṣṭa</s>.' And also: 'distinguished as pertaining to sound — let that be recognized.' This <s>śliṣṭa</s>, though twofold, attains the status of an <s>alaṃkāra</s> through generating the semblance of other <s>alaṃkāras</s> such as <s>upamā</s> (simile) and the like. Therefore, by this [figure], since it leaves no scope [for them], other <s>alaṃkāras</s> are set aside in its own domain, those [other alaṃkāras] having scope elsewhere. As stated: 'That which, through words of two kinds, produces the semblance of another alaṃkāra.' The meaning is: here there is only the semblance of other <s>alaṃkāras</s>, not an actual word-composition [of them]. Thus, <s>śabdaśliṣṭa</s> (coalescence of sound) and <s>arthaśliṣṭa</s> (coalescence of meaning) have been defined. An example of it —
She herself, resplendent with hands red like tender shoots,
like the dawn, grants what is desired to those who seek the fruit of sleeplessness. [UKss 4.*15]
Moon-beautiful of face, with glossy hair dark as great sapphires,
the beauty of liberation, the jewel of the three worlds, with feet like lotus-red petals. [UKss 4.*16]
Even without the report of the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree, she is the beauty of <s>Nandana</s> (paradise) on earth,
ever beautiful without a blemish, with drops of loveliness flowing from her neck. [UKss 4.*17]

children.text:
na kevalaṃ tvaṃ himādrerevaṃvidhasya sutā yāvatsvayaṃ caivaṃprakāreti ca śabdaḥ /
atra bhagavatī kisalayavadātāmrau
children.translated_text: The word 'ca' (and) means: not only are you the daughter of the <s>Himādri</s> (Snow Mountain) of such a nature, but you yourself are also of such a kind. Here, the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (the Goddess) has hands (<s>kara</s>) that are radiant and red like tender shoots (<s>kisalaya</s>) —

children.text:
bhāsvantau dīptimantau yau karau hastau tābhyāṃ virājate /
prabhātasandhyā tu pallavavadātāmrairbhāsvata ādityasya karairmayūkhairvirājate /
atra cobhayatrāpi halādanāṃ sāmyam /
atastantreṇoccāraṇasaṃbhavādayamarthaśleṣaḥ /
asvāpaphalalubdhe hitapradetyatra tu bhagavatīpakṣe asvāpaṃ sukhenāptuṃ yanna śakyate phalaṃ tatra ye lubdhāstebhya īhitamīpsitaṃ pradadātītyarthaḥ /
prabhātasandhyāpakṣe tu svāpasya nidrānubhavasya yatphalaṃ śramanivṛttilakṣaṇaṃ tatra yo na lubdhaḥ sandhyopāsanapravṛttatvāttadviṣayaṃ hitamadṛṣṭaṃ samarpayatītyevaṃvidhetyarthaḥ /
atra ca pūrvasminpakṣe aikapadyāt (pā. a. 6 / 2 / 144) thāthādisvareṇāntodāttatvam /
uttaratra punarasvāpaphalalubdhe iti hitapradeti ca anayorbhinnapadatvānnānāsvaratvam /
asvāpaphalalubdha ityasya "tatpuruṣe tulyārtheti"(pā. a. 6 / 2 / 2)
children.translated_text: the two hands that are shining and radiant — she is resplendent by them. The dawn (<s>prabhātasandhyā</s>), on the other hand, is resplendent by the radiant rays (<s>kara</s>) of the sun that are red like tender shoots. Here, in both cases, the consonants and other phonetic elements are identical. Therefore, since combined pronunciation is possible, this is <s>arthaśleṣa</s> (coalescence of meaning). In 'she grants what is desired to those who seek the fruit of sleeplessness' (<s>asvāpaphalalubdhehitapradā</s>), on the side of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>, the meaning is: she bestows what is desired upon those who are eager for the fruit that cannot be easily obtained — i.e., the fruit of spiritual wakefulness. On the side of the dawn, the meaning is: she bestows the unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) upon one who is not attached to the fruit of sleep, namely the relief from fatigue, because he is engaged in the twilight worship (<s>sandhyopāsana</s>). Here, in the former case, due to compound unity (<s>aikapadya</s>), there is final-acute accent by the <s>thāthādi</s> rule (Pāṇini 6.2.144). In the latter case, however, since <s>asvāpaphalalubdhe</s> and <s>hitapradā</s> are separate words, there are different accents. <s>Asvāpaphalalubdha</s>, by the rule 'in a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound with a synonymous term' (Pāṇini 6.2.2),

children.text:
pūrvapadaprakṛtisvareṇādyutāttatvāt /
hitapradetyasya tu (pā. a. 6 / 2 / 144) yathādisvareṇāntodāttatvāt /
tenātra svarabhedaḥ /
asvāpeti akārasya phalalubdhe iti ca ekārasya ubhayoḥ pakṣayoryathāyogaṃ lāghavālāghavābhyāṃ prayatnabhedo 'pi /
atastantreṇoccārayitumaśakyatā /
ekasmiṃstvatra śabde samuccarite śabdāntarasya tatsādṛśyātpratipattiḥ /
ato 'yaṃ śabdaśleṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: has initial-acute accent due to the original accent of the prior member being retained. But <s>hitapradā</s>, by the <s>yathādi</s> rule (Pāṇini 6.2.144), has final-acute accent. Therefore, here there is a difference in accent (<s>svarabhedaḥ</s>). Also, the <s>a</s>-vowel in <s>asvāpa</s> and the <s>e</s>-vowel in <s>phalalubdhe</s> have, in each of the two interpretations respectively, a difference in effort due to lightness or non-lightness. Therefore, combined pronunciation is impossible. But when one word is pronounced here, the other word is apprehended due to its similarity. Therefore, this is <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (coalescence of sound).

children.text:
etayośca dvayorapyarthaśleṣaśabdaśleṣayorupamāpratibhotpattihetutvam /
prabhātasandhyā hyatropamānam /
bhagavatī upameyā /
ivaśabdaścopamānopameyabhāvaṃ dyotayati /
śabdavyatirekeṇa tu sādhāraṇo dharmor'thādhikaraṇo 'tra na vidyate /
tena neyamupamā apitu śleṣa upamāpratibhotpattihetuḥ /
children.translated_text: And both of these — <s>arthaśleṣa</s> (coalescence of meaning) and <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (coalescence of sound) — serve as the cause for generating the semblance of <s>upamā</s> (simile). For here, the dawn (<s>prabhātasandhyā</s>) is the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison), the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (Goddess) is the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison), and the word <s>iva</s> (like) indicates the relation of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>. But apart from the word [<s>iva</s>], there is no common property (<s>sādhāraṇa dharma</s>) based on meaning here. Therefore, this is not a [true] <s>upamā</s> (simile), but rather <s>śleṣa</s> (coalescence) that serves as the cause for generating the semblance of <s>upamā</s>.

children.text:
indukāntamukhītyatra bhagavatī candravatsundaraṃ mukhaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathāvidhā /
tathā snigdhadīrghakṛṣṇakeśī /
muktā parityaktā aśrīraśobhā yayā sā tathāvidhā /
trailokyotkṛṣṭā ca /
tathā padmavat kamalavat rāgo lauhityaṃ yayostathāvidhau pādapallavau yasyāsatadrūpā /
yadā tvasau bhagavatī rūpakapratibhotpattinibandhanena śleṣeṇa trailokyodaravartimāṇikyasaṃbhārarūpatayā rūpyate tadā prakṛtor'thaścandrakāntendranīlamauktikaśobhāpadmarāgairavacchāditarūpatayā pratīyate, sākṣādevaṃvidharatnamayāvayavayogitvāt tribhuvanodarāntargataratnasamṛddhirūpeti /
atra ca muktāśrīrityatra svarabhedo vidyate /
bahuvrīhipakṣe"bahuvrīhau prakṛtyeti"pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvāt /
tatpuruṣe tu samāsāntodāttatvāt /
śiṣṭānāṃ tu śabdānāṃ svarabhedo nāsti /
prayatnagurutvāgurutve tu trijagadratnaśabdavyatirikteṣu tattadvarṇaviṣayatayā vidyete /
tena tatra śabdaśleṣatā /
trijagadratnaśabdasya tūbhayatrāpi kasyacidviśeṣasyāvidyamānatvādarthaśleṣatvam /
apārijātavārtāpītyatra bhagavatyajātaśatrutvādapagataśatrusamūhavārtā tadīyā ca śobhā sarvasya cittamāvarjayatītyato nandanā śrīryasyāstathāvidhā /
udakamadhyavartitayā ca yo 'sau apsu udake pratabimbita industadvatsundarī /
nityaṃ ca galallāvaṇyapravāhā /
yadā tvasau bhagavatī nandanaśrīśabdasya devodyānaśobhālakṣaṇārthāntarābhidhāyatvādrūpakapritibhotpattinibandhanena śleṣeṇaitadbhāvamāpadyate tadā tatsamāśrayatvena apārijātavārtāpītyādipadaparyālocanayā virodhapratibhāhetoraparasyāpi śleṣasyāvirbhāvo bhavati /
na khalu devodyānaśobhā avidyamānapārijātākhyavṛkṣaviśeṣavṛttāntā bhavati /
na cāsau bhūmau tiṣṭhati /
abindusundarītyatra tu bindubhiryasyāḥ saundaryaṃ nāsti tasyāḥ kathaṃ lāvaṇyabindavaḥ prasareyuriti virodhapratapattihetuḥ śleṣaḥ /
apārijātavārtāpītyatrāpyapagatā arijātavārteti bahuvrīhau prakṛtyeti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam /
tatpuruṣapakṣetvantodāttatvam /
abindusundarītyatra abinduvatsandarītyupamānatvā "tatpuruṣe tulyārtho"tyabinduśabdasya prakṛtisvaraḥ /

children.translated_text: And since its prior member ends in the locative case (<s>saptamyanta</s>), by this very rule the original accent gives initial <s>udātta</s> (high tone).
In '<s>abindusundarī</s>,' however, since <s>nañ</s> (the negative particle) is an indeclinable (<s>avyaya</s>), the original accent of the prior member applies in the same way.
Therefore, there is no difference in accent here.
But due to the difference in effort, from the variation of the <s>ca</s>-sound, there is <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (verbal paronomasia).

Regarding 'moon-faced' (<s>indukāntamukhī</s>): the <s>Bhagavatī</s> is one whose face is as beautiful as the moon — she is of such a nature. Likewise, she has smooth, long, black hair (<s>snigdhadīrghakṛṣṇakeśī</s>). <s>Muktā</s> means 'released' — she by whom unbeautifulness (<s>aśrī</s>) has been abandoned, she is of such a nature. And she is the most exalted in the three worlds (<s>trailokyotkṛṣṭā</s>). Likewise, her feet-sprouts have redness like a lotus — she is of such a form. But when this <s>Bhagavatī</s>, through <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) based on the arising of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) awareness, is figuratively described as being of the nature of a collection of jewels within the belly of the three worlds, then the meaning of the original words is understood as being covered by moonstone (<s>candrakānta</s>), sapphire (<s>indranīla</s>), pearl (<s>mauktika</s>), lustre (<s>śobhā</s>), and ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>) — because she directly possesses limbs made of such jewels, the meaning becomes 'the wealth of gems contained within the three worlds.' And here in '<s>muktāśrīḥ</s>' there is a difference in accent (<s>svarabheda</s>). In the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> interpretation, according to the rule 'in <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, the original form,' there is the original accent of the prior member (<s>pūrvapada</s>). But in the <s>tatpuruṣa</s>, the accent falls on the final element of the compound. For the remaining words, however, there is no difference in accent. But differences in effort — heaviness and non-heaviness — exist with respect to the respective vowels, except in the word '<s>trijagadratna</s>.' Therefore, there is <s>śabdaśleṣa</s> (verbal paronomasia) there. But the word '<s>trijagadratna</s>' has <s>arthaśleṣa</s> (semantic paronomasia), since no particular difference exists in either interpretation. Regarding '<s>apārijātavārtā</s>': since the <s>Bhagavatī</s> has no enemy born (<s>ajātaśatru</s>), the news of her is devoid of enemy-hosts, and her splendor captivates the mind of all — hence, she whose glory is <s>Nandanā</s> (delightful), she is of such a nature. And being situated in the midst of water, she who is reflected in the waters is as beautiful as the moon (<s>indu</s>). And there is a constant flow of grace from her neck. But when this <s>Bhagavatī</s>, because the word '<s>nandanaśrī</s>' can also mean 'the beauty of the <s>Nandana</s> garden (the divine garden),' through <s>śleṣa</s> based on the arising of <s>rūpaka</s> awareness assumes this state, then by virtue of being the locus of that, through consideration of the words '<s>apārijātavārtā</s>' etc., there arises a second <s>śleṣa</s> due to the apprehension of <s>virodha</s> (contradiction). For the beauty of the divine garden cannot exist without the story of the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree. Nor does she stand on the ground. In '<s>abindusundarī</s>,' however, the <s>śleṣa</s> is the cause of apprehending contradiction: if she whose beauty lacks marks (<s>bindu</s>), how could drops of grace flow forth? Regarding '<s>apārijātavārtā</s>' as well: when parsed as a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, 'one from whom enemy-born tidings have departed,' according to 'in <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, the original form,' the prior member retains its original accent. In the <s>tatpuruṣa</s> interpretation, however, the accent falls at the end.
Thus ends the fourth chapter (<s>varga</s>) in the concise commentary (<s>laghuvṛtti</s>) on the <s>Udbhaṭālaṅkārasārasaṃgraha</s>, composed by the great and illustrious <s>Pratīhāra Indurāja</s>.
Now begins the fifth chapter (<s>varga</s>).
<s>Apahnuti</s> (concealment), <s>viśeṣokti</s> (distinction), <s>virodha</s> (contradiction), <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction),
<s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant), <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise), and <s>vidarśanā</s> (illustration) — [UKss 5.1]
<s>upameyopamā</s> (counter-simile), <s>sahokti</s> (co-expression), and <s>saṃkara</s> (mixture) likewise,
and <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange) — other authorities have declared these as <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments) of speech. [UKss 5.2]
<s>Apahnuti</s> (concealment) —
<s>Apahnuti</s> is the desired [figure] wherein there is a slightly concealed simile (<s>upamā</s>);
its construction is made by the learned through the denial (<s>apahnava</s>) of what actually exists (<s>bhūtārtha</s>). [UKss 5.3]

children.text:
yatra bhūtaṃ vidyamānamupameyalakṣaṇamarthamapahnutyopamānarūpāropeṇopamānopameyabhāvo.......................... tiralaṅkāraḥ /
atra ca prākaraṇikasya
children.translated_text: Where the actual, i.e. existing, thing characterized as the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) is denied, and through the superimposition of the form of the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison), the relationship of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> [is established]... this is the figure (<s>alaṅkāra</s>). And here, of the contextually relevant

existing meaning... since the existing thing, with an indistinct form, shines forth as the relationship of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> — thus it is said: 'wherein there is a slightly concealed simile' (<s>kiñcidantargatopamā</s>). The illustration of that —

children.text: etaddhi na tapaḥ satyamidaṃ hālāhalaṃ viṣam /
children.translated_text: This indeed is not <s>tapas</s> (austerity) — truly, this is <s>hālāhala</s> poison;
especially for those like you, who are as delicate as a digit of the moon. [UKss 5.*1]

children.text:
atra prākaraṇikasya tapasaḥ svarūpamapahnutya hālāhalaviṣaviśeṣarūpatādhyāropeṇa tatsādṛśyamavagamitam /
taccātra hālāhalaviṣasādṛśyamupameyasyāpahnutatvānna sphuṭarūpam /
hālāhalākhyo viṣabhedo yaḥ śīghraṃ vyāpādayati /
children.translated_text: Here, the true nature of the contextually relevant <s>tapas</s> (austerity) is denied, and through the superimposition of the form of the specific poison <s>hālāhala</s>, the similarity with it is conveyed. And here, the similarity with <s>hālāhala</s> poison is not in a manifest form, because the <s>upameya</s> has been denied. <s>Hālāhala</s> is a particular kind of poison that kills quickly.
<s>Viśeṣokti</s> (distinction) —
Where, despite the completeness of the aggregate of causes (<s>śakti</s>), the construction involves the non-production of the result,
the intention being to express a distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>) — that is called <s>viśeṣokti</s>. [UKss 5.4]

children.text:
śaktīnāṃ kārakāṇāṃ sāmagrye 'pi avikalatve yaḥ kriyāphalasya kiñcidviśeṣamavagamayitumanutpatterupanibandhaḥ sā viśeṣoktiḥ /
tasyāśca dvaubhedau /
kvacitkhalu kāraṇasāmagrye 'pi yatkāryaṃ notpadyate tasyānutpattau svakaṇṭhena nimittamupādīyate, kvacittvarthasāmarthyādavagamyate tadāha---
children.translated_text: Where, despite the completeness, i.e. the non-deficiency, of the aggregate of causes (<s>kāraka</s>), the construction concerns the non-production of the result of action, in order to make known some distinction — that is <s>viśeṣokti</s>. And it has two varieties. Sometimes, when despite the completeness of causes, the effect does not arise, the reason for its non-arising is stated explicitly; sometimes it is understood from the force of meaning. Thus he says —
With the cause shown, and without showing the cause,

children.text: tasyā bandho dvidhā lakṣye dṛśyate lalitātmakaḥ // UKss_5.5 //
children.translated_text: the construction of that [figure], having an elegant nature, is seen in two ways in practice. [UKss 5.5]
'Not-showing' (<s>adarśana</s>) means non-employment. The illustration of the second variety of that —
Birth in a house of great prosperity, beauty, youth rivaling that of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love) —

children.text: tathāpi na sukhaprāptiḥ kasya citrīyate na dhīḥ // UKss_5.*2 //
children.translated_text: yet there is no attainment of happiness — whose mind is not astonished by this? [UKss 5.*2]

children.text:
atra dhanasaṃbhārayogaḥ surūpatvaṃ yauvanaṃ ceti yānyetāni sukhaprāptau kāraṇānyavikalāni tatsadbhāve 'pi kriyāphalabhūtāyāḥ sukhaprāpteranutpattirupanibaddhā /
pūrvoktānāṃ sukhahetūnāṃ vismayavibhāvanātmakaviśeṣakhyāpanāya /
atra ca nimittaṃ khakaṇṭhenānupāttamapyarthasāmarthyādavagamyate /
vidhivaidhuryādirūpaśabdo 'tra śarīrasya rūpamātrāvyabhicāritvādrūpaprakarṣatātparyeṇopāttaḥ /
smarasuhṛdvayo yauvanam /
yauvane hi manmathābhimukhībhavati /
ādyabhedodāharaṇaṃ tu----
children.translated_text: Here, the possession of abundant wealth, handsome appearance, and youth — these are the complete causes for the attainment of happiness; yet despite their presence, the non-production of the attainment of happiness, which is the result of action, is constructed — for the purpose of making known a distinction in the form of the evocation of wonder (<s>vismayavibhāvanā</s>) regarding the aforementioned causes of happiness. And here, the cause, though not stated explicitly, is understood from the force of meaning: namely, fate (<s>vidhi</s>)
Having seen your conduct thus disordered,

children.text: nodeti kimapi praṣṭu satvarasyāpi me vacaḥ // UKss_5.*3 //
children.translated_text: no word of mine rises to ask anything, even though I am full of eagerness. [UKss 5.*3]
Here, despite the presence of the cause characterized by eagerness to ask, the non-production of a questioning utterance is constructed.
And through this, the distinction called the evocation of wonder (<s>vismayavibhāvanā</s>) regarding the cause of the questioning utterance is made known.
And here, the cause — the seeing of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>'s disordered conduct — is stated explicitly.
<s>Virodha</s> (contradiction) —
Where speech expressing another action contradictory to a quality or an action
is made for the purpose of conveying a distinction — that they call <s>virodha</s> (contradiction). [UKss 5.6]

children.text:
yatra kavinā guṇasya vā kriyāyā vā athavā dvirvāśabdasyopāttatvāt dravyasya viruddho 'nyaḥ padārthaḥ sajātīyo vijātīyo vā vacasā svapratibhāprasūtena varṇanikātmanā kriyate kañcidviśeṣamavagamayituṃ sa virodhākhyo 'laṅkāraḥ /
guṇakriyādravyāṇāmutprekṣālaṅkāralakṣaṇavyākhyānasamaye svūrūpamuktam /
kriyā kāraṇamutpādanaṃ, ttpradhānaṃ vacaḥ kriyāvacaḥ /
kavipratibhayā khalu purāṇaprajāpatinirmitaśuṣkaparuṣapadārthavilakṣaṇāḥ sarasāḥ padārthāḥ abhinavā eva nirmīyante /
ataḥ kriyāvaca ityuktam /
tasyodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: Where the poet, by means of his own creative utterance in the form of description, presents another thing — of the same kind or of a different kind — that is contradictory to a quality, or to an action, or to a substance (since the word <s>vā</s> is employed twice), in order to convey some distinction — that is the figure called <s>virodha</s>. The nature of quality, action, and substance has been explained at the time of discussing the definition of the figure <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy).

children.text: yadvā māṃ kiṃ karomyeṣa vācālayati vismayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or rather, what shall I do — this amazement renders me loquacious!

children.text: bhavatyāḥ kvāyamākāraḥ kvedaṃ tapasi pāṭavam // UKss_5.*4 //
children.translated_text: Where is this appearance of yours, and where is this proficiency in <s>tapas</s> (austerity)? [UKss 5.*4]

children.text:
atra yadetatpūrvamupakrāntaṃ vaco me nodetīti tasyākṣepo yadvetikṛtaḥ /
kiṃvā karomi vismayavācālitaḥ san bravīmi bhavatyāḥ kvate /
eṣa vismayo māṃ vācālayatīti saṃbandhaḥ /
atrākṛteḥ sukumārāyāḥ pāṭavasya ca kaṭhinakāyasādhyasya virodho bhagavatīniṣṭhatvenopanibaddhaḥ /

children.translated_text: And through this, the distinction called the evocation of wonder (<s>vismayavibhāvanā</s>) is made known here.
And this is a <s>guṇavirodha</s> (contradiction of qualities), because it rests upon properties whose nature is unestablished (<s>asiddhasvabhāvadharma</s>).
Similarly, examples should be cited for <s>kriyāvirodha</s> (contradiction of actions) too, which rests upon properties whose nature is to be established.

children.text: tathā dravyavirodhe guṇakriyāvirodhe guṇadravyavirodhe kriyādravyavirodhe ca //
children.translated_text: Likewise for <s>dravyavirodha</s> (contradiction of substances), <s>guṇakriyāvirodha</s> (contradiction of quality and action), <s>guṇadravyavirodha</s> (contradiction of quality and substance), and <s>kriyādravyavirodha</s> (contradiction of action and substance).

Here, the speech previously begun — 'my word does not rise' — is retracted with 'or rather' (<s>yadvā</s>). 'What shall I do — being made loquacious by amazement, I speak: where is this appearance of yours?' The connection is: 'this amazement renders me loquacious.' Here, the contradiction between her delicate form (<s>ākṛti</s>) and proficiency (<s>pāṭava</s>), which requires a hardened body, is constructed with the <s>Bhagavatī</s> as its locus.
<s>Tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction) —

Speech that expresses sameness through words that are irrelevant [to the main topic] and devoid of the [explicit] mention of <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison),
or through words that are relevant to the occasion — that is <s>tulyayogitā</s>. [UKss 5.7]

children.text:
aprastutānāmeva vā yatra sāmyamabhidhīyate sā tulyayogitā /
ata eva prākaraṇikāprākaraṇikobhayārthaniṣṭhatvābhāvāttatropamānopameyoktiśūnyatvaṃ prastāvabhāgbhiḥ prastutaiḥ sāmyābhidhāyi vaca iti saṃbandhaḥ /
tasyāḥ pūrvabhedasyodāharaṇam-----
children.translated_text: Where sameness is expressed only among irrelevant things — that is <s>tulyayogitā</s>. And precisely because of the absence of being grounded in both the contextually relevant and irrelevant meanings, there is the absence of the mention of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> in the former. The connection is: speech that expresses sameness 'through relevant words' (<s>prastāvabhāgbhiḥ</s>), i.e. through words pertaining to the main topic. The illustration of the first variety of that —

children.text: tvadaṅgamārdavaṃ draṣṭuḥ kasya citte na bhāsate /
children.translated_text: In whose mind does there not appear, upon seeing the softness of your limbs,
the hardness of the <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine), the crescent moon, and the <s>kadalī</s> (plantain)? [UKss 5.*5]

children.text:
tvaccharīrasaukumāryadarśinaḥ kasyeva cetasi mālatyādīnāṃ kāṭhinyaṃ na bhāsata ityarthaḥ /
atra mālatyādīnāmaprākaraṇikānāmevārthānāṃ kaṭhoratvalakṣaṇaṃ sāmyamupanibaddham /
draṣṭuriti tṛn /
tadyoge ca tvadaṅgamārdavamiti "na lokāvyayaniṣṭhe'ti ṣaṣṭhīniṣedhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: in whose mind does the hardness of the jasmine and the rest not appear, upon seeing the delicacy of your body? Here, the sameness characterized as hardness is constructed only among the irrelevant things — the jasmine and the rest. '<s>Draṣṭuḥ</s>' is formed with the <s>tṛn</s> suffix. And in conjunction with that, 'the softness of your limbs' — the prohibition of the sixth case (<s>ṣaṣṭhī</s>) 'not in the case of <s>loka</s>, indeclinables, and <s>niṣṭhā</s> [participles]' [applies].
The illustration of the second variety —
A yoga-band (<s>yogapaṭṭa</s>), a mass of matted locks (<s>jaṭājāla</s>), bark-garment (<s>tāravītvak</s>), and a deerskin (<s>mṛgājina</s>) —
if these are suited to your body, then let that be stated. [UKss 5.*6]

children.text:
atra prākaraṇikānamapi yogapaṭṭādīnāṃ bhagavatīśarīre saṃsparśanaucityalakṣaṇaḥ samāno dharmo nibaddhaḥ /
tāravītvak valkalam /
aṅgasya śarīrasya /
children.translated_text: Here, the common property characterized by unsuitability of contact with the <s>Bhagavatī</s>'s body is constructed even among the contextually relevant things — the yoga-band and the rest. <s>Tāravītvak</s> means bark. '<s>Aṅgasya</s>' means 'of the body.'
<s>Aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) —
Where there is praise of another thing that has departed from the subject under discussion,
that is <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>, [and it is] connected to the relevant meaning. [UKss 5.8]

children.text:
adhikārādupavarṇanāvasarādapagatasya prākaraṇikādaparasya vastuno yatropanibandhaḥ sā aprastutapraśaṃsā /
na caivamapi tasyā unmattapralāpaprakhyatā, yataḥ sā kenacitsvājanyena prastutamarthamanubadhnati /
taduktam---prastutārthānubandhinīti /
tasyā udāharaṇam-----
children.translated_text: Where the construction concerns another thing that has departed from the subject under discussion, i.e. from the occasion of description — that is <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>. Nor does it thereby become like the raving of a madman, because it connects to the relevant meaning through some affinity of its own. Thus it is said: 'connected to the relevant meaning' (<s>prastutārthānubandhinī</s>). The illustration of that —
The splendors of forests in inaccessible regions, though endowed with abundance of fruit and flowers,
attain old age in their own forms, without anyone to enjoy them. [UKss 5.*7]

children.text: atra kṛcchreṇa gantuṃ śakyate yasmindeśe tadgatakānanānāṃ śobhā aprākaraṇikya eva svadehajarjaratayopavarṇitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the beauty of the forests located in a region that can be reached only with difficulty — an irrelevant topic — is described as decaying in its own form.
And through these, the conduct of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>, which is the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison), is understood as being of such a nature, through the affinity [between the two].
In '<s>durga</s>,' the <s>ḍa</s>-suffix is [applied] according to the rule '<s>suduroradhikaraṇa</s>' (in the sense of location with <s>su</s> and <s>dur</s>).
<s>Vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) —
Where, by the inherent nature of the power of words, what is understood appears to be censure (<s>nindā</s>),
but in reality the intention is praise (<s>stuti</s>) — that is regarded as <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise). [UKss 5.9]

children.text: yatra śabdānāmabhidhāyakānāṃ yā śaktirarthapratyāyanautsukyaṃ tasyā yaḥ svabhāvo niyatārthaniṣṭhatvātmakastena nindā gamyate iva natvasau nindaiva /
children.translated_text: Where, by the inherent nature of the power of words — that is, the eagerness of their capacity to convey meaning — which by its nature is fixed on a determinate meaning, censure is understood, as it were — but it is not truly censure;

children.text:
padārthaparyālocanasāmarthyotthāyāṃ stutau vākyārthībhūtāyāmavāntaravākyārthatvāt /
ata evāha----
vastutastu stutiśceṣṭeti /
vastuta ityarthasāmarthyādityarthaḥ /
tatra vyājastutirnāmālaṅkāro bhavati /
children.translated_text: because the praise, which arises from the force of considering the meaning of the constituent words, having become the sentence-meaning, [supersedes] the subordinate clause-meaning. Therefore he says: 'but in reality the intention is praise.' 'In reality' (<s>vastutaḥ</s>) means 'by the force of meaning.' There, the figure called <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) obtains.

children.text:
nindāvyājena hi sā stutiḥ /
ato vyājastutiḥ /
tasyā udāharaṇam-----
children.translated_text: For it is praise through the pretext of censure. Hence it is <s>vyājastuti</s>. The illustration of that —
Fie upon this beauty of yours, which has no equal!
For in all the three worlds, no suitable husband for you can be found. [UKss 5.*8]

children.text: atra yadetaddhigvādopahatatvaṃ rūpasaṃpadaḥ sākṣācchabdavyāpāreṇa spṛṣṭaṃ na tatsvātmaparyavasitaṃ, arthasāmarthyotthalokottarabhagavatīrūpotkarṣapratipādanaparyavasitatvāt /

children.translated_text: Therefore, that [censure] has the status of a subordinate clause-meaning.
Hence this is <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise),
because the excellence of beauty is being praised through the pretext of censure.
In '<s>dhigananyopamām</s>,' the second case (<s>dvitīyā</s>) ending [is applied] according to the rule '<s>ubhasarvatasoḥ kārye</s>' (the accusative is used with <s>ubha</s> and <s>sarvatas</s>).

Here, the fact that the beauty is struck by the expression of censure 'fie' (<s>dhik</s>) — this is touched upon by the direct function of the words, but it does not rest in its own purport, because it terminates in conveying the extraordinary excellence of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>'s beauty, which arises from the force of meaning.
<s>Vidarśanā</s> (illustration) —
Where one constructs a relationship between things that does not [naturally] obtain, or where one that does obtain
[is shown to have] the character of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> — that is called <s>vidarśanā</s>. [UKss 5.10]

children.text:
yatra padārthānāṃ saṃbandhaḥ svayamanupapadyamānaḥ sannupamānopameyabhāve paryavasyati athavā upamānopameyabhāvakalpanayā svātmānamupapādayati tatra vidarśanā, viśiṣṭasyārthasya upamānopameyabhāvātmakasyopadarśanāt /
tasyā udāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: Where a relationship among things, being one that does not of itself obtain, culminates in the status of <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison); or alternatively, where through the construction of the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relationship it establishes itself — there is <s>vidarśanā</s>, because of the showing (<s>upadarśana</s>) of a distinguished meaning in the form of the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relationship. The illustration of that —
Even a beautiful woman (<s>kāminī</s>), without a suitable husband,
bears the unsightliness of a night bereft of the moon. [UKss 5.*9]

children.text:
vidhuścandraḥ /
vibhāvarī rātriḥ /
atra rajanikararahitavibhāvarīviśobhatvasya yadetatkarmatvaṃ tatkāminīkartṛkāyāṃ bharaṇakriyāyāṃ na samanvayaṃ gacchati /
na hyanyasya saṃbandhinīṃ viśobhāmanyo bibharti /
ataḥ padārthasamanvayasyātrānupapattiḥ /
upamānopameyabhāvastvatra vākyārthaviśrāntisthānaṃ kṛṣṇarātrivadviśobhatāṃ bibhartiti /
evametadbhavati vastvasaṃbandhe upamānopameyabhāvakalpanāyāmudāharaṇam /
yatra tu padārthasamankya upamānopameyabhāvakalpanayā svātmānamupapādayati tasya vidarśanābhedasyodāharaṇamudbhaṭapustake na dṛśyate /
tasya tu bhāmahodatamidamudāharaṇam---
children.translated_text: <s>Vidhu</s> means the moon. <s>Vibhāvarī</s> means night. Here, the objecthood (karmatva) of the unsightliness of a night devoid of the moon does not find syntactic connection (samanvaya) with the action of bearing whose agent is the woman. For one does not bear the unsightliness belonging to another. Therefore, there is an impossibility of syntactic connection of word-meanings here. But the relation of <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) is the resting place of the sentence-meaning here — she bears unsightliness like a dark night. Thus this becomes an example of the construction of an <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation where there is no real connection between the things. But where the syntactic connection of word-meanings establishes itself through the construction of an <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation, an example of that variety of <s>vidarśanā</s> (illustration) is not found in <s>Udbhaṭa</s>'s text. However, the following example given by <s>Bhāmaha</s> illustrates it —
This sun, of diminished radiance, wishes to proceed toward setting;
"Rise leads to fall" — thus awakening men of fortune. [UKss 5.*10]
Thus.

children.text:
tatra prathamodayasamayavijṛmbhamāṇasvakāntirahitasaya bhāsvato yadetadastamayaunmukhyaṃ tadupetasya śrīmataḥ prayojyakartṝn prati pātāvasānodayakarmake 'vabodhe tatsamarthācaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ hetukartṛtvamupanibaddham /
tathāvidhaṃ khalu bhāsvantaṃ paśyantaḥ śrīmanto budhyante bhāsvata iva sarvasyodayaḥ pātāvasāna iti /
tāṃścāsau tathāvabudhyamānān svāvasthopadarśanena prayuṅkte yathā mamāyamudayaḥ pātāvasānastathā bhavatāmapīti /
children.translated_text: And he (the sun) impels those who thus understand, by displaying his own condition: "Just as my rise ends in a fall, so too does yours."

children.text: atra ca preṣaṇādhyeṣaṇayorabhāvāttatsamarthācaraṇalakṣaṇa eva prayojakavyāpāraḥ kārīṣo 'dhyāpayati bhikṣā vāsayatīti yathā /
children.translated_text: And here, since there is an absence of both sending and requesting, the activity of the causal agent is characterized only by conduct capable of producing that effect — just as in the expressions "the cowdung teaches" and "alms make one stay."

children.text: tena ca prayojyaprayojakabhāvena svātmānamupapādayitumupamānopameyabhāva ākṣiptaḥ he śrīmanto yathā mamāyamudayaḥ patanāya tadvadbhavatāmapīti yūyaṃ budhyadhvamiti /
children.translated_text: And through this relation of effect and cause (<s>prayojya-prayojaka-bhāva</s>), in order to establish itself, the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation is implied: "O fortunate ones, just as my rise leads to fall, so too does yours — understand this!"

children.text: tenātra prayojyaprayojakabhāvalakṣaṇena padārthasamanvayena svātmopapādanāyopamānopameyabhāvasyākṣepāt dvitīyo vidarśanāyā bhedaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation is implied for the purpose of self-establishment through the syntactic connection characterized by the <s>prayojya-prayojaka-bhāva</s> (effect-cause relation), this is the second variety of <s>vidarśanā</s> (illustration).

There, the sun, deprived of its splendor that had blazed forth at the time of its first rising, now faces setting; and the causal agency (<s>hetukartṛtva</s>) characterized by conduct capable of producing that effect is connected with the awakening of the fortunate ones (the causative agents) regarding the action of awareness that rise ends in fall. Indeed, seeing the sun in such a state, the fortunate ones understand: "Like the sun, everyone's rise ends in a fall."
<s>Saṃkara</s> (mixture of figures) —

It is of four kinds, distinguished as: <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt), <s>śabdārthavartyalaṅkāra</s> (mixture of figures residing in sound and meaning), <s>ekaśabdābhidhāna</s> (denoted by a single word), and <s>anugrāhyānugrāhaka</s> (the supported and the supporter). First, <s>saṃdeha-saṃkara</s> (mixture through doubt) —
When there is an appearance of multiple ornaments simultaneously, and the simultaneous operation of those is impossible,

children.text: ekasya ca grahe nyāyadoṣābhāve ca saṃkaraḥ // UKss_5.11 //
children.translated_text: and in grasping one of them there is no logical ground or fault — that is <s>saṃkara</s> (mixture). [UKss 5.11]

children.text:
anekasyālaṅkārasyollekhe cetasyupārohe saṃdehasaṃkaro bhavati, na tvekaśabdābhidhānasaṃkarādāvapi anekālaṅkārollekhaḥ saṃbhavati /
yathā---
children.translated_text: When there is an appearance, a mental apprehension, of multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments), <s>saṃdeha-saṃkara</s> (mixture through doubt) occurs; but it is not the case that in <s>ekaśabdābhidhāna-saṃkara</s> and the like too, the appearance of multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> is possible. For example —
"Surely having issued forth from <s>Murāri</s> (Viṣṇu), obstructing <s>Naraka</s> (the demon),
the discus-stream (<s>cakradhārā</s>) will fall upon your head too, like the <s>Gaṅgā</s>."

children.text:
atra hyupamānopameyabhāvastatpratibhāhetuśca śleṣo 'nekālaṅkāra ullikhyate /
upamānopameyabhāve tāvat
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation and <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) as the cause of its apprehension — multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> are suggested. Regarding the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation:

children.text:
gaṅgopamānam /
cakradhārā upameyā /
murārinirgatatvaṃ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ /
śleṣastvatra narakapratipanthiśabdādātmānaṃ labhate /
ekatra hi narako dānavaḥ /
aparatra tvavīcyādiḥ /
etau ca dvāvalaṅkārāvekasminnivaśabde 'nupraviśataḥ /
na hyupamānopameyabhāvastatpratibhāheturvā śleṣaḥ samāsādyabhāve ivaśabdādimantareṇa svarūpaṃ pratilabhate /
tenātra dvāvalaṅkārā vekasminvācake iva śabde 'nupraviṣau /
yadi cānekālaṅkārollekhe sati saṃdehasaṃkarastata evamādāvapyanekālaṅkārollekhasya saṃbhavātsaṃdehasaṃkaraprasaṅga ityāśaṅkyoktam---samaṃ tadvṛttyasaṃbhava iti /
tasyānekasyālaṅkārasya samaṃ yugapadyadi vṛttirvyāpāro 'laṅkāryālaṅkaraṇātmako na saṃbhavatītyarthaḥ /
pūrvokte tūdāharaṇe murārinirgateti sādhāraṇadharmopādānānnarakapratipanthinīti ca śleṣapadopadarśanānnānekasyālaṅkārasya yugapadvṛtterasaṃbhavaḥ /
tena tatra na saṃdehasaṃkaratā /
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṅgā</s> is the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison). <s>Cakradhārā</s> (the discus-stream) is the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison). Having issued from <s>Murāri</s> is the common property (<s>sādhāraṇa dharma</s>). The <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) here obtains itself from the word <s>narakapratipanthin</s> — in one sense, <s>Naraka</s> is the demon; in the other, it refers to hell (<s>avīci</s> etc.). These two <s>alaṅkāras</s> enter into a single word <s>iva</s>. For neither the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation nor the <s>śleṣa</s> that is the cause of its apprehension obtains its own form without the word <s>iva</s> and the like in the absence of a compound. Therefore, here two <s>alaṅkāras</s> have entered into a single expressive word <s>iva</s>. Now, if <s>saṃdeha-saṃkara</s> occurs whenever there is an appearance of multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s>, then in cases like this too, since the appearance of multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> is possible, there would be the unwanted consequence of <s>saṃdeha-saṃkara</s> — anticipating this objection, it is said: "and the simultaneous operation of those is impossible." The meaning is: when the simultaneous operation — the activity of ornamenting the thing to be ornamented — of those multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> is not possible. But in the previously cited example, since the common property is presented in "issued from <s>Murāri</s>" and the <s>śleṣa</s> word is shown in "obstructing <s>Naraka</s>," the simultaneous operation of multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> is not impossible. Therefore, there is no <s>saṃdeha-saṃkara</s> there.

children.text:
nanu yadyanekālaṅkārolleke yugapadvṛttyasaṃbhave ca saṃdehasaṃkaratvam /
eva sati yatra pratibhāmātreṇānekasminnalaṅkāre ullikhyamāne yasya sādhakaṃ pramāṇamasti sa upādīyate /
yasya tu bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ vidyate sa tyajyate /
tatrāṣyanekālaṅkārollekhasya samaṃ tadvṛttyasaṃbhavasya ca saṃbhavātsaṃdehasaṃkaratvaṃ prasajjatītyāśaṅkyoktam---ekasya ca grahe nyāyadoṣābhāve ceti /
nyāyaḥ sādhakaṃ pramāṇam /
doṣo bādhakaṃ pramāṇam /
yatrānekālaṅkārollekhe yugapadvṛttyasaṃbhave ca ekatarasya grahaṇe sādhakabādhake pramāṇe samastavyastatayā na vidyete tatra saṃdehasaṃkaraḥ /
tena nāniṣṭaprasaṅgaḥ /
tathāhi---yatra sādhakabādhake pramāṇe sāmastyena vidyate tatra yasya sādhakaṃ pramāṇamasti tasyopādānādbādhakasya pramāṇopetasya ca tyāgādekasya grahaṇaṃ bhavati /
yatrāpi sādhakabādhakapramāṇayorvaiyastyenānyatarasya vidyamānatā tatrāpi pratibhollikhyamānānekālaṅkāramadhyātsādhakapramāṇopetasyopādānātpramāṇaśūnyasya copekṣyatvāt, tathā bādhakapramāṇopetasya parityāgāttditarasya ca pūrvollikhitasya pāriśeṣyeṇopādānādekasya graho bhavati /
yatra tu sādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāvastatra saṃdeha eva /
evamayaṃ saṃdehasaṃkaro lakṣitaḥ /
tasyodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: Now, if <s>saṃdeha-saṃkara</s> requires both the appearance of multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> and the impossibility of their simultaneous operation — then in a case where, through mere apprehension, multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> are suggested, whichever has supporting evidence (<s>sādhaka pramāṇa</s>) is accepted, and whichever has invalidating evidence (<s>bādhaka pramāṇa</s>) is rejected. Even there, since the appearance of multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> and the impossibility of their simultaneous operation are both present, <s>saṃdeha-saṃkara</s> would undesirably follow — anticipating this objection, it is said: "and in grasping one of them there is no logical ground or fault." <s>Nyāya</s> means supporting evidence. <s>Doṣa</s> means invalidating evidence. Where there is an appearance of multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> and impossibility of simultaneous operation, and in grasping one of them, supporting and invalidating evidence are not found either collectively or individually — there is <s>saṃdeha-saṃkara</s>. Therefore, there is no undesired consequence. For where both supporting and invalidating evidence exist together, by accepting that which has supporting evidence and rejecting that which has invalidating evidence, one of them is grasped. Even where supporting and invalidating evidence exist separately, from among the multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> suggested through apprehension, by accepting the one supported by evidence and disregarding the one devoid of evidence, and similarly by rejecting the one with invalidating evidence and accepting the other previously suggested one by elimination — one is grasped. But where there is an absence of both supporting and invalidating evidence, there is indeed doubt. Thus this <s>saṃdeha-saṃkara</s> is defined. Its example —
"Even though the most fitting husband is not obtained for you,

children.text: tathāpi vacmi kutrāpi kriyatāmādaro nare // UKss_5.*10 //
children.translated_text: still I say: let regard be shown to some man." [UKss 5.*10]

children.text:
atra varenduriti vara eva induḥ, vara induriveti rūpakasamāsopamayordvayoralaṅkārayorullekhaḥ /
na ca tasyānekasyālaṅkārasya yugapadvṛttiḥ saṃbhavati /
ekālaṅkārasaṃśrayeṇaivālaṅkārasya kṛtakṛtyātvāt /
na cātra dvayormadhyādekatarasya grahaṇāya sādhakabādhakapramāṇayogaḥ. sādhakaṃ hi pramāṇaṃ vidyamānaṃ vidhimukhenālaṅkāraṃ jñāpayet /
tathā bādhakamapi prahātavyālaṅkāraniṣedhamukhenopādeyamalaṅkāraṃ pūrvollikhitaṃ pāriśeṣyādupādeyatayā pratipādayati /
atra tu dvayoḥ sādhakabādhakapramāṇayorabhāvātsaṃdehaḥ /
tena saṃkaro 'laṅkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, <s>varendu</s> means either "the husband himself is the moon" (vara eva induḥ) or "the husband is like the moon" (vara indur iva) — thus there is an appearance of two <s>alaṅkāras</s>, <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and <s>samāsopamā</s> (compound simile). The simultaneous operation of these multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> is not possible, since the ornament achieves its purpose by relying on a single <s>alaṅkāra</s> alone. And here, there is no availability of supporting or invalidating evidence for grasping one of the two. For supporting evidence, if present, would indicate the <s>alaṅkāra</s> through affirmation. Similarly, invalidating evidence too, through the negation of the <s>alaṅkāra</s> to be rejected, would establish the <s>alaṅkāra</s> to be accepted by elimination from the previously suggested ones. But here, due to the absence of both supporting and invalidating evidence for either, there is doubt. Therefore, the <s>alaṅkāra</s> is <s>saṃkara</s> (mixture).
Now, <s>śabdārthavartyalaṅkāra</s> (mixture of figures residing in sound and meaning) —
<s>Alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments) residing in sound and in meaning, shining together in a single sentence,
that too is <s>saṃkara</s> (mixture). [UKss 5.12a]

children.text:
yatraikasminvākye śabdavartinor'thavartinaścālaṅkārāḥ saṃsargamupayānti sa śabdārthālaṅkāraḥ /
tasyodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: Where in a single sentence, <s>alaṅkāras</s> residing in sound and <s>alaṅkāras</s> residing in meaning come into conjunction — that is <s>śabdārthālaṅkāra</s> (mixture of sound and sense ornaments). Its example —
"If your condition is such that you seek a husband, do not make your entreaty in vain;

children.text: rūpeṇa te yuvā sarvaḥ pādabaddho hi kiṅkaraḥ // UKss_5.*11 //
children.translated_text: by your beauty, every young man is a servant bound at your feet." [UKss 5.*11]

children.text:
varārthā bhartrarthā /
kiṅkaro dāsaḥ /
atra thakāropanibaddho 'nuprāsātmakaḥ śabdālaṅkāraḥ /
arthālaṅkāraścārthāntaranyāso vidyate /
tathāhi---atra mākṛthā vyarthamarthitāmityupāditsiter'the 'rthitvasyākaraṇaṃ yadupanibaddhaṃ tadanupapadyamānatayā saṃbhāvya tatsamarthanāyoktaṃ 'rūpeṇa te yuvā sarvaḥ pādabaddho hi kiṅkara'iti /
yo guṇotkarṣaśālī sa nārthayate, apitvarthyate yathā ratnādi /
tvaṃ ca rūpavattvādguṇotkarṣaśālinī /
tasmādupāditsiter'the
children.translated_text: <s>Varārthā</s> means desiring a husband. <s>Kiṅkara</s> means servant. Here, the <s>śabdālaṅkāra</s> (sound ornament) is <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) constructed upon the <s>tha</s>-sound. And the <s>arthālaṅkāra</s> (sense ornament) is <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration). That is to say — here, the statement "do not make your entreaty in vain," which presents the non-performance of entreaty in the sense of desire for acquisition, is something that needs to be established as plausible, and for establishing it, it is said: "by your beauty, every young man is a servant bound at your feet." He who possesses excellence of qualities is not entreated, but rather is himself sought after, like a jewel and so forth. And you, being endowed with beauty, possess excellence of qualities. Therefore, in the sense of desire for acquisition,
your entreating is improper.
Therefore, this is <s>śabdārthavartyalaṅkāra-saṃkara</s> (mixture of figures residing in sound and meaning).
Now, <s>ekaśabdābhidhāna-saṃkara</s> (mixture denoted by a single word) —
It is denoted through entry into a single part of a sentence. [UKss 5.12b]

children.text:
ekasminvākyāṃśe vākyaikadeśe yatrānekasyālaṅkārasyānupraveśaḥ sa ekaśabdābhidhānasaṃkaraḥ /
tasyodāharaṇam----
children.translated_text: Where there is the entry of multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> into a single part of a sentence, a single portion of a sentence — that is <s>ekaśabdābhidhāna-saṃkara</s>. Its example —
"Do not be thus! With beautiful complexion and lovely earrings,
like a lotus-pool in a painting, she gives pleasure to the eyes alone." [UKss 5.*12]

children.text:
atropamālaṅkāra upamāpratibhotpattihetubhūtaśca śleṣa ityetau dvāvalaṅkārāvekasminvākyāṃśe ivaśabde 'nupraviṣṭau /
tathāhi---ambhojinī upamānam, gaurī upameyā, dṛṣṭimātrasukhapradatvaṃ sādhāraṇo dharmaḥ ityupamā /
sacchāyavarṇikā cārukarṇiketi śleṣaḥ /
ambhojinyāṃ hi varṇā rājavartādayaḥ gauryāṃ tu gauratvam /
ambhojinyāṃ karṇikā kamalamadhvarttibījakośaḥ /
gauryāṃ tu cārū karṇau /

children.translated_text: <s>Kap</s> is here a <s>samāsānta</s> (compound-final suffix).
Therefore, this is <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia).
These two <s>alaṅkāras</s> have entered into a single part of the sentence, the word <s>iva</s>.
Therefore, this is <s>ekaśabdābhidhāna-saṃkara</s> (mixture denoted by a single word).

Here, the <s>alaṅkāra</s> of <s>upamā</s> (simile) and <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) as the cause of the apprehension of the simile — these two <s>alaṅkāras</s> have entered into a single part of the sentence, the word <s>iva</s>. That is to say — <s>ambhojinī</s> (lotus-pool) is the <s>upamāna</s>, <s>Gaurī</s> is the <s>upameya</s>, and giving pleasure to the eyes alone is the common property — this is the <s>upamā</s>. <s>Sacchāyavarṇikā cārukarṇikā</s> is the <s>śleṣa</s>. For in the case of the lotus-pool, <s>varṇa</s> refers to colors such as <s>rājavarta</s> (indigo) etc., while for <s>Gaurī</s>, it refers to fair complexion. In the case of the lotus-pool, <s>karṇikā</s> is the seed-pod in the center of the lotus; for <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>cāru karṇau</s> means beautiful ears.
Now, <s>anugrāhyānugrāhaka-saṃkara</s> (mixture of the supported and the supporter) —
Where ornaments stand through mutual assistance,

children.text: svātantryeṇātmalābhaṃ no labhante so 'pi saṃkaraḥ // UKss_5.13 //
children.translated_text: and do not independently attain their own form — that too is <s>saṃkara</s> (mixture). [UKss 5.13]

children.text:
yatrobhayorupamānopameyayoḥ parasparamupamānopameyabhāvastatropameyopamā /
upameyenopamānasyopamānāt /
nanu ca prākaraṇikaṃ sāmyābhidhānasaṃbandhi upameyaṃ /
aprākaraṇikaṃ upamānaṃ /
yadi cātropameyasyopamānatvamabhidhīyate, evaṃ
children.translated_text: Where there is a mutual <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation between both the standard and the object of comparison — there is <s>upameyopamā</s> (counter-simile). The <s>upameya</s> serves as <s>upamāna</s> for the <s>upamāna</s>. Now, objection: the contextually relevant entity connected with the statement of similarity is the <s>upameya</s>; the contextually non-relevant one is the <s>upamāna</s>. If here the status of <s>upamāna</s> is predicated of the <s>upameya</s>, then

children.text:
sati tasya prākaraṇikatvaṃ vyāhanyate ityāśaṅkyoktam---pakṣāntarahānigāmiti /
nātropamānopameyabhāve tātparyaṃ kintu etadeva dvayamevaṃvidhaṃ vidyate, na tvanyadetayoḥ sadṛśaṃ vastvantaraṃ vidyate iti /
ataśca etatpakṣadvitayavyatiriktasya pakṣāntarasyātra hānervivakṣitatvāt parasparamupamānopameyabhāvo na duṣyatīti tasya pakṣāntarahānau pratapādyāyāmavāntaravākyārthatvenāvasthānāt, varaṃ viṣaṃ bhakṣaya mā cārasya gṛhe bhuṅkthāḥ itivat /
atra hi viṣabhakṣaṇaṃ na vidhīyate /
durjanagṛhe bhojanaparivarjanatātparyāt /
evamihāpyupamānopameyabhāvasyāvivakṣāpakṣāntarahānau tātparyāt /
tasyā udāharaṇam---
children.translated_text: its contextual relevance would be contradicted — anticipating this, it is said: "entailing the exclusion of an alternative interpretation" (<s>pakṣāntarahānigā</s>). The purport here is not the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation, but rather: these two alone of this kind exist, and no other entity similar to them exists. Therefore, since the intended meaning is the exclusion of any alternative position (<s>pakṣāntara</s>) other than these two sides, the mutual <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation is not faulty, because its function is to serve as the subordinate sentence-meaning for establishing the exclusion of the alternative — just as in the expression "Rather eat poison than dine in the house of a scoundrel." For here, eating poison is not enjoined; the purport is the avoidance of dining in the house of a wicked person. Similarly here too, the <s>upamāna</s>-<s>upameya</s> relation is not intended in itself; the purport lies in the exclusion of the alternative. Its example —
"Like a deer, the hunter of <s>Smara</s> (Love), even though rejected (<s>anaṅgīkṛta</s>) by you,

children.text: tvadvapuḥ kṣaṇamapyeṣa dhārṣṭyādiva na muñcati // UKss_5.*13 //
children.translated_text: does not release your body even for a moment, as if out of boldness." [UKss 5.*13]

children.text:
atra dhārṣṭyādi na muñcatīti yāsāvutprekṣā sā hareṇeva smaravyādhastvayānaṅgīkṛto 'pi sannityupamāpratibhotpattihetuśleṣavaśena svarūpaṃ pratilabhate /
anaṅgīkṛto hi anaṅgatvamaśarīratvamāpāditaḥ anūrīkṛtaśca /
yaścānūrīkṛtaḥ kṣaṇamapi na muñcati tatra dhārṣṭyaṃ hetutayotprekṣituṃ śakyate /
tena śleṣavaśenātrotpreksā āsāditasvabhāvā /
atoyamanugrāhyānugrāhakasaṃkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) in "as if out of boldness, does not release" obtains its form through the force of the <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) that is the cause of the apprehension of the simile in "like a deer, the hunter of <s>Smara</s>, even though rejected by you." For <s>anaṅgīkṛta</s> means both "made bodiless" (<s>anaṅgatva</s>, incorporeality) and "not accepted" (<s>anūrīkṛta</s>). And when one who is not accepted does not release even for a moment, boldness can be fancied as the cause. Thus, here the <s>utprekṣā</s> has obtained its nature through the force of <s>śleṣa</s>. Therefore, this is <s>anugrāhyānugrāhaka-saṃkara</s> (mixture of the supported and the supporter).

children.text:
evamayaṃ caturvidhaḥ saṃkaro nānālaṃkāragatavikalpavyavasthāsamuccayāṅgāṅgibhāvasamāśrayaṇenābhihitaḥ /
tatrānekālaṃkāravikalpātsaṃdehasaṃkaraḥ /
nibhinnādhāratvena śabdārthavartinolaṃkārayoravasthānādvyavasthāsamāśrayaḥ śabdārthavartyalaṃkārasaṃkaraḥ /
ekaśabdābhidhānasaṃkare tu samuccayenānekolaṃkāra ekasminvākyāṃśe ivādāvanupraviśati /
anugrāhyānugrāhakasaṃkare tvanakasyālaṃkārasyāṅgāṅgibhāvaḥ /
ato vikalpa-vyavasthā-samuccayāṅgāṅgibhāvasaṃśrayā ete catvāraḥ saṃkarabhedāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, this fourfold <s>saṃkara</s> (mixture) has been described by resorting to <s>vikalpa</s> (alternation), <s>vyavasthā</s> (fixed arrangement), <s>samuccaya</s> (accumulation), and <s>aṅgāṅgibhāva</s> (principal-subordinate relation) pertaining to various <s>alaṅkāras</s>. Among these, <s>saṃdeha-saṃkara</s> arises from the alternation of multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s>. <s>Śabdārthavartyalaṅkāra-saṃkara</s> resorts to fixed arrangement, since ornaments of sound and meaning subsist in distinct substrata. In <s>ekaśabdābhidhāna-saṃkara</s>, multiple <s>alaṅkāras</s> enter a single part of a sentence such as <s>iva</s> etc. through accumulation. In <s>anugrāhyānugrāhaka-saṃkara</s>, there is a principal-subordinate relation among the <s>alaṅkāras</s>. Therefore, these four varieties of <s>saṃkara</s> are based on alternation, fixed arrangement, accumulation, and principal-subordinate relation.
<s>Upameyopamā</s> (counter-simile) —
Where there is mutual relation of <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison),
they call that <s>upameyopamā</s> (counter-simile), which entails the exclusion of an alternative interpretation. [UKss 5.14]

children.text:
yatrobhayorupamānopameyayoḥ parasparamupamānopameyabhāvas tatropameyopamā /
upameyenopamānasyopamānāt /
nanu ca prākaraṇikaṃ sāmyābhidhānasaṃbandhi upameyam aprakaraṇikamupamānam /
yadi cātropameyasyopamānatvam abhidhīyate evaṃ sati tasya prākaraṇikatvam vyāhanyate ityāśaṅkyoktam -- pakṣāntarahānigāmiti /
nātropamānopameyabhāve tātparyaṃ kiṃtu etadeva dvayamevaṃvidhaṃ vidyate na tvanyadetayoḥ sadṛśaṃ vastvantaraṃ vidyata iti /
ataśca etat pakṣadvitayavyatiriktasya pakṣāntarasyātra hānervivakṣitatvāt parasparamupamānopameyabhāvo na duṣyatīti /
tasya pakṣāntarahānau pratipādyāyāmavāntaravākyārthatvenāvasthānāt -- varaṃ viṣaṃ bhakṣaya mā cāsya gṛhe bhuktvā -- itivat /
atra hi viṣabhakṣaṇaṃ na vidhīyate durjanagṛhe bhojanaparivarjanatātparyāt /
evamihāpyupamānopameyabhāvasyāvivakṣā pakṣāntarahānau tātparyāt /
children.translated_text:
Where both the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) and the object of comparison (<s>upameya</s>) mutually assume the roles of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>, there is <s>upameyopamā</s> (mutual simile).
The <s>upameya</s> serves as the <s>upamāna</s> of the <s>upamāna</s>.
Now, the contextually relevant term connected with the statement of similarity is the <s>upameya</s>, and the non-contextual term is the <s>upamāna</s>.
If here the <s>upameya</s> is said to function as the <s>upamāna</s>, then its contextual relevance would be contradicted — anticipating this objection, it is stated: 'because of the elimination of another alternative.'
The purport here is not the mutual relation of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>, but rather that this pair alone of such a nature exists — there is no other thing similar to these two.
Therefore, since the intended meaning is the elimination of an alternative other than these two options, the mutual relation of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> is not faulty.
Since the elimination of the other alternative, which is to be conveyed, subsists as the subordinate sentence-meaning — just as in 'rather eat poison, but do not eat at his house.'
For here the eating of poison is not enjoined, since the purport is the avoidance of eating at a wicked person's house.
Likewise here too, the relation of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> is not the intended meaning, since the purport is the elimination of another alternative.
Uprooting the heads of enemies with force, like lotuses,

children.text: ājau karopamaṃ cakraṃ yasya cakropamaḥ karaḥ // UKss_5.*14 //
children.translated_text: in battle, whose discus (<s>cakra</s>) resembles the hand, and whose hand resembles the discus. (UKss 5.*14)

children.text:
atra yasyetyupāttsya tvatkṛte so 'pi vaikuṇṭha ityatra tacchabdasamanvayenā kāṅkṣāvicchedo bhaviṣyate /
uttareṣvapi ca ślekeṣu tenaiva yacchabdārtho nirākāṅkṣī kāryaḥ /

children.translated_text: Here there is a mutual relation of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> between the hand and the discus.
And the common property (<s>dharma</s>) here is the cutting off of enemies' heads with extreme swiftness.
